items.body: Clock DVA has released a 45th-anniversary remastered reissue of “Thirst” through The Grey Area of Mute. The Clock DVA “Thirst” reissue is the second instalment in Mute’s campaign to reissue the Sheffield industrial and post-punk group’s catalogue, following the 2025 remaster of “White Souls in Black Suits”. The reissue appears on double thirst-red 2LP, CD and digital. “Thirst” was first issued in 1981 on Fetish Records . It was Clock DVA’s second album, following the 1980 debut “White Souls in Black Suits”, and marked the band’s move from the improvised, tape-driven approach of that debut into a sharper, song-based framework. What the Clock DVA ‘Thirst’ reissue includes The 2026 edition was cut from the original tapes with input from surviving members and carries the original sleeve notes by Genesis P-Orridge. It expands the original nine-track album with live recordings, the original single mixes of “4 Hours” and “Sensorium”, and two newly recorded DVATION 2026 versions by the current line-up. Side-Line previously reported on the remastered “Sensorium” two-track single issued ahead of the album. Clock DVA – “Thirst” 2026 tracklist “Uncertain” “Sensorium” “White Cell” “Piano Pain” “Blue Tone” “North Loop” “4 Hours” “Moments” “Impressions of African Winter” “The Opening (Live at The Lyceum)” “Remain Remain (Live at The Lyceum)” “4 Hours (Single Mix)” “Sensorium (Single Mix)” “4 Hours (DVATION 2026 Version)” “Sensorium (DVATION 2026 Version)” The vinyl edition is a double thirst-red 2LP set, issued in a standard pressing and a signed art-card edition, while the CD comes in an eco card sleeve. The reissue is also available digitally and can be streamed and ordered via the official “Thirst” 2026 remaster page. Thirst (2026 Remaster) by ClockDVA The original recordings feature Adi Newton (voice, clarinet, manipulated tapes, piano, modified guitar, EMS Synthi E), Steven J. Turner (bass and treatments), Charlie Collins (saxophones, African flute, African thumb piano), Paul Widger (guitar) and Roger Quail (drums). The album was recorded at Jacobs Studio in Surrey and produced and engineered by Ken Thomas with the band, with artwork by designer Neville Brody. About Clock DVA Clock DVA are an industrial, post-punk and electronic group from Sheffield, formed in 1978 by Adi Newton and Steven “Judd” Turner. The name pairs Anthony Burgess’ Nadsat slang from “A Clockwork Orange” with the Slavic word for “two”. The band worked early on with treated tape loops and EMS Synthi E electronics, releasing cassette material before the 1980 debut “White Souls in Black Suits” on Industrial Records; that debut returned in a remastered edition on The Grey Area of Mute in 2025, when Side-Line covered the single “Brigade”. “Thirst” followed in 1981 on Fetish Records and reached the top of the UK indie charts. Newton later steered the project toward a more electronic direction, signing to Polydor for “Advantage” (1983) before moving into sample-based and cybernetic work on releases including “Buried Dreams” (1989) and into the early 1990s. Newton also ran The Anti Group Communications (T.A.G.C.) as a separate research vehicle; Side-Line reported on the vinyl reissue of its 1994 album “Iso-Erotic Calibration”. The band reactivated in 2008 with a new line-up and has since revisited its catalogue, including the vinyl release of rare tracks on “Re-Konstructed”. The 45th-anniversary “Thirst” reissue continues this chronological re-presentation of the group’s early work.
items._cn_summary: Clock DVA来自谢菲尔德，是工业、后朋克与电子领域的重要乐队。本文报道其1981年专辑《Thirst》45周年重制版由Mute旗下The Grey Area发行。原专辑融合了工业噪音、磁带实验、EMS合成器、萨克斯、非洲笛与拇指钢琴等元素，从即兴磁带手法转向更清晰的歌曲结构，跨越工业、电子与世界音乐边界。重制版收录原始九首作品、Lyceum现场录音、单曲混音及当前阵容重新录制的DVATION 2026版本，保留了Genesis P-Orridge的原版说明。整体内容贴合暗潮、工业与实验电子口味，但本文属新闻发布性质，缺乏深度评论与批判性分析。

items.body: Carlos Henriquez has long understood that rhythm tells stories long before words arrive. On Monk Con Clave, he takes Thelonious Monk's angular brilliance and brings it back to the streets, dance halls, and other crowded spaces across New York's Afro-Caribbean neighbourhoods. The result is not merely a tribute album but a living dialogue between Monk's genius and Henriquez's Nuyorican identity. Leading his self-named big band, Henriquez has assembled a remarkable multigenerational ensemble featuring musicians from the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra, along with the propulsive conguero Pedrito Martinez, the sparkling trumpet of Michael Rodriguez, pianists Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Osmany Paredes, and Robert Rodriguez, vocalist Anthony Almonte, and flautist Jeremy Bosch. Yet despite the star power, the performance succeeds because Henriquez never loses sight of the groove beneath the architecture. "'Round Midnight" opens not at midnight but in atmosphere. The familiar melody floats over layered percussion and brass voicings, with Rubalcaba feeding off the rhythmic texture. Trumpeter Michael Rodriguez offers a brief solo in a warm, centred tone. Henriquez's arrangement avoids sentimentality, letting the rhythm coalesce beneath the harmony. "I Mean You" bolts awake with swagger. Henriquez opens with a big-toned bass foundation, and the brass section punches hard in the follow-up, turning Monk's quirky accents into dance impulses. Paredes jumps into the arrangement, which swings fiercely without sanding off Monk's jagged edges. Henriquez's own compositions, "El Son de Teo" and "San Juan Hill," follow and are among the album's emotional centres. The former is rooted in Afro-Cuban traditions, with the rhythm section honouring that musical ancestry. Bosch brings a folkloric vocal spirit to the performance, and his singing becomes part of the rhythmic fabric, warm and immediate. Rubalcaba is masterful throughout, threading sharp harmonic ideas and flowing montuno figures into the arrangement. The latter number carries historical weight, as it was named for the Manhattan neighbourhood erased by urban renewal. This memory music, proud, bittersweet and defiant, is captured vocally, both separately and together, by Martinez, Almonte and Bosch, with the upper-register trumpet work delivered by Nathaniel Williford. "Raise Four" ignites the band's adventurous side, full of rhythmic displacement and ensemble interplay. Trumpeter Jesus Ricardo cuts through with fire and precision over Martinez's slap, open tone, and muted stroke. Pianist Rodriguez and alto saxophonist Ted Nash make their presence felt throughout the ensemble. "Green Chimney" arrives with buoyant, almost playful energy, capitalizing on Henriquez's big, bold tone throughout the number. As the band transforms Monk's quirky composition into a number that maintains a relaxed yet insistent groove, soloists Chris Lewis on tenor saxophone, Marshall Gilkes on trombone, and pianist Robert Rodriguez each add their expressive voices to the arrangement. The closing track pairs Henriquez's "Plena Azul" with Monk's "Blue Monk," beautifully tying the project together. Almonte and Bosch infuse the performance with a communal spirit as their voices weave naturally through the plena rhythms and blues-infused ensemble lines. Over this celebratory pulse, Dion Tucker and trumpeter Kali Rodriguez-Peña add intensity and spontaneity, deepening the sense of cultural continuity. This album does not merely reinterpret Monk but reveals that he was closer to the clave than many listeners had thought.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以爵士大乐队编制为核心，融合Thelonious Monk经典作品与Afro-Cuban节奏传统的跨界专辑。贝斯手兼领班Carlos Henriquez以其Nuyorican文化身份为支点，将Monk棱角分明的和声语汇重新置入纽约拉丁社区的舞曲与街头语境中，构建Monk爵士语汇与加勒比传统之间的持续对话。专辑汇集了来自Jazz at Lincoln Center乐团的跨世代乐手，搭配Conguero Pedrito Martinez、钢琴家Gonzalo Rubalcaba、小号手Michael Rodriguez等知名音乐人。Henriquez原创作品'El Son de Teo'与'San Juan Hill'分别承载古巴音乐谱系与曼哈顿被城市更新抹去的San Juan Hill街区记忆，是专辑情感重心。'Raise Four'展示了乐队在节奏位移与集体即兴方面的探索性，'Green Chimneys'则呈现放松而坚持的律动。整体定位介于学院派爵士大乐队传统与拉丁世界音乐融合之间。

items.body:
Treasured slow motion trance rustlers Full Circle rack up a decade of remixes for the likes of Vox Populi!, 10LEC6, Tapan, and Die Orangen, plus a trove of unreleased goodies, on this limited edition mixtape, further to their much-adored albums and mixes for Good Morning Tapes and Offen Music.

The eternal sunrise of late ’80s / early ’90s Goa dance & European proto-trance guides Alexis Le Tan & Joakim’s cult duo on their by-now trademarked style of chopped & screwed x Mediterranean drug chug hypno-bullets, pulling a broad range of source material into their own world of hazed offbeat grooves and arps with a rare je ne sais quoi that’s made their catalogue a proper cult property, fulfilling a need for this type of aerobic mysticism on modern dancefloors.

As with their slew of Good Morning Tapes mixes and LPs it’s all arranged with a slick, sick, effortless aerodynamic, glyding between the likes of their subcontinental-slanted rework of fellow French psych-o-nauts Vox Populi!, and the remix for Die Orangen that really placed them on the map back in 2019. It’s never hurried, always zoned-in, flowing with a careful attention to the good of your trip and heavy as you like.

The frisson is real!
items._cn_summary: Full Circle是法国二人组Alexis Le Tan与Joakim的合作项目，这张限量版混音合辑收录了近十年来为Vox Populi!、10LEC6、Tapan、Die Orangen等艺术家创作的混音作品及未发表素材。音乐风格融合了八十年代末至九十年代初Goa舞曲与欧洲proto-trance的慢速变体，以chopped & screwed手法处理各类来源素材，呈现出地中海式的迷幻律动与催眠质感。作品在Good Morning Tapes、Offen Music等小型独立厂牌发行，具有明显的地下亚文化属性。整体编排注重流畅性与空间氛围，音色处理上兼顾了舞曲的律动需求与迷幻听觉体验，定位于实验电子与世界音乐融合的边缘地带。

items.body:
A second pressing of last year’s gorgeous fourth and final album from Old Saw, the American Primitive project of Tongue Depressor's Henry Birdsey, riffing on the classic Takoma paradigm with additional ferric washes and layered instrumental drones, huge recommendation if yr into Bruce Langhorne’s ‘The Hired Hand’ or classic work by Daniel Lanois, Laraaji, Pelt, Stars Of The Lid, State River Widening.

'The Wringing Cloth' is Birdsey’s fourth and final Old Saw outing, and ironically it’s also the one that has garnered most amount of critical and commercial success. Old Saw’s shimmering, drone-heavy soundscapes were recorded on 1/4" tape at various locations in New England over the last few years and are once again paired with evocative black and white imagery from photographer Dylan Hausthor, whose landscapes somehow perfectly capture the timeless, widescreen appeal of the music inside.

Birdsey's pedal, lap steel and resonator are at the core of each track, but the album also features Old Saw’s usual personnel; Harper Reed on nylon string guitar and banjo, Ira Dorset on fiddle and bowed strings, Ann Rowlis on reed organ and harmonium, Jim Cutler on telecaster, Addison Starkweather-Price on bass, and Peter Catchpole on metal objects and power hammer. That lap steel lends the music its stylistic anchor, taking us through decades of American folk before gently fraying at the edges. Birdsey's application of classical minimalism - the themes that surge through his work with Zach Rowden as Tongue Depressor - is still somehow present here, especially as the record pulls into its second side and the shimmering country-fied atmosphere is pierced with bell-like sounds, but the overall mood and flavour of the record is distinctly easy on the ear and timeless in its appeal.

As the label put it, “What has always been uncanny about this music is that it arrives in a state at once familiar and obscured, like a memory weighed down with sensory information but no identifying details to place it. The Wringing Cloth walks off further into that geographical dream without time or language, until it’s just a speck of light….”
items._cn_summary: Old Saw是美国新英格兰地区的American Primitive（四指弹拨）风格项目，由Henry Birdsey主导，同时也是实验二人组Tongue Depressor的核心成员。这张专辑是系列的第四张也是最后一张作品，延续了Takoma学院派的指弹传统，以踏板滑棒吉他、resonator吉他为核心乐器，融合了班卓琴、小提琴、风琴等原声乐器。音乐在传统美国民谣的基础上叠加了磁带录音质感的环境声场和铺底drones，并融入了古典极简主义的结构思维，使整体呈现出宽广、朦胧且具有时间感的氛围美学。与Stars of the Lid、Laraaji等环境音乐家存在风格交集，属于民谣与drone/ambient之间的跨界实验作品。

items.body:
Donato Dozzy and Neel's critically lauded 2012 opus is re-pressed for 2026, highlighting just how influential it's been in the years since,

If you're into psychedelic, trance-inducing minimal techno, then you've probably come across Voices from the Lake already. If not, then prepare yerself for an interface with yr new favorite album. Released over a decade ago, the record made an immediate connection with clubgoers searching for a lysergic alternative to minimal's booming, avoidant monotony. Dozzy and Neel approach their tracks with enviable restraint: kick drums are present on the self-titled album, but forced into submission, not dominating the tracks but occasionally adding punctuation to their whirling structures. The key to each segment - which run into each other to form a longform heat haze of abstract percussion and offworld sound effects - isn't the drums exactly, but the mood the two Italian veterans are able to extract using only the most spartan ingredients.

The elements are familiar - cycling melodic phrases, distant pads, unstable rhythms - but the way Dozzy and Neel assemble them feels human and connected. On 'Iyo' there's barely a chance for the track to develop into a proper banger; all tension, no release. Elsewhere on 'Manuvex' the kick is softened into a damp thud, left to underpin shivery Porter Ricks-esque glitches and peculiar, dissonant synthetic elements that breathe with rare humanity. With the shortest track weighing in at a generous seven and a half minutes, and the longest hitting 16, it's an epic that's not afraid of simmering in its own juices until it's fully cooked. Bit of a classic?
items._cn_summary: Donato Dozzy与Neel合作的迷幻极简techno专辑，2012年发行后于2026年再版。作品以极度克制的制作手法著称：底鼓被压制在混音底部，不再主导节奏，而是作为断句标点融入长篇结构。专辑由抽象打击乐、外太空音效、循环旋律短语和远距离pad构成绵延的氛围层，单曲长度在七分半至十六分钟之间，以缓慢酝酿为特征。整体风格融合了techno的骨架与ambient的呼吸感，并带有鲜明的迷幻质感。两人的编曲方式以极简素材营造出高度人性化的情绪张力，在极简techno领域具有重要的影响力。意大利制作人的独立厂牌背景也为作品增添了地下电子音乐特有的实验气质。

items.body:
Surf Gang co-founder Harrison follows his work on MIKE and Earl Sweatshirt's 'POMPEII // UTILITY' with his first solo album, a tight set of wonky, atmospheric instrumentals that establishes him as one of rap's most reliable minimalists.

Harrison's been around for ages - he even held the camera on those Spooky Black videos back in the day - but it was only this year when his profile really spiked. Previously an almost anonymous presence alongside Evilgiane in New York City's Surf Gang collective, Harrison's work on 'POMPEII // UTILITY', an ambitious double album that he produced almost single handedly, took his name far beyond Reddit threads and YouTube credits. And the modestly titled 'Taking a walk & calling a car home' arrives only a matter of weeks later, sweeping up 10 of the beatmaker's oddest cues, collaborations with Bryce Byrd, Cajm, Earl Sweatshirt, Elipropperr, Harto Falión and TAKA and moody solo experiments that help establish his lore. On the opener, for example, the expected roll of clipped hi-hats and booming 808s never arrives; instead we're trapped in an uncanny back alley, met with saturated FM pads, ghostly moans and pulsing bass twangs.

Alba Collective's ambient/improv operative Byrd shows with an assist on 'graffititowers1&2', a squashed, Actress-like house sketch with breathy Y2K synths and London's Cajm, who we last spotted working alongside Bianca Scout, appears on 'Fieldsloop', a glitchy rumble of clicks 'n cuts percussion and booming bass. Even when Earl joins for 'officeloop with t + e', the mood never ruptures, carrying Surf Gang's most ambient ambitions into unknown territory with ratcheting foley clanks and reverberating woodwind loops. And when Virginia rapper Harto Falión breaks the silence on 'Wrong', it's with wordless chants that sound more horizontal than Harrison's comparatively upbeat kicks and snaps. It's worth holding out until the title track, six minutes of submerged, almost dubbed-out rhythms, Badalamenti keys and cryptic SFX that helps us contextualize the entire record. Whatever Harrison's doing, it's not strictly rap, that's for sure.
items._cn_summary: Harrison的首张个人专辑延续了他为MIKE和Earl Sweatshirt制作时展现的极简美学，呈现十首离奇且氛围感强烈的器乐作品。专辑融合故障电子、ambient即兴、dub节奏与暗色调电影配器，引用了Actress式的house草图、glitch碎拍及Badalamenti式的键盘音色。与Alba Collective的ambient/即兴音乐人Bryce Byrd等合作，将嘻哈制作语境推向实验电子领域。开篇摒弃传统嘻哈鼓组，以饱和FM合成器铺垫和幽暗低频营造诡异巷道氛围；终曲以六分钟的沉浸式dub节奏收束全篇。整体氛围阴郁、疏离，展现了制作人在地下音乐场景中独特的声响设计能力和跨类型融合意识。

The effortless drift of ’In Spring’ is the trio’s 2nd vinyl release after 2019’s eponymous debut and a tape
items.body:
Dead strong etheric elisions of chamber-jazz, trip hop and dream-pop from Bristol’s Tara Clerkin Trio, following up their acclaimed self-titled debut with a new EP of subdued but glowing reveries somewhere between Dominique Lawalrée's intimate parlour music, Third Eye Foundation's atmospheric configurations and the sort of skewed pop we'll always associate with the Laika x Moonshake axis. 

The effortless drift of ’In Spring’ is the trio’s 2nd vinyl release after 2019’s eponymous debut and a tape with Dublin’s Weeding in 2020. It’s a distinctly Bristolian affair in its beatdown pacing and smoky atmosphere, which the label themselves compare to the roster orbiting the city’s Planet Records (Flying Saucer Attack, The Third Eye Foundation) in the ‘90s, with hints of a less noirish Portishead, or the sweeter ends of the Young Echo sound.

'Memory' dissolves into the atmosphere, all muted woodwind and organ moans that erupt into a half-time drum warble; if trip-hop is back in 2021, "In Spring" recalls the genre's most low-key and thus enduring moments, while harmonizing with the wyrd-world narco-pop abstraction of contemporary forces Cucina Povera and Leila Sakini. 

Their elegant chamber sashay ‘Done Before’ carries Tara’s vocals on beautifully buoyant string and piano phrases trimmed with a sort of tripped sensibility, and ‘Night Steps’ pushes that aspect with crushed drums and filtered vox that feel like Teresa Winter on a Portishead track, and their nuanced range finally reaches into a sort of modal, 4th world lounge style recalling Julia Holter via Air on the impessively accomplished title tune. 

A quietly brilliant, memorable record >> Tipped!
items._cn_summary: 塔拉·克莱尔金三重奏的第二张黑胶作品，融合室内爵士、trip-hop与梦幻流行，呈现独特的布里斯托式低沉吟唱氛围。音乐在Dominique Lawalrée式的亲密沙龙音乐与Third Eye Foundation的大气架构间游走，带有Laika x Moonshake般的偏斜流行质感。作品以缓慢的节奏和烟雾感声场为底色，木管与管风琴的呜咽在半拍鼓点中涌动，人声在弦乐与钢琴短语间优雅漂浮。第四世界休闲风格的影响在同名曲中浮现，呼应Julia Holter与Air的融合美学。整体呈现出柔和而层次丰富的实验性声响，跨越当代古典、电子实验与世界音乐等多个领域。

items.body:
Deep club modernist Sa Pa mints his own new label, Dub Techno For Life, with four top drawer cuts of textured, strident pressure tipped FFO classic Chain Reaction x Short Span.

Since 2015 Sa Pa has carved a heads-down path between techno, proper, and its conceptual adjuncts in ambient and sound designer atmospheres, most recently on Short Span and Astral Industries. Now taking matters into his own hands, the ‘Girls on Tour EP’ squares up his most robust club material alongside more experimental urges for a definitive self-portrait displaying a fine spectrum of strengths. 

The four tunes clearly speak to his diversity within a theme, checking for a firm touchstone in Andreas Tilliander aka Mokira with the 10 mins of rolling, claggy heft to ‘Mokira Ultra Dub’, unshelving his 2016 rework for deep ’26 ‘floors, alongside the puckered elegance of ‘Waiting For You’, harking to roots in Teutonic house minimalism, whereas the B-side attends to grubbier urges in the bittersweet, sludgy budge of ‘Modular System’, and lusher, abstract feels on the Actress or Rezzett-esque whorl of ‘World Saving Banger’.
items._cn_summary: Sa Pa 创办个人厂牌 Dub Techno For Life 发行此张四曲 EP，横跨俱乐部 techno 与实验声响设计领域。音乐风格扎根于经典 Chain Reaction 系的 dub techno 传统，同时融入声音设计与极简主义元素。十分钟长曲 Mokira Ultra Dub 展现厚重质感的回响氛围，其余曲目在抽象电子、暗黑律动与实验声响之间游走。整体定位介于舞池功能性与听觉实验之间，呼应 Actress、Rezzett、Mokira 等当代实验电子音乐人的美学路径，属于独立地下电子场景中兼顾深度与多样性的扎实之作。

items._cn_summary: Khun Narin Electric Phin Band 是一支来自泰国北部乡村的多代际迷幻摇滚乐队，《III》是他们的第三张专辑兼首张录音室作品。乐队核心特色在于将泰国传统三弦拨弦乐器 phin 通过自制电路和廉价效果器进行信号处理，融合 DIY 电子美学与迷幻自由摇滚即兴传统。他们使用自制乐器搭配大型自制音响系统，延续了 2013 年因 YouTube 短视频在海外音乐圈走红的那种粗粝原始的能量。这张作品将东南亚民间音乐传统与实验性电子声响相结合，体现了乡村仪式即兴精神在当代迷幻摇滚语境中的延伸，属于世界音乐与实验音乐交叉领域的独特案例，兼具文化异域性与声音实验性。

items.album: David A. Jaycock :: Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] (Subexotic)
items.excerpt: This is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. The suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock   Reflectin
items.body: This is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. The suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock   Reflecting a conceptual framework deeply familiar to me as a generational conceit—Cold War nihilism and the erstwhile apocalyptic triptych—David A. Jaycock channels Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] with remarkable emotional precision, beautifully building on his frankly magnificent, intelligent discography thus far. The spectral ache of “Raymond Briggs’ When the Wind Blows” lingers throughout this musical equivalent: a work that captures both the naïveté and fragile beauty of the human waltz when refracted through that same recurring self-sabotaging hubris—the assumption that humanity alone are the rightful architects of profit alone, war, where we are seen functioning primarily as an economy disguised as an ideology of safety or rescue. As a result, a soulful, melancholic humility is woven throughout the album’s musical palette. There is sadness here. There is a deeper knowing that belies the intent. Jaycock understands, through lived experience, the emotional residue left behind by generations raised beneath the abstract possibility of absolute annihilation. The album is a reflection of that. Sonically, the tracks evoke those same BBC Sound Effects themes and atmospheres: enormous synthesis, tender tonality, vast reverbs, and big drums carry a cinematic weight without ever surrendering their innate intimate fragility. Melodies tenderly strum, and arpeggiations roll and coil gently; tempos remain calm, measured, almost comforting—and that restraint ultimately strengthens the conceptual brilliance of the work. It is an exceptionally well-executed, collated duality of paradox: human advancement through its own experience in real time. Tracks such as the beatific opener “Circling the Church,” or track three’s synth-pop-inflected “Butterflies Disco,” recall the emotional architecture of early DinDisc-era OMD before the hairstyles, presets, and pop polish calcified the aesthetic. There is an overt sincerity in the open-hearted circuitry. There is vulnerability inside the man-machine. For me, the standout on my second listen is “Secret Bunkers Under Civic Centres,” where colossal synth textures form a glowing, miasmic wall of oranges and yellows, through which warm winds carry a delicious rolling synth figure bearing faint flute-like traces of BoC-style pastoral dislocation. But that possibly inhibitory simile is merely a reflection of a similar DNA through the cultural mores and timeframe of history itself—a generational propensity lost elsewhere. Echoes of an imagined dystopia that never truly disappeared :: The warmth of the album becomes iridescent and undeniable, neatly juxtaposing echoes of an imagined dystopia that never truly disappeared—and has now resurfaced in its attempts to profit from newer forms, as the money machine liquefies into the empty form it has always been: a resource for life more than the very reason to live it. I remember the inherited threat of doom. I remember the awareness of the capitalist machinery beneath it all—the arms trade swelling quietly beneath public language and political theatre. Yet despite the ever-present duality of darkness and light, fear and tenderness, Children of the Cold War is an example that ultimately arrives at something profoundly giving that cannot be bought, and is more human: the suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor. And wins. And in that sense, this is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] is available on Subexotic. [Bandcamp] Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock
items._cn_summary: David A. Jaycock的《Children of the Cold War [Phase 7]》是一部以冷战概念为框架的电子/氛围音乐作品，在独立厂牌Subexotic发行。作品以宏大的合成器音色、深远混响和电影化的鼓点为基调，营造出既亲密又浩瀚的声场氛围。曲目中融合了早期DinDisc时期OMD的合成流行质感与BoC式的田园疏离感，在旋律的温和铺陈与音墙的厚实构建之间取得平衡。整体呈现出忧郁、深沉的情绪质地，探讨人性在核威慑阴影下的脆弱与坚持。制作精良，概念完整，在电子与暗氛围的交汇地带展现了成熟的艺术控制力。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Taking out the flute, which unmistakably evokes Jethro Tull, Tausendf�ssler, the opening track of Embryo's second album, showcases a very funky clavinet, then the organ solo...and a strong percussion that is omnipresent; it's a quartet...with a guest sextet, and it shows in their sound!Time continues this free and bohemian rock, featuring flute and blurring the boundaries of psychedelia, jazz rock, and krautrock. When the organ replaces the flute, it becomes a completely different band, with a bassist possessing a great groove reminiscent of Glenn Cornick. In Eva's Nuvola, the second part of the track, Edgar Hofmann's saxophone recalls his bandmates in Eilif, and the percussion connects him to the earth like a root carrying moisture to its mother plant.Revenge maintains a funky feel with the keyboards at the forefront, reminiscent of Les McCann, but then the composition takes on more epic and progressive nuances with the saxophone, before returning to jazz with the organ. When a mellotron joins the saxophone section, the album's potential becomes clear.Spain Yes, Franco Finished, with its mellotron and saxophone, creates a very intimate jazz atmosphere, reminiscent of the soundtrack to Leandro "Gato" Barbieri's Last Tango in Paris, who himself was influenced by John Coltrane.Next, the flute and clavinet build a slightly flamenco melody, imbued with funk, and that percussion, as fundamental as it was for Santana's band in the Woodstock era, but here with his own personal contribution. The vocal part was somewhat weak, as in several German bands, but the emphasis was on the instrumental aspect, and in fact that compositional freedom went well with a less noticeable presence of the vocalist, leaving the starring role to the instruments and the composition.An African feel goes hand in hand with Sittin' At The Moon, foreshadowing the band's ethnic future, and which proves very fitting in fusion with the funk that runs throughout the album. Verwandlung... half progressive, half krautrock, with the keyboard traversing scales until finally forming, together with the mellotron, a melody where the saxophone and an improvised piano contribute jazzy energy, but from this strange atmosphere not unlike King Crimson or Soft Machine, and when Edgar Hofmann's violin joins in, it acquires progressive touches, always arising from improvisation and continuing to resonate in later albums like an echo with eternal returns.
items._cn_summary: 1971年德国乐队Embryo发行的第二张专辑，跨越爵士摇滚、前卫摇滚、克拉夫特摇滚与放克之间的边界，呈现出自由即兴的波西米亚气质。专辑以电风琴、古钢琴、弦乐合成器、萨克斯风与长笛为核心乐器，融合迷幻与前卫元素，在器乐编排上极具探索性。部分曲目已显露非洲节奏与世界音乐倾向，预示乐队后来的民族融合方向。评论将之与Jethro Tull、King Crimson、Soft Machine、Santana等乐队并置，凸显其跨界融合的丰富层次与即兴驱动的创作理念。作为德语区地下场景的早期作品，兼具爵士的自由精神与前卫摇滚的结构野心。

items.body: This is already the sixth album from the French act Dekad. We had to wait another four years for “A Distorted View”, but fortunately the excellent predecessor “Nowhere Lines” (2022) remained fresh in our memories. Operator JB Lacassagne has prepared ten new tracks for us, preceded by the single “I Should Have”. The album offers a diverse selection of material: on the one hand, harder, darker, and highly danceable songs infused with clear EBM elements, interwoven with the characteristic beeps and sequencer patterns so typical of the French Boredom label; on the other hand, quieter, more ethereal, and even ballad-oriented Electro-Pop compositions. Throughout the album, these contrasting elements are held together by a strong foundation of melodic Pop sensibilities. The first half of the album is simply outstanding. Despite the wide range of influences and styles, one excellent track follows another. From menacing atmospheres and aggressive sequences filled with dark sonic manipulations to soft, dreamy passages enhanced by refined arrangements, Dekad seems capable of turning everything he touches into gold. The closing tracks lose a little of the momentum established earlier on. They are by no means weak, but they do feel somewhat less inspired compared to the album’s strongest moments. From a technical and production standpoint, this may well be Dekad’s finest album to date, although I still have a particular fondness for its predecessor. Either way, “A Distorted View” is an essential listen and a welcome highlight within today’s often rather predictable Electro-Pop landscape. (Rating:8). Listen to “Adrenaline”: https://boredomproduct.bandcamp.com/track/adrenaline
items._cn_summary: 法国电子艺人Dekad的第六张专辑，融合EBM的硬朗律动与电子流行的梦幻质感，兼具暗潮氛围与旋律流行基底。专辑前半段在深沉的序列器模式、黑暗声响处理与柔和梦幻段落之间自如切换，展现出成熟的制作水准与多样的风格驾驭力。后半段略显动能回落，但整体技术完成度高，是独立暗潮/EBM厂牌中品质稳定的作品。风格契合暗潮与电子领域偏好，但在实验性与前卫突破方面相对保守，旋律流行元素的比重使其更偏向精致的类型化制作而非先锋探索。

items.body: My heart is wounded on the left side Your shot hit the mark the first time Terminal Serious’s Every Time You Cry, written and directed by Elio De Filippo, is a black-and-white miniature about attachment, memory, and the strange prestige people grant to their own pain. Terminal Serious typically works within dark wave, cold wave, post-punk, and alternative rock, but this new single carries a leaner, more elegant chill. For the first time, the band gives up electric bass in favour of old Roland analogue synthesizers, which lend the track an icier architecture. The guitars have changed as well; with the overdrive switched off, they cut with precision, less brute force than bright blade. Filmed by Jessica Squillante with a cool debt to silent cinema, the video follows a woman, played with severe delicacy by Federica Mancuso, in the company of…a rock. The object is plain enough to seem comic at first, a mute companion dragged through private space, but De Filippo gives it the gravity of a relic. It is burden, anchor, witness, and beloved nuisance, an earthly mass that turns feeling into something touchable. Every Time You Cry keeps drama close to the body. Love becomes a wound with aim, striking the heart on the left side and leaving it marked by first contact. Yet the video widens that private injury into a study of habit: how pain becomes company, how company becomes identity, and how difficult it can be to lay down what one has learned in the shape of one’s hands. “Now that everyone has a camera pointed at them, everything becomes narration, but no one really knows each other anymore,” says the band. “We still believe in video as a tool for inner investigation, a story of the viscera. We’ve focused on the pain of separation, trying to explain how, paradoxically, pain makes us seem special. We grow fond of that boulder that slowly drags us down, because the fear of abandoning it is greater. Until the luckiest can balance the boulders in a delicate “cairn” of good and bad memories, which ultimately make up who we are.” That explanation could have produced a stiff Symbolist exercise, but De Filippo favours touch, posture, and pressure. The mind becomes a mason, arranging grief into cairns, small architectures of survival made from weight rather than air. Anna Flavia Castaldo’s presence deepens the piece’s sense of doubled interior life, while the stark photography gives each gesture a clean, almost ceremonial force. The band’s literary inspirations, from Virgil, Dante, and Petrarch to the smaller epics of complicated lives, sit quietly beneath the surface. Every Time You Cry treats separation as a material problem: how to lift what hurts, where to set it down, and whether the pile it forms might become sturdy enough to live beside. Watch below: The song belongs to Tear You Away, Terminal Serious’s third full-length album and the follow-up to Fear and Cure, released a year and a half earlier. The record moves through pride and shame, envy and boredom, fear and loneliness, dependence and bodily unease: ordinary states with the power to knock serenity out of reach. Still, the album keeps a narrow path open toward hope and rebirth, treating contradiction as part of daily life rather than a grand exception. Listen to Every Time You Cry below, and order Tear You Away here. items._cn_summary: Terminal Serious是来自意大利的暗潮/后朋克乐队，新单曲"Every Time You Cry"收录于其第三张全长专辑《Tear You Away》。音乐上首次放弃电贝斯，转而采用Roland模拟合成器，构建出更冷峻、精致的声音架构，电吉他卸去过载后呈现出刀刃般的锋利感。MV以黑白影像呈现，向默片致敬，由Elio De Filippo执导，描绘一位女性与一块石头相伴行走的故事——石头被赋予遗物般的庄严，象征情感的重量、记忆的锚点与分离之痛。乐队援引维吉尔、但丁、彼特拉克的文学谱系，将私人创伤升华为关于痛苦如何转化为身份认同的寓言。整体展现出暗潮范畴中较为突出的文学性与影像艺术深度，声音设计偏向克制与精密。

items.body: Oppenheimer MKII’s Oh! My Mind Is a Storm is paranoia rendered as pop machinery: compact, severe, oddly catchy, and built around the sense that the private mind has become a public emergency. The duo of Andy Oppenheimer, on lyrics and vocals, and Mahk Rumbae, on arrangements and production, work inside a strain of icy synth-pop that has always understood dread as a useful dance partner. Here, that dread is internalized, digitized, and sent back through the screen as a command. Mahk Rumbae’s production tightens around it with crunchy drums, rippling minimal synths, and ghostly pads that recall an eighties science-fiction serial caught between public-access television and a government transmission. Andy Oppenheimer’s soft-clipped delivery lands like a machine reciting beat poetry after reading too many classified reports. That sense of psychic pressure is the point. Oh! My Mind Is a Storm drives panic into club form, with Andy Oppenheimer declaring, ‘When I go dark, I’m into demon mode’. The line is funny, faintly ridiculous, and unnervingly current, catching the way contemporary anxiety often borrows the language of online performance. Demon mode becomes a state of overload, a persona, a coping mechanism, a threat. The accompanying video is deliberately austere: Andy Oppenheimer faces the camera, his head floating in greyscale, the image warped and reduced until he appears less like a performer than a transmission that has survived from some late-twentieth-century broadcast bunker. There is a touch of Max Headroom in the presentation, though drained of commercial smirk and turned into something more spectral: a pair of cathode-tube ghosts, bending time while barely moving at all. The minimalism suits the song. Nothing distracts from the faces, the voices, or the sense of a mind caught in feedback with itself. Watch below: The track also sharpens the broader concerns of Embrace The Dark, the long-awaited second album from Oppenheimer MKII, due June 30th via Wave Tension Records. Embrace The Dark does exactly as its title suggests: it welcomes dark, apocalyptic themes for our current turbulent times. In nine mind-blowing tracks, Mahk’s thunderous dance rhythms and addictive synth-pop melodies combine with Andy’s latest dystopian (and sometimes utopian) visions of our past, present and future. Andy Oppenheimer, formerly one-half of the cult 1980s synth-pop duo Oppenheimer Analysis, brings the clipped authority of the early minimal-synth era, while Mahk Rumbae, known for Codex Empire, Mitra Mitra, and Konstruktivists, gives the material a harder frame. Since their 2013 debut, The Presence of the Abnormal, Oppenheimer MKII have issued singles through Falco Invernale Records, Peripheral Minimal, and TONN Recordings. With “Oh! My Mind Is a Storm,” Oppenheimer MKII turns mental overload into a stark little broadcast from the edge of the future. Listen to Oh! My Mind Is a Storm below and order the album here. My Mind Is a Storm》定位为冰冷极简合成器流行与暗潮后朋克的交叉地带。评论以偏执狂作为切入，描述其制作包含清脆鼓机、涟漪式极简合成器音色及幽灵般垫底音，营造出八十年代科幻电视剧与政府广播之间的氛围感。MV 采用极简灰度处理，致敬 Max Headroom 的视觉语言，将人声转化为来自二十世纪末广播掩体的信号残片。专辑《Embrace the Dark》由独立厂牌 Wave Tension Records 发行，收录九首曲目，延续极简合成器时代的节制美学与硬派舞曲节奏的结合，主题涉及反乌托邦与当代焦虑。整体属于地下暗潮/后朋克圈层内的扎实作品，风格辨识度清晰但实验性与前沿性有限。

items.body: You felt so big when you held me down You’re not so tough now I’ll rise, and he will drown Black Bordello’s latest single, Numb-Lock, is a song that begins in a theatre of injury, but its drama is never decorative. The London art-rock group, led by Sienna Bordello, treats excess as a form of precision: operatic singing, gothic glamour, piano-room grandeur, and lyrics that peer into psychic damage without turning it into costume. Here, the band narrows its aim. The subject is physical abuse, inflicted by a former friend, and the strange afterlife of the body once trust has been turned into threat. Numb-Lock is concerned less with spectacle than with the slow return of sensation: the frozen mind, the private inventory of harm, the labor of self-protection when the danger has passed but the body has kept its own evidence. Bordello sings with an almost formal control, allowing emotion to gather through restraint rather than volume alone. Her soprano can recall Kate Bush’s bright altitude, Kristeen Young’s melodrama, and Siouxsie Sioux’s theatrical command, though its force here comes from the way she lets beauty carry dread without sweetening it. The arrangement has the broad, dangerous elegance of a Bond theme, but Black Bordello gives that scale a bruised interior. Classical flourishes rise against post-punk undertow; the song moves with ceremony, yet its emotional motion is jagged, as if each grand entrance must first pass through a locked room. Altsach’s production gives the instruments enough space to loom without crowding the central performance. When the track swells, the effect is architectural: arches, chandeliers, cracked plaster, a voice standing in the middle, too exacting for easy rescue. Produced by Balazs Altsach, the single takes the shape of an orchestral post-punk ballad, built for velvet curtains and hard facts, with strings and bass pressure moving around Bordello’s voice as if the room were being rearranged by memory itself. Numb-Lock suggests that a band’s most powerful work often may come when the music is made to serve a wound, and the wound is allowed to speak in a voice large enough to survive it. Listen to the song below, or via the band’s streaming page here: Numb-Lock by Black Bordello Since forming after the pandemic, Black Bordello have built a career on theatrical risk. They have shared stages with The Libertines, Goat Girl, Fat Dog, and Pete Doherty, while recent appearances at Left of the Dial and New Colossus have placed them in a wider transatlantic frame. With a third album drawing attention, and 2026 dates including London’s 100 Club, Kendal Calling, Oslo, Berlin’s 8mm Festival, and selected shows supporting David J, Black Bordello are moving with unusual assurance, gathering baroque ambition into something hard, lucid, and oddly intimate. items._cn_summary: Black Bordello是一支来自伦敦的后朋克/哥特艺术摇滚乐队，由Sienna Bordello领导。这首单曲将歌剧式女高音、古典管弦乐编制与后朋克底色融合，形成类似邦德电影主题曲的宏大优雅，但内部带有伤痕般的暗沉质感。制作上由Balazs Altsach操刀，弦乐与贝斯在声乐周围构建出建筑感的空间层次。该作品主题涉及身体伤害与创伤后的知觉恢复，歌词与演唱克制而精准，避免了戏剧化的浮夸。音乐风格上接近暗潮/后朋克与当代古典的交汇地带，女声演绎兼具Kate Bush的高远与Siouxsie Sioux的剧场感。作为独立厂牌发行的作品，其跨界融合的野心与艺术表达均有一定水准。

items.body: Eyes wide weary to a midday sun Oh! what could have been The Monolithic slab of this endless drab We’re living, in the cracks between NAUT’s latest single, Liberation, comes barging out of Bristol as both a warning flare and a love letter to the goth club as a sanctuary: a room set against the technocratic nightmare of compliance, optimization, surveillance, and dead-eyed productivity. Outside, the world measures, manages, and flattens the self into data. Inside, under low light and heavy sound, outsiders gather, move, and become whole. That opposition sits at the heart of goth itself. Gothic romanticism has always been the enemy of clean systems and obedient surfaces, answering utility with mystery, control with desire, productivity with ritual, and rational order with the unruly intelligence of grief, beauty, fear, and longing. For NAUT, this is no abstract pose. The band were born on goth dancefloors around the world, forged in the spaces where the strange find recognition, and where night offers a freedom the day cannot authorize. Liberation treats the night as a force of release: the hour when fear loosens, false selves fall away, and the dark night of the soul becomes a kind of transformation. The track confronts both personal darkness and the wider machinery of control and compliance, treating inner turmoil and outside pressure as parts of the same struggle. Its death-rock heft comes across as disciplined rather than gaudy, with coldwave restraint folded into a thicker, more physical frame. The guitars descend in heavy black planes, sharpened at the edges, while the synthesizers sit at a glacial remove, throwing the bass into relief. Beneath it all, the drum machine advances with bureaucratic menace, each strike suggesting the dull violence of systems that never need to raise their voice. The lyrics to Liberation aim their anger at the systems that shape modern life: work targets, digital metrics, managed desire, and the dead-screen obedience of a world lived through devices. NAUT set private ambition and historical burden inside that same tightening mechanism, where the self is measured, monitored, and made useful until little remains but exhaustion and performance. The song treats the daylight world as a monolithic slab of endless drab, a regime of polished surfaces, shrinking choices, and constant compliance, where the human soul is expected to survive in the cracks between. Against that machinery, the club becomes a counter-institution: a place where the body is no longer something to discipline, optimize, or make productive, but something to release. The chorus rises with the severe grandeur of a vaulted ceiling, while the bassline keeps the song locked to the floor, reminding us that transcendence can begin with movement, with hips, shoulders, boots, and bodies finding freedom together before anything reaches the heavens. The DIY video, filmed in Bristol, sharpens this idea by refusing elaborate explanation in favour of pressure, performance, and nocturnal momentum. It carries the charge of a horror film opening in real time, less through plot than through atmosphere: bodies caught in artificial light, faces moving through darkness, the band appearing as both witnesses and accelerants. Watch the video for Liberation below: Following the release of Hunt, and after tours alongside Creeper, The March Violets, She Past Away, and Katatonia, NAUT sound tighter, meaner, and more club-minded here. Liberation is gothic post-punk built for boots on sticky floors, for mascara running by choice, and for freedom from the status quo. Listen to Liberation below, and order the single here. items._cn_summary: NAUT是来自布里斯托尔的哥特摇滚乐队，单曲《Liberation》将死亡摇滚的厚重质感与冷潮（coldwave）的克制冷静相融合，鼓机以机械化节奏营造出制度性的压迫感，合成器冰冽疏离，吉他以沉重的黑色块面下沉，贝斯线则将整首作品锁定于舞池律动。歌词层面，作品将哥特俱乐部塑造为对技术官僚体制的抵抗空间，以夜晚作为自我释放的仪式化力量，主题涉及数字监控、绩效管理与主体性的丧失。该作品根植于哥特/后朋克传统，在声音设计上具有一定工业电子元素，但整体仍属类型框架内的扎实创作，概念表达明确，乐评文字详实且具一定思想深度，适合暗潮与哥特类音乐爱好者。

items.body:
Brazil’s premiere guess-again specialists Lugar Alto have been threatening to unleash this one for a while and here it finally is; compiled by the goat GG Albuquerque and mixed by label enigma Akira Umeda, “My Life is a Movie and In It I Am the Villain” is a compendium of signature DJ drops and idents used in soundsystems from Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo going back to the 1980's and right up to the present day - a genuinely synapse-popping madness that maps the constant evolution of the most vibrant and forward-facing soundsystem cultures of our time...

If you've spent any time with Brazilian funk, you'll know the sonorous intros - always larger-than-life, tongue-in-cheek, fluoro-flavoured - almost as important as the songs themselves. You don't have to understand Portuguese to get the message, either; the cacophony of pitch-wonked vocal stims, familiar samples, pop culture references and cheapo effects is borderless in its appeal, a core component of contemporary funk that's just as important as the syncopated tamborzão beat itself. We've copped tracks that are entirely reliant on the "carimbos" (literally "stamps") and "vinhetas" (intros) so we were hoping someone would put together something like this. And Lugar Alto - the Brazilian imprint responsible for releasing those essential DJ Ramon Successo LPs and that shocking Djalma Corrêa anthology - have taken the most impressive approach imaginable, tasking fount of all knowledge and journalist GG Albuquerque (last seen putting together that sick MÉDIO GRAVE tape for Nyege Nyege Tapes) with compiling something from a genuine street's-eye perspective.

The mix tells a non-linear, multi-dimensional story of Brazilian sound system culture, using DJ drops, stage calls, adverts, cheeky samples and explosive intros made between the 1980s and 2025. It takes us from the point where local sounds collided with funk, freestyle, electro and Miami bass in the wake of 'Planet Rock’ to the moment the scene eventually evolved into the splintered landscape of bruxaria, ritmado, brega and other sounds that we can interface with today via TikTok and Insta. It's a dense, fittingly psychedelic and suitably impertinent mosaic of references, in-jokes and mind-tickling sonics that's seemingly without beginning or end, a time-fluxing braindump of laugh tracks and aborted rhythmic snaps that's best compared to being airlifted into a Rio street party after being shot with medical-grade ketamine. Within a matter of seconds we get John Williams' 'Star Wars' intro followed by a Portuguese Darth Vader voice and a barrage of buzzing "tuin" effects - and it just gets madder and more frenetic from there.

A sort of heatsick parallel narrative to decades of British pirate radio culture, 'Minha Vida...' Is an incredible artefact of a movement that defies easy categorisation, a multi-coloured collage of sounds, humour and idiosyncratic energy that's driven the sound since the very beginning. You can take the boom-cha-cha boom-cha-cha beat, but you can't even begin to mimic the sheer gusto.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了里约热内卢和圣保罗音响系统文化中的DJ口号、标识和声音片段，时间跨度从1980年代至2025年。由GG Albuquerque策划、Lugar Alto独立厂牌发行，呈现巴西funk音响文化从早期受freestyle、electro和Miami bass影响，逐步演变为当代bruxaria、ritmado、brega等流派的完整脉络。整张作品以非线性的拼贴手法构建，混合格调怪异的变调人声、流行文化引用、廉价音效与爆发性的intro段落，形成迷幻且层次丰富的声景。评论将其与英国海盗电台文化进行平行对照，既是一份独特的文化档案，也具备实验性的声响拼贴特质，兼具世界音乐与电子声响领域的跨文化价值。

items.body:
Alex Nut ushers his new band of crackshot players, Sum Of Its Parts, on a pair of lush jazz and beatdown cuts, backed with Boddhi Satva remixes.

Opening out into deep, jazzy space limned on his ‘Under Construction’ EP in ’25, Alex Nut gathers Sum Of Its Parts, aka Sam Crowe (Lianne La Havas) on keys, Junior Ali-Balogun (Sault/Cleo Sol) on percussion and Duane Atherley (Kokoroko) on bass, to explore expensive jazz horizons in the 8 mins of woozy sway to ‘The Message’, while locking tighter into a Detroit beatdown house shuffle ‘Hello High’ surely winking at classic KDJ and Theo Parrish. Brussels’ BBE & Yoruba regular Boddhi Satva resets ‘The Message’ to a sort of slowed, dubbed, and triplet-metered broken beat hustle in his signature Ancestral Soul style, and farther swept out with a dusky appeal on its dub.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由Alex Nut召集的爵士团体Sum Of Its Parts与布鲁塞尔制作人Boddhi Satva合作完成，呈现出爵士与电子舞曲的跨界融合。主打曲《The Message》以八分钟篇幅展开朦胧摇摆的爵士空间探索，乐手阵容来自Sault、Kokoroko及Lianne La Havas等英国当代爵士与灵魂乐场景。《Hello High》则转向底特律风格的beatdown house律动，向Moodymann和Theo Parrish等先辈致敬。Boddhi Satva的混音版将原曲重构为减速、三连音节拍的碎拍作品，带有其标志性的祖传灵魂风格。整体定位在学院爵士质感与地下舞曲文化之间，融合了碎拍、deep house与爵士即兴元素，但实验性和前卫程度相对克制。

items.body:
Surface Access chases a pair of ace dub techno 12”s for Nico Jaar's Other People with two more strips of claggy depth for East Paris label 59 Bel, tipped FFO Sa Pa, Intertoto, vintage Chain Reaction.

Both sides fathom flooded catacombs of club music for anyone bored with modern techno excess and seeking more muted immersion in the dance. In that sense, A-side ’Status.Density’ brings heads deep inside his sound with careful unfolding of FX envelopes drawing bodies into echoic play of shivered, coruscating chords and skudgy bass for nearly 10 minutes, and acting as entry portal to the more reserved depths of ‘Immersion Thrust’, packing more info in the low end shifts and yoked-back, smeared textures that plunge like the most mesmerising Substance & Vainqueur works.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品聚焦于深沉的Dub Techno领域，在法国东巴黎独立厂牌59 Bel发行，延续了Nico Jaar旗下Other People厂牌的地下电子脉络。整张EP如同一场潮湿的地下声音考古，FX包络的缓慢展开构建出回声弥漫的声响空间，闪烁的和弦与粗糙的低频质感相互交织。与当代Techno的浮夸形成对比，追求更为内敛、沉浸式的舞池体验。A面以近10分钟的绵延递进为入口，B面则在低频位移与拉伸质感中构建更深邃的声场层叠，呼应了Chain Reaction及Substance & Vainqueur等人的极简催眠美学。整体定位明确，属于偏向Ambient质感的深度电子乐，适合沉浸式聆听与凌晨时段的氛围型俱乐部场景，与实验电子及氛围音乐偏好高度吻合。

items.body:
Kosmiche krautrock mainstay Harald Grosskopf operates at full wingspan on a new raft of astral-planing arps and motorik pulses laced with wistful extended melodies and atmospheric sleaze, together with a titular nod to Miles Davis’hinting at the album’s underlying theme: the productive friction between man and machine.

"For the uninitiated, Grosskopf’s career spans six decades of German music history. From early beat groups in Hildesheim, through Krautrock propulsion with Wallenstein, cosmic explorations alongside Ashra, and defining work with Klaus Schulze, he has consistently pushed rhythm into evolving technological contexts. His 1980 solo debut Synthesist, previously reissued on Bureau B, helped establish a sequencer-driven language that bridged kosmische tradition and modern electronic form.

Created over three to four months in his garden studio, Glitches Brew is shaped by speed and responsiveness. Grosskopf worked primarily with digital instruments this time, travelling light and favouring fast access from feeling to recording. Ideas arrive spontaneously; he works until satisfied, often reshaping sounds the next day if they fail to spark with the same intensity. What emerges is a vivid, present-tense record where human instinct and electronic process remain in constant, audible conversation. Stems are recorded in mono or stereo, passed through a Studer desk and printed to two-track, restoring weight and tactility to digital sources. Where VST synthesis can lack transient bite, analogue circuitry restores what he calls the sensation of leather, wood and metal. The signal path is humanised without surrendering to nostalgia.

The opening track, “Leisure Life,” establishes the album’s language immediately: low-end bubbles and chewy filters pulse beneath crystalline sequencers and shuffling hats. Optimistic pads bloom around frazzled lead lines as the piece glides forward, building toward a rolling bass climax that feels both euphoric and grounded. Grosskopf has long embraced the click track, relishing the freedom it brought during sessions for Klaus Schulze’s Moondawn: when rhythm is sequenced, the drummer is freed from marking the “one,” and can instead explore texture and propulsion. That commitment to free movement persists here.

On “Spheroids,” stargazing synth motifs orbit percolating bass and alien percussion, slipping into a techno-pop wormhole. Midway through, dramatic trills rupture the flow like a gravitational tear before the groove reasserts itself with cosmic poise. “Flow” descends into colder terrain: icy chimes shimmer above a slow, low rhythm, while snaking lead lines and robotic churn carve through gloomy pads, creating a hypnotic, glacial drift.

“Stranger Strings” pushes further into the uncanny. Warped electronic strings emerge from cavernous reverb and short delays, entangled with mechanical pulses, whirring and hissing as if half-forgotten machines were stirring back to life. Yet Grosskopf never lingers in abstraction for its own sake. “Panta Rhei” snaps the album back into direct physicality, a driving, rhythmic surge pierced by heartrending synth strings and blinking circuitry, all anchored by the mother of all mutant funk basslines. It is elastic, restless and gloriously corporeal, a blast of body music which reaffirms his belief in groove as emotional catalyst.

“LiLaLu” shifts the mood again. Sampler voices and Fairlight-era textures drift through a shimmering digital dream, conjuring a romantic escape on the shores of the Sea of Tranquility. It’s space-age spa-core in the lineage of the old Innovative Communications aesthetic - retro-futurist, tender and quietly playful. By contrast, “Kalter Lärm” closes the album in uplift: rave-style hits, expansive pads and a roving bassline gather collective momentum, shoulders rolling and arms aloft, before dissolving into cosmic bliss.

Grosskopf has spoken of the early thrill he felt hearing The Beatles, the breathtaking shock of newness, and of the early 70s Berlin scene’s determination to detach from Anglo-American models and pursue something wholly original. That refusal to look backwards still guides him. Synthesisers were never retro fetish objects but tools of liberation, instruments capable of breaking from guitar history and opening fresh terrain, and he continues to embrace whatever technologies expand the field of possibility.

Glitches Brew balances analogue intuition and digital immediacy, kosmische heritage and contemporary electronic language. It is the work of an artist still following his own ideas, still excited by sound, still testing the edges. Sixty years on from his first beat-group rehearsals, Harald Grosskopf remains what he has always been: a musician for whom rhythm is liberation, technology is possibility, and the future is something to invent again and again. – Patrick Ryder, 2026"
items._cn_summary: 德国老牌Krautrock音乐人Harald Grosskopf发行的新专辑《Glitches Brew》，延续其横跨六十年德国电子音乐史的风格脉络。专辑以数字合成器为主，结合模拟电路处理，在音序器驱动的Motorik律动之上构建宇宙感的琶音与氛围肌理。标题致敬Miles Davis的《Bitches Brew》，暗示人与机器之间张力这一核心主题。曲目涵盖乐观的水晶音序与脉冲低音（Leisure Life）、Techno-pop风格的星际律动（Spheroids）、冰冽质感的极地漂移（Flow）以及幽暗机械声响交织的电子弦乐（Stranger Strings）。整体定位介于传统Kosmische与现代电子之间，强调即时创作与模拟质感的人性化回归，发行厂牌为德国独立厂牌Bureau B。

items.body:
A hardy perennial, Boards of Canada’s definitive "lost" 1995 debut is back in circulation for the first time in a few years.

Originally dished up on Marcus and Eoin Sanderson’s Music70 label in edition of only 100 copies in 1995, rumour has it that a copy was sent to Clair Poulton at Clear Records as a demo, who passed on it before Skam up in mcr signed up the pair for the Hi Scores 12", Aquarius 7" and eventually 'Music Has The Right To Children', released in conjunction with Warp. By the time Twoism was officially reissued in 2002, people had been known to spend upwards of £500 for original copies if they were lucky enough to find them.

Alongside Hi Scores, Twoism provides the definitive BoC blueprint, melding classic electro tropes with analog synth tones redolent of soundtracks to ‘70s and ‘80s Canadian nature programmes, sewing the seeds of a sound that would bloom in their classic 1998 side ‘Music Has The Right To Children’. It still slaps.
items._cn_summary: Boards of Canada 1995年首张专辑《Twoism》重新流通。这张被奉为乐队开篇之作的录音最初仅以100张限量形式由Music70厂牌发行，后由独立电子名厂Skam签约，最终在Warp旗下推出其代表作。音乐融合了经典电子律动与模拟合成器音色，带有浓厚的怀旧质感与低保真美学，音色氛围类似70至80年代加拿大自然纪录片配乐风格。作为BoC音乐版图的起点，此作为其1998年经典专辑《Music Has The Right To Children》的美学语言奠定了基础，在模拟温暖音色与电子律动之间构建了独特的听觉空间。

items.body:
Natty digi-dub frolics from Mermaid, a Japanese reggae dub and chamber music fiend, doubling down on his ’25 debut LP with 10 takes on Bach, Gossec, and trad Japanese songs inna dub style FFO Tapes, 7FO, Froid Dub, SKRS Intl., Disrupt.

One up to their debut LP, ‘Dubmaid’, Mermaid’s 2nd set pairs ostensibly, mutually exclusive bedfellows under the same sheets on handfuls of bubblers defined by piquant melodies and ruggedest, sine wave-sculpted bass. The combo works a treat for those who like to dance between styles, across borders, registering big cuts in his ludicrous flip of ‘Air on a G String’, and a nice ’n easy version of Gossec’s C.18th work ‘Gavotte in D’, and a Japanese traditional ‘1st January’ named ‘New Year’ and strapped with bubbling bass, also teased out in wilder dub on ‘Long Ago’. DJs and dancers also need to test out the moon boot cosmic skank of ‘A Nap’, and the Tempo Riddim-riffing ‘Lucifer’.
items._cn_summary: 日本制作人Mermaid的第二张专辑，将巴赫、戈塞克等欧洲古典曲目与日本传统民歌以数字dub手法重新演绎。整张作品以正弦波雕琢的低频为骨架，旋律线在dub的回响与延迟中若隐若现，既有'Gavotte in D'的柔和抒情，也有'Tempo Riddim'式的律动冲击。'New Year'与'Long Ago'两首对日本传统曲调的不同dub处理形成有趣的对照。Mermaid将巴洛克室内乐、日本传统音乐与雷鬼dub的结合展现出明确的跨文化实验意图，在地下dub与实验电子的交汇地带寻找独特的声音定位，对于关注电子与世界音乐融合的听众具有参考价值。

items.body:
Meditative new age ambient poetry recited by Benjamin Burke and fronded with modular synths, sitar, bells and bowls by Bear Glass and pals, shades away from Moondog or Ernest Hood​.

"Following streams of consciousness that contemplate the stardust that forms us to the very first human sound that reverberated through a cave, Shape of the Moon intertwines language and music into ambient dream-weaving narratives.

When the land is laid bare forms a collection of recordings composed of Burke reciting his introspective poems and Glass improvising gripping modular synth and string patterns. Burke brings a wealth of experience working between an impressively vast range of written and visual mediums to Glass’s live electronics and acoustic instrumentation mirroring the spoken word. The pieces on the album consist of excerpts from live outdoor performances under the night sky in the Mojave desert as well as sessions in Glass’s off-grid solar powered studio. Burke drapes vivid vocal narration over deeply immersive textures and melodies conjured up by Glass on Buchla, bass and sitar, painting peaks and valleys that live score the storytelling. The duo tread their own path fusing poetry with undulating electroacoustic instrumentals, arriving at meditative and ASMR territories that draw inspiration from ambient and electronica. Often joined on stage by guest musicians playing anything from Rhodes, percussion, jaw harp and saxophone, the recordings edge towards blues and spiritual jazz.

Benjamin Burke is a poet, writer, performer, and visual artist who spends his time lending a hand to unusual artistic expeditions around the world. Most recently, he helped to launch Dhun and Dhun School, a humanist eco-township and progressive education center on a 500 acre biopreserve in Rajasthan, India. He has written and performed countless unusual shows, experimenting widely and, through that, witnessing firsthand what makes ideas resonate for his audiences. This work evolved over time into an approach he refers to as Applied Poetics which he employs to help communities set intentions, scientists present their findings, and humanitarian organizations find their footing.

Bear Glass is a sound artist, multi-instrumentalist, music teacher, live sound engineer, and founding member of Mobius Acoustics who build innovative sound systems and host events on the West Coast (utilizing a quadraphonic setup for live performances and immersive drone bath sessions). Glass is involved in various collaborative projects with a couple of releases under different pseudonyms as well as a solo tape featuring a track with prolific producer Carlos Niño. For most of the year, Glass lives sustainably off-grid with his family on a plot of land outside Joshua Tree, a mini utopia infamous for his well curated private campouts and artist residencies. Wide skies, magnificent climates, and being surrounded by the love of family and friends inform Bear’s musical output and artistic practice."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将诗朗诵与模块化合成器即兴演奏深度融合，由诗人Benjamin Burke在声音艺术家Bear Glass的电子与原声乐器伴奏下完成。作品在加州莫哈韦沙漠户外夜空下以及离网太阳能工作室中录制，融合了Buchla合成器、低音吉他、西塔琴、钟磬与颂钵，并辅以Rhodes电钢琴、打击乐、口琴与萨克斯等客座乐器即兴。整体风格介于新纪冥想氛围与电子原声即兴之间，呈现出蓝调与灵性爵士的色彩。模块化合成器与原声乐器的实验性配器、即兴演绎的现场感以及沙漠环境的空间声场均体现出明确的实验音乐倾向，西塔琴等世界音乐元素也为作品增添了跨文化维度。不过作品整体偏重冥想与ASMR式的内省氛围，与偏好更激进前卫或暗潮工业风格的听感存在一定距离。

items.body:
PT Musik (fka Puto Tito) epitomises Príncipe’s brand of rugged but melancholic batida on a standout new album dripping with piquant hooks and puckered grooves set to travel far beyond his Lisbon base.

One of the many joys of following Príncipe is hearing its artists grow over the years, as with Domingos Aleixo’s shifts from a bare-boned but vividly colourful 2019 debut ‘Carregando A Vida Atrás Das Costas’, to the notably lusher, more romantic harmonies of the ‘Não Sou Perfito’ 7”, which introduced his name change in 2021.The confident swagger and shrug-it-off sentiments ramps up on his second LP ‘Consumação’, featuring eight cuts that amount to a properly charming self-portrait of an artist coming into his own.

The blend of reflective melody and variegated, seductive and then urgent rhythms that has kept us all rapt to Príncipe is in ideal effect on this one. Themes of broken relationships, loneliness and navigating life’s travails prompt PT to his strongest work, manifest in a strong grasp of expressive, extended melody and breezy vibes that transcends language and speaks directly to both dancing bodies and dreamy minds.

Hooks are bitter-sweet, edged with a tang of heightened emotional maturity from tarraxho opener ’Nha Budjura’ thru a sentimental fave ‘Hot Girl’ that first appeared on 2020’s ‘Verão Dark Hope’ comp, and now closes the LP with a glimpse of their former self. In between, they serve the club with proper orders of sinuous breeziness on ‘Lembranças’ and ‘Leave me Alone’, plus the needling heat of ‘Movimento’, reserving the most poignant moment to the ‘90s R&B soul-inflected ’Não Acredito’ and elegant, dusky ambiguity of ‘Me Suga’ with minor key harpsichord and pitch-bent leads bound to burrow into memory.
items._cn_summary: PT Musik（原名Puto Tito）来自里斯本，签约于以巴蒂达音乐闻名的独立厂牌Príncipe。专辑收录八首作品，融合电子制作与安哥拉/佛得角离散族群的传统舞蹈节奏（如塔拉沙），呈现出粗粝而忧郁的质感。曲目在旋律的反思性与节奏的多变性之间游走，主题涉及破裂的情感关系、孤独与生活挣扎。值得关注的是融入九十年代R&B灵魂乐元素的'Não Acredito'，以及使用大键琴与变调领奏的'Me Suga'，体现出跨风格融合的野心。整体定位为面向俱乐部场景的世界电子舞曲，在里斯本独特的非洲离散音乐文化语境下生长，具备较强的文化辨识度与情绪深度。

items.body:
Balmat alum Patricia Wolf flits to Ransom Note’s ambient tape series with a 45 min session of carefully pruned synth wooze and new age whims evoking private press cassettes via early ‘90s garden centres.

"‘Yarrow’ is a bouquet of new music by Portland, Oregon-based musician and field recordist Patricia Wolf, marking the label’s ninth release and the third of Season Two. The works are her reflections on the life cycle of plants and their dynamic ecological relationships.

Wolf created the album in response to her artist residency at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Gothic, Colorado, as part of the Art-Science Exchange Project in the summer of 2024. She worked closely with ecologists Dr Paul CaraDonna, Dr Amy Iler, Dr Jane Ogilvie, Dr Nickolas Waser, Dr Mary Price, and Dr Will Petry, spending weeks engaged in long-term research on plants, pollinators, and their interactions as the climate changes. 

Each track on Yarrow looks at a different part of a plant’s life. The songs touch on the conditions that plants need to grow, the quiet life of roots, how flowers attract pollinators, and the strength of seeds. The first single, 'Inflorescence', the scientific name for the floral display that a plant makes in an effort to reproduce, captures this event in song. The music slowly builds layers, reflecting the album’s overall feel. The album ends with the majestic Boards of Canada-esque 'Adapted for Extreme Conditions', and the entire b-side features Patricia’s field recordings from around Gothic, Colorado, and a guided meditation by Dr Paul CaraDonna, whose research inspired the project, inviting listeners to tune into the sounds and activities of the ecosystem."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是美国波特兰音乐人与田野录音师Patricia Wolf的作品，源自她在科罗拉多落基山生物实验室的艺术驻留项目。Wolf与多位生态学家合作，以植物生命周期为主题进行创作，融合了合成器氛围音景、新世纪元素与田野录音。整张专辑以缓慢层叠的电子织体为基底，搭配自然环境中的实地声音采样，呈现出冥想式的聆听体验。制作风格接近Boards of Canada的怀旧电子质感，同时带有九十年代私人出版磁带的精神气质。作为独立厂牌Ransom Note的磁带系列发行，这张作品在概念深度与环境氛围构建上具有独到之处，适合偏好实验氛围与跨界艺术合作的听众。

items.body:
Blackpool and Skam’s greaziest electro mutant coughs up an addendum to their first LP in decade with a side quest ,’Phasia’, that continues the B-movie misadventures of ‘Phocus’

‘Phasia’ feels like finding a near derelict - but actually open - video store on the backstreets on Blackpool (the bit where it gets really reel), and being granted access to the bit behind the chain curtains by a proprietor not dissimilar to the joke shop owner in The League of Gentlemen. Behind the rare blueys, video nasties and forbidden Chubby Brown section, lies a portal to ‘Phasia’; a wormhole into the high grade ’80s funk smut and fractalized memory reflux of VHS Head projected onto all walls and jacked into the nipples of local council bigwigs, the £1 burger bloke on his day off, and the likes of Lewis Jones and intrepid holidaymakers looking for summat a bit more exotic, y’know, for specialist tastes.

Between the neon sludge and brassy fanfare of opener ‘Locus’ and never-made-it-to-video-reverie ‘Phocus Trailer’, the cutting room floor offcuts of ‘Phocus’ make a highly entertaining album in their own right, swerving from the electro-jump-cuts of ‘Strange Food’ to screwed power-pop like Peter Gabriel on quaaludes in ‘Mouth Matte’, thru the heart-in-mouth romance of its title tune, the orchestral stab flashes of ‘Head Crimes’ to the briny tang of ‘Dream Peeping’, like some curdled Kate Bush, and killer drug chug of ‘Phocus’. Love it.
items._cn_summary: 英国电子音乐人VHS Head在曼彻斯特独立厂牌Skam旗下推出的续作专辑，延续首张全长专辑的影像化美学，以八十年代B级片录像带文化为视觉与听觉灵感。作品将复古电子、放克碎拍、流行扭曲与拼贴采样相融合，呈现出迷幻、粗糙且带有浓重怀旧质感的声响景观。曲目在电子跳切、管乐号角、弦乐碎片与梦幻流行之间游走，兼具娱乐性律动与实验探索精神。整张专辑如同对录像带时代的一次声音考古，介于复古致敬与前卫拼贴之间，风格上偏向带有怪奇趣味的实验电子路线。

items.body:
One of the weirdest gadges in UK dub flexes his authority on unique concoctions of roots reggae, digidub, cumbia, and folksy chamber drone for the Breadminster Board of Abstinence. big tipped FFO Nearly God, Tapes Lee “Scratch” Perry & The Congos, Elysia Crampton, DINTE archives.

In cool pursuit of his reggae-voiced folk covers LP for FatCat, ‘Perpetual Musk’ - and 12”s for Accidental Meetings, Elijah Minnelli keeps it ideally offbeat with a deft, hands-on concision and deeply rooted steez throughout ‘Clams As A Main Meal.’ There’s a charmingly daft backstory involving oysters, frisky fictional villagers, and burnt-out hippies, that gives the LP its title, but let’s focus on the music here. 

It’s dead special stuff, surely certified by Dennis Bovell chiming in like all members of The Congos at once in the swaying harmonies knit to nyabinghi drums in ‘Canaan Land' somehow sounding like a score to an Emir Kusturica film, while Welsh singer Carwyn Ellis helps characterise Minnelli’s dare-to-differ audness on the sea-legged cumbia shanty ‘Donna Donna (Chwerthin)’ which clearly suits their lilt of their mother tongue. 

Elsewhere the producer’s feted dub tekkerz and feel for proper folk wise dub groove really come into play, in step from the jaw harp twang and jaw bone friction dematerialised in ‘Sumptuous Promise,’ thru a heavy lamenting ‘Watercraft Apologist’ that wouldn’t sound out of place in a Mark Jenkin flick, to the insectoid digidub of ‘Calopify Now!,’ gently psychoactive cumbia of ‘Bomb the Green Belt,’ and ghostly chamber keen of ‘Long Conifer.’ Play it over and again!
items._cn_summary: 英国制作人Elijah Minnelli的专辑将根源雷鬼、数码dub、cumbia与民间室内嗡鸣等元素融于一炉，呈现高度实验化的跨文化声响图景。制作风格强调手工质感与低保真美学，邀请Dennis Bovell参与人声编排，威尔士语元素与拉丁美洲节奏相互交织。整体氛围偏怪异、疏离，具有强烈的地下独立气质。专辑在dub框架下融入了世界音乐、实验声响设计与当代室内音乐的多重维度，适合偏好跨界融合与异质审美的听众。来自小型独立厂牌，定位明确指向小众实验听众群体。

items.body:
Belgian avant-pop outfit Sergeant return to STROOM with a second album and a new member. RIYL Milan W, Total Blue or Animal Collective.

Since 2023's self-titled debut album, movie bro Benjamin Cools and actor Ferre Marnef have invited a new artist into the fold. The project was initially conceived as a live band, so the additional personnel just allows Sergeant to spread their creative wings; 'Symbols' is a more complicated record than its predecessor, packed out with byzantine arrangement and layered compositions, but it's also tighter. There's a feeling that their influences - '80s DIY pop, krautrock and post-punk - have been more fluidly lashed together this time around and Marnef's voice sounds more assured bedded in his collaborators' woozy, sometimes spiky productions. 

If their last record was "DJ Shadow in reverse", made from collaged elements and half-songs, 'Symbols' is a suite of proper compositions that dissolve as they play out, with tempos fluctuating and components mutating and vaporizing as Marnef sings. It's pop music that's engineered with Martin Hannett's ear for wacked-out production - fans of Ariel Pink (before he went full fash) or Panda Bear's 'Person Pitch' should investigate without delay.
items._cn_summary: 比利时前卫流行乐队Sergeant的第二张专辑，由独立厂牌STROOM发行。作品融合了八十年代DIY流行、克拉夫特摇滚与后朋克的元素，编曲繁复且层次丰富，制作风格让人联想到Martin Hannett式的迷幻扭曲质感。专辑相比首作结构更完整但也更复杂，作曲更加正统，却在展开过程中不断溶解、变形，节奏与构成元素在演唱过程中持续流动与消散。新成员的加入拓宽了创作的边界，人声在迷离且偶尔尖锐的配器中更加沉稳自信。整体定位介于前卫流行与实验声响之间，适合对后朋克及实验制作感兴趣但不排斥旋律性的听众。

items.body:
100% Silk veteran, Wisconsin’s Auscultation, does his raw but slinky, offbeat electro-house thing at a breezy mid-and-downtempo pace on the ever-charming label.

Their 4th bow on Amanda Brown’s sophisticate sub-division of NNF pursues a fine feel for dream house puckered with syncopated electro pulses and glazed in shine-eyed pads. It makes for warmest comparisons with vintage ’90s Rephlex of Bochum Welt in the iridescent whirl and parry of ‘Dysania’, and touches on Balihu-esque disco-house élan on ‘Mend’, while ‘Lusting’ slips of to Haruomi Hosono-like intricacies, and ‘Pinned’ drifts into dreamy dub. His strolling 8 min standout ’Severed Cord’ is primed for summer waft-offs, along with the effortless, feathered whirr of ‘Hazel Vacancy’.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由来自威斯康星州的电子制作人Auscultation操刀，是其在独立电子厂牌100% Silk的第四张作品，收录于Not Not Fun的子厂牌。音乐风格以中低速的电子浩室为核心，融合梦幻浩室的迷离质感与错拍电子脉冲，并点缀Dub氛围与迪斯科浩室的律动。评论将其与经典Rephlex厂牌旗下Bochum Welt的虹彩质感、细野晴臣式的精巧细节以及Balihu的迪斯科浩室气质相比较，定位介于智能电子舞曲与休闲电子之间。整体氛围轻盈通透，旋律悦耳，编曲成熟，但并未走向极端实验或先锋路线，更偏向精致的俱乐部向电子制作。

items.excerpt: Accident Fantôme is the portmanteau for the project of two otherwise autonomous, established musical duos, Accident du Travail and Fantôme Josepha. United by shared interests in historical instruments and long-form, ambient drone composition, the four gathered in an old church in a village just west of Metz (where some of the group are based) early last year to perform and record together.
items.body:
Home/Reviews/Accident Fantôme
ACCIDENT FANTÔME — OBJETS ENCHÂSSÉS DANS DES ANNEAUX PLANÉTAIRES( OBJECTS EMBEDDED IN A PLANETARY RING )
[moli del tro — 2026]
★
★
★
★
★
Reviewed 5 June 2026
by Colin Lang
Artist website →

Accident Fantôme is the portmanteau for the project of two otherwise autonomous, established musical duos, Accident du Travail and Fantôme Josepha. United by shared interests in historical instruments and long-form, ambient drone composition, the four gathered in an old church in a village just west of Metz (where some of the group are based) early last year to perform and record together.

The ecclesiastical setting was selected for its mid-19th-century pipe organ — the instrument par excellence of the dronies — along with its remoteness, outside of the hustle and bustle, though situated near the Front of the First World War and all its spectres. In addition to said organ, Objects Embedded in a Planetary Ring features guitar, harp, and the ondes Martenot, one of the earliest electric instruments, which, following in its use by Messiaen, Boulez, and others, has become something of a cult object among French classicists.

“Cosmos“: the opening track, is a swirl of harp and organ, pulling heavenward with little to no anchor, so that when an electric guitar struts its way into the mix, we get a bit more electronics and processing along with it. The whole thing is drowning in reverb, whether added through effects or culled from the church environs, it makes for an engrossing if familiar haze. “Euphorie”, the longest of the five compositions, leans pretty heavily into the organ, a single chord depressed, vibrating and blanketing the empty space into which it moans. Here, we get the clearest picture of the theremin-like whirling of the ondes Martenot, which takes us out of the house of worship and onto Mars. All of this ushers in some higher frequency squeaks before Brother Pipes takes control of the party. The last piece, “Brief Whistling” is just that, something straight out of a Morricone Western, Cinecittà suddenly rolling over the graves of unnamed soldiers.

Fans of lowkey drone and the cinematic side of ambient work should find plenty to scratch that itch. Others interested in the otherworldly beauty of the ondes Martenot should probably tune in too.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Radwan Ghazi Moumneh与Frédéric D. Oberland的首张合作专辑，两位音乐人此前在Godspeed You! Black Emperor与Oiseaux-Tempête等实验/后摇滚项目中已积累了丰富经验，因此并非真正意义上的首次接触。Moumneh拥有黎巴嫩-加拿大双重文化背景，为作品注入了中东音乐元素与世界音乐视角；Oberland则以欧洲前卫声响美学著称。专辑融合了实验音乐、仪式民谣、即兴演奏与氛围电子等多种元素，在学院派实验与世界音乐交汇的地带展开探索。Songlines作为世界音乐权威媒体的关注进一步印证了其跨文化声响实验的定位。原文内容过于简短，仅为开篇片段，无法对专辑全貌和具体音乐细节做出更深入的判断。

items.body: I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by David Dzubinski as part of the Prism Quartet 's new series of collaborations called Unlocking Your Inner Composer . If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this. Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist Ursula Rucker , percussionist Tyshawn Sorey , and violinist Carlos Santiago to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor Find Prism Quartet online.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品由作曲家David Dzubinski创作，Prism Quartet萨克斯四重奏与诗人Ursula Rucker、实验打击乐家Tyshawn Sorey及小提琴家Carlos Santiago合作呈现，属于'Unlocking Your Inner Composer'系列。作品时长不到四分钟，在粗粝与抒情之间快速切换，融合室内乐、实验爵士与口语诗歌，呈现出跨界即兴的特质。Prism Quartet以打破流派边界著称，Sorey的参与进一步强化了作品的先锋爵士色彩。整体定位介于当代古典、自由即兴与实验音乐之间，是面向小众听众的实验性合作项目。乐评本身偏短，偏向编辑推荐性质，深度分析有限。
