items.body: Króta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Edén has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sjøfløyte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with “Fossgrimen,” a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish “Polska from Per Myhr,” having played a repeated introductory riff on the sjøfløyte, with Mats Edén providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Edén who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio From the title of "Springar from Knut Nord-Juveli" we learn that it was taken from the repertoire of a renowned sjøfløyte player from Numedal, a valley in the east of Norway and is an appropriate feature for Tellef Kvifte. A springar is a Norwegian triple-beat dance whose three beats vary in length depending on which region of Norway the tune comes from. In this case the underlying pulse resembles that of a rhumba with each bar having two similar beats followed by a shorter one; but the melodic structure is unmistakably Norwegian with a motif being repeated, then the third time through it developing into a variation. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio “På Siljan“ was taken from a collection of old Swedish tunes, but the version here is not so much an interpretation as a deconstruction of an item from the Swedish fiddle tradition. Beginning with Edén playing freely, seeking out the resonances of the fiddle through the gentle scraping of the strings with the bow, the tune eventually arrives quietly through the back door, carried by Kvifte on his sjøfløyte while Edén continues to improvise, along with Nesheim playing loosely around his kit. Tellef Kvifte pretty much sticks to the tune, a thread that runs through the track while the other two work around it, creating a rich sound texture, the listener being challenged to decide which is in front and which is behind. An adventurous and worthwhile endeavour which shows once again how traditional music can be not merely a legacy to uphold, but a catalyst for creativity. Find the artists online. Mats Edén Tellef Kvifte Knut Kvifte Nesheim Further reading: Groupa - Kind Of Folk Volume 2: Norway Guro Kvifte Nesheim and Floating Sofa Quartet - Kystnært Tellef Kvifte - The Norwegian Bagpipe (?) Vol.2
items._cn_summary: Króta是瑞典小提琴家Mats Edén、挪威横笛与多乐器演奏者Tellef Kvifte及鼓手Knut Kvifte Nesheim组成的三重奏专辑，收录于挪威独立厂牌Taragot。三位音乐人将斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲（挪威springar、瑞典polska等）以非传统方式重新演绎，弱化舞蹈功能，转而呈现为类似室内乐的亲密对话。编曲中融入即兴元素，旋律在行进中逐渐碎片化并停滞，挖掘传统曲调中隐藏的深层意蕴与暗色潜流。Kvifte的横笛、萨克斯与风笛与Edén的小提琴、Nesheim的打击乐形成织体丰富的声场，既有北欧民间传统的神话色彩（fossgrimen水妖传说），又具学院派即兴与当代室内乐的实验气质。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single “A história de nossa língua” features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including “Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapuã, Ipanema, Maracanã, Capoeira, etc.” This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer’s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track “Ver meu povo se abraçar” to the convincing reggae of the second single, “Que seja um reggae”. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, “Independência” features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings “Battre des ailes” accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on “Dans le sud feat”. The gentle “Strati di tempo” is the closest to Santtana’s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political. For example, on “Línguas Gerais,” French rapper Oxmo Puccino “speaks about colonization.” Continuing to quote from the liner notes, “Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.” Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing “Cocanha” in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out. Like his popular previous recording O Paraíso (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Paraíso , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. Find the artist online.
items._cn_summary: 巴西音乐人Lucas Santtana的专辑《Brasiliano》以多语言歌词为线索，葡萄牙语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及图皮-瓜拉尼语交织呈现，围绕巴西葡萄牙语的语言文化史展开。制作上以层次丰富的人声与原声乐器（钢琴、小提琴、中提琴、吉他、鼓）为基底，辅以合成器与mellotron，带来温暖的当代质感。专辑风格跨越巴西传统、雷鬼、法式香颂、意大利民谣等，与多国音乐人合作，体现了跨文化融合的开放姿态。Gilberto Gil的参与为专辑注入政治与历史维度，涉及殖民、语言权利等议题。整体定位为具有学术深度与政治自觉的当代世界音乐，编曲精致且具可听性，但在实验性与前卫性方面相对克制，更偏向成熟的跨界融合路线。

items.body: Dani Jané Vida Segell Microscopi Review by Michael Stone V ida , the third release by Dani Jané (Spanish guitar, loops, synthesizer, composition), is a lyrical, rhythmically driven title that combines elements of flamenco, Catalan folk, classical music, jazz, and Catalan and U.S. poetry. A graduate of the Conservatori Superior de Música del Liceu (Barcelona), Jané pursued further study (classical, flamenco, jazz, tango) elsewhere in Spain, and in Germany, France, Italy, and India. Among others, Jané has worked with the flamenco fusion ensemble Tío Montero, flautist Neus Plana Turu, and singers Manuel Araya, Marta Casals, Rusó Sala, and Giulietta Vidal. Marcel Torres (second guitar, effects), Pablo Giménez (transverse flute or side-blown flute, Andean panpipe, percussion), and percussionist Pulmon Beatbox accompany Jané on Vida . Backing the core quartet are flamenco singer Pere Martínez, bassist Tomàs Pujol, and drummer-percussionist Martí Hosta. While studying in Berlín, Jané composed “Preludi” and “El vol de la Vida,” conceived as a classical suite of two movements; about four minutes in, the latter concludes with Martínez’s keening bulerías , with passages from Walt Whitman’s Song of Myself (sung in Spanish-language translation). “Clara” sets up a subtle interplay between Jané’s guitar and Gimenez on flute, over a subdued but insistent bass and percussion foundation. Jané’s grandfather Miquel Castanys wrote the lyrics to “Les penes de l’amor” (the pain of love) in 1938, adapted to a rumba Jané composed during his Berlin sojourn, in tribute to a forebearer Jané knows only through family stories, photos, and his grandfather’s verses. “Lau” presents another guitar-flute encounter accented by understated effects and percussion. Jané composed the instrumental “Milonga C.F. 2.0” with reference to his parents’ home, C.F., i.e., Can Finestres, in the province of Girona, where he spent his early years and first studied with a local guitarist. “Lydda,” a tanguillos by Barcelona’s Toti Soler (whom Jané cites as a major influence), wraps the album, wherein guitar and flute trade licks accented with Carnatic-like vocal percussion. Vida gives voice to a new generation of conservatory trained Catalan artists for whom flamenco is but one among myriad influences. Find the artist online.
items._cn_summary: 丹尼尔·哈内第三张专辑《Vida》以抒情性与节奏性为底色，将弗拉门戈、加泰罗尼亚民谣、古典音乐、爵士及探戈元素融为一体。哈内毕业于巴塞罗那 Liceu 高等音乐学院，作品融合多种文化背景，在德国柏林求学期间完成多首曲目创作。专辑中吉他与长笛、打击乐形成细腻对话，节奏型覆盖 bulerías、rumba、milonga 与 tanguillos，并融入印度卡纳提克式人声打击元素。歌词来源多元，包括惠特曼《自我之歌》西班牙语译本及哈内祖父1938年诗作。整体定位为受过音乐学院训练的新一代加泰罗尼亚艺术家的跨文化融合之作。

items.body: Stelios Petrakis Lyric Buda Musique Review by Andrew Cronshaw Photo: Claudia de Ventura Crete’s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island’s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics. Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he’s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings. True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture. “Astro Sti Gaza” (‘Star in Gaza’), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis’s laouto and lyra, Maëlle Duchemin’s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos’s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. “Nathenas,” a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou’s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle. “Anglianico,” a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efrén López and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos’s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like “Pukanè” is based. Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition “Panj Pol,” a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, “Agrilos,” by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan’s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou. “Evlerin Önü Mersin,” a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou’s zurnas. “Muixeranga,” again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024. Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of “Nothing Else Matters,” is unexpected: it’s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number. Find the artist online. Further listening: Stelios Petrakis Quartet: Spondi Queyras, Sinopoulos, Chemirani: Thrace: Sunday Morning Sessions Ettore Castagna: Eremìa
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由克里特岛里拉琴演奏家Stelios Petrakis领衔，汇集希腊、伊朗、布列塔尼、亚美尼亚、瓦伦西亚等地音乐家，展现了地中海及周边地区的跨文化音乐对话。专辑以克里特传统里拉琴与劳托琴为核心，结合波斯手鼓、布列塔尼管乐、亚美尼亚锡哨、瓦伦西亚曼陀林等多种传统乐器，在旋律与音色层次上追求丰富的抒情性。Petrakis同时也是制琴师，参与研发了带共鸣弦的改良里拉琴。作品以器乐为主，融合各地传统曲调与原创创作，节奏型态多样，包含亚细亚民谣、塔兰泰拉风格及庆典音乐元素。作为Buda Musique厂牌发行的跨地域世界音乐合辑，作品在保持各地传统底色的同时呈现出开放的音乐视野。

items.body: Darkwave duo Vox Umbra released “Afterglow,” a two-song maxi-single paired with “The Train,” on June 5, 2026 as a digital release through Bandcamp. Here’s the video for “Afterglow”. The duo says that “Afterglow” / “The Train” “is a cohesive two-song statement about how people carry each other through uncertain times.” The duo describes “Afterglow” as “a sweeping and urgent meditation on disillusionment, loyalty and perseverance in a world where direction grows uncertain,” citing the lyric “I loved you before the damage, I’ll love you through the break.” They describe “The Train” as “reflective, restrained and quietly devastating,” built around the lyric “Maybe this time I have done enough.” Afterglow by Vox Umbra About Vox Umbra Vox Umbra is a darkwave duo formed in 2025 as a transcontinental collaboration. Tiffany, based in Seattle, composes the music; Florian, based in northern France, provides vocals. The two work across the geographic distance to produce what they describe as a fusion of introspective, melancholic rhythms with dark, cinematic arrangements. The project’s first releases reached listeners through video premieres. Vox Umbra premiered the debut single “Cold Heart” as a video in October 2025, then premiered the video for “On the right” in November 2025 ahead of the duo’s debut EP, “Unchained.” The two-song maxi-single “Afterglow” / “The Train,” released June 5, 2026, follows that debut EP.
items._cn_summary: Vox Umbra 是 2025 年成立的暗黑浪潮双人组合，由西雅图的 Tiffany 负责作曲、法国北部的 Florian 负责演唱，以跨大西洋远程协作的方式创作。2026 年 6 月 5 日通过 Bandcamp 数字发行两首单曲《Afterglow》与《The Train》，延续此前首张 EP《Unchained》的方向。作品风格被乐队自述为内省、忧郁的节奏与黑暗、电影化编曲的融合，主题围绕不确定时代中人们之间的相互支撑。《Afterglow》被描述为关于幻灭、忠诚与坚持的急切冥想，《The Train》则以反思与克制为核心。该项目在暗黑浪潮谱系中定位清晰，编曲强调氛围感与情绪张力，但文章本身更接近新闻通稿，缺乏对声音设计或音乐结构的实质评析。

items.body: It’s hard enough to walk away when it’s familiar I saw the cost in your eyes of all my failures We found a bond in the beauty of a flame Stood in together but it didn’t burn the same Parasocial love is the bargain-bin séance of modern fame: strangers staring into the glass, inventing a person from fragments, then getting offended when the real one has bones, bills, bad moods, and a private life. They think they know your motives, your secrets, your breakfast, the shape of your loneliness. They imagine being you, being near you, being chosen by you, until the fantasy becomes a little apartment with no doors. The cruel joke is that all this imagined closeness creates distance. Everyone feels intimate, nobody is touched, and the room gets colder. Stare Away’s video for Familiar takes this heartache into poignant territory: telling the story of how the camera can be a trap, a lover, a heckler, and possibly a union grievance filed by your own nervous system. Directed by Brooklyn’s Gabriel Stanley, the clip takes Ben Nelson’s bright, synth-heavy ache and throws it into a room full of hands, bodies, stares, and theatrical trouble. Nelson, the New York City artist behind Stare Away, sings straight into the lens with the dazed concentration of a man trying to finish a thought while being spiritually repossessed. Around him, disembodied arms drag, clutch, adore, and interfere, the kind of devotion that looks flattering until it starts feeling like a very bad meet-and-greet. The video’s central gag, if you can call emotional suffocation a gag, is that the artist becomes the audience’s object, pulled through the machinery of attention while still expected to look good under practical lighting. Show business remains undefeated, and possibly sticky. The song itself, from the upcoming album In Absence, due July 31 via A La Carte Records, carries a dark elegance: the synths shine hard, the bass drives with purpose, and Nelson’s thundering voice tugs our heartstrings. There is a heartfelt power in the vocal and melody that recalls the Scottish band Lowlife, that same wide-open ache where post-punk grandeur meets bruised romantic confession. Familiar is about the last words that never quite arrive, and the private aftermath of a bond that once felt sacred but could no longer hold its heat. The lyrics circle the difficulty of leaving something known, even after love has become damaged by failure, silence, and uneven devotion. Images of an open-window song, a needle spinning beside an empty room, and a sanctuary turned into a house of sighs give the track its wounded center: the question of whether someone will keep dancing alone, or find another body to share the memory with. “I felt something very heavy when recording the opening riff, it had a much larger story to tell,” says Ben Nelson. “The moment I knew where the bass guitar was going to drive and where the melodies would rest, it brought a balance I needed at the time.” In the video, the forced perspective gives it a funhouse intimacy, making the viewer complicit in all the grabbing and gawking that ensues. Performers keep hauling their deepest wounds onto stages and screens, which can be cathartic in the way surgery is cathartic: messy, necessary, and best handled with decent lighting. People connect to it, truly – but parasocial devotion takes that gift and stuffs it into a souvenir cup. The artist bleeds; the crowd applauds, projects, assumes, diagnoses, and sends heart emojis like tiny invoices. Everyone claims intimacy, while genuine reciprocation stays scarce. The performer gives a diary entry, a nerve ending. Mostly, though, they receive mirrors held by strangers who love their own reflections. “One of the great things about Ben’s music and Familiar, in particular, is the driving nature of the arrangements,” says director Gabriel Stanley. “I wanted to explore a forced perspective and thought it would be really interesting to flip the idea of parasocial relationships on its head, giving the viewer a look from the eyes of the artist instead of how it’s normally portrayed…Real fans, practical lighting, and old school camera moves with modern lenses felt like a great way to set the tone for anyone hearing the song for the first time while watching this video.” By the time Nelson reaches the stage, Familiar has turned heartbreak into a public event, which is probably why pop music exists and why therapists keep calendars. items._cn_summary: Stare Away是来自纽约的艺术家Ben Nelson的暗潮/后朋克项目。专辑《In Absence》由独立厂牌A La Carte Records发行。单曲《Familiar》以合成器为主导，辅以推进感强的贝斯线和深沉的人声，整体呈现出暗黑优雅的气质，被类比于苏格兰后朋克乐队Lowlife的宽广忧伤感。歌词聚焦于熟悉却已破碎的情感羁绊，以及无法说出口的告别。MV由Gabriel Stanley执导，通过大量肢体、视线和被拉扯的意象，探讨准社会关系（parasocial relationship）中注意力机制如何将表演者变为客体。整张作品在暗潮/后朋克框架内具备一定的文学性表达，但并未展现出显著的实验性或跨界突破。

items.body: The Glorious Assembly Jazz Orchestra is the creation of Emmy Award-winning film composer David Mitcham . After a career writing music for the screen, often with jazz undertones, Mitcham has chosen to expand his ambitions by directing a full-on extended big band playing new compositions on Glorious Assembly. The 20- piece group features some of the UK's top players, with additional specialists on flute, E-flat clarinet, bass and contrabass clarinet, and tuba. The palette is further expanded by performers doubling on various ukuleles, piccolo, alto flutes and echo harmonicas (with two reeds for each set of notes giving an echo effect). The album, recorded in one day at Mark Knopfler's British Grove Studios, sets out Mitcham's stall with eight varied tracks showing a range of sound and style. His background in composing comes to the fore immediately; the tunes develop musically with momentum and grace, as if sliding down a spiraling banister with new ideas waiting on every floor. The soloists are given just enough space within each number, time to state their case with purpose and then depart as a new focus appears. Mitcham clearly has an ear for an evocative melody, as demonstrated by the opening "The Autumn of Our Days." Andy Wood 's gorgeous thematic statement on trombone leads first to a lyrical tenor solo by Mark Lockheart. The feel builds into a well-honed electric guitar solo by John Parricelli and further into Tom Rees-Roberts's full-on trumpet take. The track subsides—but whoever's autumnal days we are talking about, there is clearly life remaining. "335," named for the iconic Gibson model, opens with a riff from Parricelli (playing the selfsame guitar) alongside Loz Garrett's double bass. Gareth Williams takes a turn on piano before sax-swapping and fiery brass take over. Gareth Lockrane 's flute provides the icing on a particularly tasty cake. "Tom Wallager" recalls a John Steinbeck passage from his 1954 novel Sweet Thursday, where the characters decide to have "a Tom Wallager of a party"; wild carousing ensues. It is never made clear who Tom Wallager is, but he is effectively brought to life by this rapid-fire sax/brass interplay led by high E-flat clarinet lines. Phil Meadows seizes the moment on alto sax before Lockrane's flute appears to call a temporary relaxation. The pace picks up again with Claire McInerney having the last hurrah on baritone sax. Every track has treasures to offer. "Gold in the Depths" opens with a wistful piano/arco bass theme with a Latin lilt before a welcome extended flute solo from Lockrane and a fluid trumpet solo from Laura Jurd. "Bop Canon" (strictly more canon than bop, it should be said) is a six-part canon driven by the energetic drums of Ian Thomas, aka 'Ianto.' There is a great deal of smart writing here, reminding me somewhat of Mike Westbrook's large-scale works in its exuberance and rich instrumentation. The group performed in concert at the album launch, and I hope more outings will be possible. The appearance of a new voice in large-group jazz is a welcome addition to 2026.
items._cn_summary: Glorious Assembly是由英国电影作曲家David Mitcham创立的20人编制大乐队首张专辑，延续了Mike Westbrook式的大型爵士乐团写作传统。乐队在传统大乐队编制基础上引入了尤克里里、高音长笛、低音单簧管、倍低音单簧管、回声音簧口琴等非常规乐器，拓展了音色空间。专辑共八首曲目，展现了作曲家的叙事性写作功底——主题发展兼具推进力与优雅，乐手独奏在结构中恰如其分地展开。音乐风格以学院派大乐队爵士为核心，融合了拉丁元素与复杂对位手法（如六声部卡农）。整体定位偏向学院派/进步爵士范畴，在编制与配器上展现了一定的探索意识，但未深入实验/即兴/电子等更前卫的领域。

items.body:
DINTE dip into a rich archival pot of 1930’s-1950’s rural Greek demotika, a style of folksong rooted in the Byzantine era and practised between Greece and its diaspora.

Timeless themes of love, death, matrimony, nature and whatever is the Greek word for “the craic”, spur the singers on board to a range of keening laments of the slower Syrtos style, and ecstatic folk dance of the Pidiktos mode, in time-honoured style across ‘Curse You, Foreign Lands’.

While those themes may only be literally understood by Greek speakers, the songs’ passionately emotive delivery transcends tongues, variously mesmerising on the swaying, forlorn romance of Georgia Vasilopoulou, and male/female vocal in the heady helix of Nikolaos Chalkias’ ‘Σταφύλι μοσχοστάφυλο’, which kinda reminds us of Thai molam, or instrumentally emoting as on two standouts by Vaios Malliaras, while saving a drum and horn-led gem for Kostas Zografos’ ‘Ανάπλι στο βουλευτικό’.
items._cn_summary: 《Curse You, Foreign Lands》是一张由DINTE厂牌策划的希腊乡村demotika民谣合辑，收录1930至1950年代间录制、根植于拜占庭时期的传统民歌，涉及希腊本土及其散居社区。专辑主题涵盖爱情、死亡、婚姻与自然，以Syrtos挽歌式吟唱和Pidiktos欢快民间舞曲两种形式呈现。乐评特别提及Georgia Vasilopoulou的摇摆式悲情浪漫、Nikolaos Chalkias作品与泰国molam的听觉关联，以及Vaios Malliaras的器乐段落和Kostas Zografos的鼓与号角主导曲目。作为档案性质的乡村民谣汇编，该合辑在文化地域性上具有特色，与世界音乐偏好相吻合，但在实验性、跨类型融合方面较为有限，整体定位偏向传统民间音乐的整理与再发现。

items.body:
Good Morning Tapes back with a new album of lushest New Age sound-bathing x emotionally gooey trip hop from Andro Gogibedashvili aka Saphileaum, delivered in a mode that’s highly tipped for anyone on the line from Enigma to All Saints, from a.s.o to Boards of Canada.

Saphileaum has spent the past decade in passage between notable houses of atmospheric sorcery - Mule Musiq, Not Not Fun, Slow Life, Constellation Tatsu - and of course Good Morning Tapes, who now host their 3rd meeting, ‘Heavenly Hills’. A definitive chapter in his ten year saga, it is flush with symphonic strings and sky born keys, breezily urged by percussion that straddles chill out and folk zones. That said there’s also a Balearic - or should that be Black Sea? - appeal to its title tune, that lingers in the glistening wake of ‘Your Grace’, to the shimmering breaks of a parting piece ‘Alarko (Cosmic Eagle)’, falling into the space between Boards of Canada's cult-inspired hauntological nostalgia and Shackleton's hallowed ethno-dub.

“The tracks in the album were written with the inspiration of the kingdom of Shambhala in the Himalayas. I'm deeply fascinated and touched by it. Even the album title, holds the idea of its Heavenly nature and the tracks are like individual, elemental parts of it. The album is not a journey into Shambhala, but rather a play and a dance with its energy, image and presence in my world. Alarko (Cosmic Eagle) is dedicated to my grandfather, Temur Tsiklauri, and I dedicate the whole album to my country Georgia, which I deeply love.”
items._cn_summary: 来自格鲁吉亚的制作人Saphileaum推出新专辑《Heavenly Hills》，以New Age氛围浸泡与trip hop律动为核心框架，融合弦乐铺陈、民谣打击乐、巴利阿里律动及民族dub质感，在Boards of Canada式的怀旧电子与Shackleton的实验dub之间游走。专辑以喜马拉雅香巴拉王国为创作灵感，末曲致敬其格鲁吉亚祖父，整张作品亦是献给他深爱的祖国。Good Morning Tapes这一独立小厂牌延续了其在氛围电子领域的美学追求，结合格鲁吉亚的地域文化视角，使作品在世界音乐与电子声响的交汇处展现出独特的文化底蕴与细腻质感。

items.body:
Shinichi Atobe fiends will be in their element with Yuji Takenouchi aka Mr. YT’s iridescent techno-house perlers, his first new material in years and the latest in Short Span’s stream of chef’s kiss goodies.

With ‘Universo’ Short Span look beyond contemporary circles to a cult Japanese artist renowned for a string of EPs in the late ‘90s, and Ron Trent co-productions in the mid ’10s, and only scarcely heard since then on his label Element of Souls. The four-tracker effectively picks up where he left the dance years ago, ushering bodies to effortless flight in a mode that reminds of Shiichi Atobe via Shed and Microworld style Detroit elegance in ‘Acuario’, flexing his fruitiest jazz-fusion-house chops on the whirring swang of ‘Escorpio’. He simmers it down to a breezier flow led by puckered, G-funky trills on ‘Tauro’, and smartly defers gratification on ‘Piscis’, blooming lushest harmonic pads that eventually sync with syrupy deep house grooves for graceful end-of-night business.
items._cn_summary: 日本地下电子音乐人Mr. YT（Yuji Takenouchi）暌违多年后在独立厂牌Short Span发表的四曲EP。作品横跨深沉浩室、底特律 techno与爵士融合浩室，融合了Shed式的律动骨架与Microworld式的优雅质感，'Acuario'呈现细腻的techno-house线条，'Escorpio'展现果味浓郁的爵士融合浩室律动，'Piscis'则以绵密的和声铺垫收束。作为九十年代日本地下电子场景的代表人物，作品延续了与Ron Trent合作时期的深邃美学，风格精致而不流于套路。

items.body:
Toronto-based brothers Kevin and Patrick Cahill return to Death Is Not The End with another set of introspective folk-inspired instrumentals.

They might play nylon strung guitar and make what's in all respects "folk" music, but East of the Valley Blues don't draw from the expected sources, balancing out their interest in Americana with an understanding of music from across the world that genuinely widens their perspective. So their percussive opener 'Sitting in the Poem' can swerve utterly fluidly from serpentine Tuareg-inspired riffage to Fahey-esque fingerstyle and you barely notice it. And 'The Spider Underneath' can sound utterly outside the timeline, playing like an extended post-rock jam recorded in a basement in North Africa.

Taking one side of the stereo spectrum each, the brothers play off each other perfectly, leaving us to fill in the gaps. And they peak on the brilliant 'Like Fitzcarraldo', seemingly blending South American styles and plodding rock - no need to tug a steamboat over a mountain though, right? Or play Enrico Caruso in the Amazon.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以尼龙弦吉他为主轴的器乐民谣专辑，由多伦多的Cahill兄弟二人组创作。两人各占据一个声道声场，形成对话式的呼应结构。专辑的核心特色在于跨文化融合：图阿雷格风格的沙漠布鲁斯、北非后摇滚式即兴、南美节奏律动与Fahey式指弹技巧被自然地编织在一起，模糊了地域音乐的边界。整体氛围内省而开阔，具有一定的实验探索意识，但本质上仍以原声民谣为基底，在声音设计和结构突破上偏向保守。发行厂牌Death Is Not The End为独立小众厂牌，Boomkat的乐评也具备一定深度。适合喜欢世界音乐融合与原声实验的听众。

items.body:
Tokyo-based artist Ayami Suzuki remembers her father on 'Remnants', considering the traces that loved ones leave when they die by blurring her musical elements into indistinct but emotional clouds of ambient sound. RIYL William Basinski, Celer or Lawrence English.

Who said mourning needed to be solemn? 'Remnants' is an album about grief, in a way, but it's also about presence itself - the pieces of a person that are left after they're gone. Interpreting that in sound isn't easy, so Suzuki stays relatively abstract, hiding her intentions behind droning, harmonic clouds, melancholy breaths that sound as if they're trapped behind layers of noise. It's nothing particularly novel, but it's affecting all the same, especially if you listen while studying the cover.
items._cn_summary: 东京艺术家铃木亚弥以《Remnants》追忆亡父，以氛围声响探讨亲人离世后残留的痕迹。音乐呈现出绵延的和声云团与低沉的嗡鸣，旋律模糊却充满情感张力，呼吸般的声响隐于噪音层之后。整体风格属于氛围/实验音乐领域，与William Basinski、Celer、Lawrence English等人的作品有相近气质。专辑以抽象手法处理哀悼主题，概念完整，但在声响设计层面缺乏显著的新颖性，评论也坦承其手法并非突破性创作。适合偏爱drone氛围与情感化实验声响的听众聆听。

items.body: Tariq Goddard dodges the punches and negotiates with arthritis in order to bear witness to one for the ages I remember the shock at discovering that Marlene Dietrich was still alive in 1992. She lived long enough to have raised a glass with Brecht and listened to all but one of Kraftwerk’s albums; and if she hadn't been careful, ample time to take in Klaus Kinski and The Scorpions as well. I feel something of the same era-straddling incongruity watching Kraftwerk play live in 2026 in Bournemouth,... The post Europe Eternal: Kraftwerk in Bournemouth appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文是The Quietus发表的关于电子音乐先驱Kraftwerk 2026年伯恩茅斯现场演出的乐评。作者Tariq Goddard以独特的文学笔法切入，将演出置于跨越时代的文化语境中，引用Marlene Dietrich、Brecht、Kinski等文化符号，探讨创新者与时代之间的张力。Kraftwerk作为电子音乐的开创性力量，与用户对电子、IDM、Ambient等领域的关注高度契合，其音乐史地位毋庸置疑。然而，从现有文本来看，文章更偏向文化随笔式的感悟与回忆，实际涉及音乐本身的声音、编曲、舞台呈现等具体分析极为有限，信息密度不足以构成深度乐评。文章虽出自独立音乐媒体The Quietus，具有一定的独立视角，但内容偏短、实质性音乐讨论不足，限制了其参考价值。

items.body: A 2022 record-digging trip through Bogotá gave Venezuelan-born guitarist Manuel Rivas the grounding for Niña Volcán. He spent time inside the city’s cumbia scene, working through its history from the coastal originals to the experimental wave that Meridian Brothers, Frente Cumbiero and Romperayo had been driving out of Bogotá for two decades. Back in Toronto, he put the band together with saxophonist Adlar Gross and bassist Pāvils Hawkins, and when it came to recording their Ontario Arts Council-funded debut, Macondo, he went straight back to that scene for the key personnel: Pedro Ojeda, the Bogotá percussionist at the centre of Romperayo and Frente Cumbiero, on drums, and Eblis Álvarez of Meridian Brothers on the mix. “Cumbia del Destello”, the second track on the album named after García Márquez’s fictional Colombian town, has trumpeter Morgan Gardner alongside Gross in the horn section, the horns trading lines over that locked 4/4 cumbia groove. Ojeda drives the rhythm while Álvarez shapes the sound at the desk. Recorded at Half Moon Audio in Toronto, and mastered by Noah Mintz, the album came out in November 2025. items._cn_summary: Niña Volcán是一支由委内瑞拉裔吉他手Manuel Rivas在多伦多组建的乐队，首张专辑《Macondo》以哥伦比亚文学为概念基底，融合了哥伦比亚昆比亚音乐传统与实验性元素。乐队邀请了波哥大实验昆比亚场景中的核心人物参与录制与混音，包括Romperayo和Frente Cumbiero的打击乐手Pedro Ojeda以及Meridian Brothers的Eblis Álvarez。音乐风格属于拉美世界音乐范畴，植根于沿海昆比亚传统，同时吸收了二十年来波哥大实验浪潮的养分。作品呈现典型的4/4昆比亚律动，配以铜管乐段的交织，整体定位介于传统世界音乐与实验性跨界融合之间。文章本身偏向新闻稿性质，对音乐本身的深度评论较为有限。

items.body: Review by ProgfanJP — Formed in 2023 around guitarist Fernando de la Figuera, who cites King Crimson and Robert Fripp as his primary influences, the band came together when drummer Fran Gazol and bassist Mart�n Gros joined the fold. Their debut album arrives in 2025 through Spanish label Astronomy Recording Music, released on CD.The band's sound takes King Crimson's 1980s-2000s era as its foundation and channels it into math rock territory reminiscent of Polyphia and Animals as Leaders. Central to it all is de la Figuera's technically commanding guitar work, with high-speed arpeggios and cross-picking that carry the direct stamp of Robert Fripp, while a muscular bass and explosively dynamic drumming respond in kind. The balance between advanced technique and precisely composed, note-perfect arrangements is pulled off with a naturalness that's hard to fake.The rhythmic structures are complex throughout, but the album leans into four-beat grooves often enough that the bright, major-key melodies get room to breathe, pushing the overall feel closer to the punch of emo and melodic hardcore than to King Crimson's heavier, more aggressive side.Standout moments include "Radical", which the band themselves call their calling card, built on ostinato guitar figures reminiscent of "Fracture" and restless rhythmic shifts that generate a peculiar sense of weightlessness. "Planet 503" heads in a more symphonic direction, with synth pedal textures and lyrical melodies that lift the whole thing into proper progressive rock territory.More than just homage, this is an ambitious debut that announces a genuinely distinctive voice in the genre.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙乐团Le Tour de Force的首张专辑，由吉他手Fernando de la Figuera领衔，2025年通过独立厂牌Astronomy Recording Music发行。音乐以King Crimson八九十年代风格为根基，融入数学摇滚（Polyphia、Animals as Leaders影响）和情绪硬核元素。de la Figuera的吉他技术精湛，高速琶音与交叉弹奏带有明显的Fripp印记，贝斯与鼓以爆发力回应。复杂节奏结构常以四拍律动承载明亮大调旋律，兼顾技术性与可听性。《Radical》以ostinato动机和不稳定节奏切换营造失重感，《Planet 503》走向更交响化的方向。作为西班牙独立厂牌发行的前卫摇滚新作，展现出超越单纯致敬的独立声音。

items.body: The history of America is haunted by ghosts of the past. These ghosts transform our present-day landscape, our everyday lives, and inform the very core of our existence. On Alive With Ghosts Today (Edition Records, 2026), saxophonist Chris Potter steps away from the normal high-adrenaline jazz that has signified his recent outings and has instead put together a band designed to feel more like a small-town ensemble, a mixture of jazz and folk, to lead through a suite of tunes that examines the legacy of abolitionist John Brown and his raid on Harpers Ferry in 1859 and begs to ask the question: what have we learned, what can we learn, why are we still, wrestling with these same ghosts from the past? The ensemble Potter has assembled is the key to the album's success. Bill Frisell plays with a spacious grace that wonderfully supports all the musicians. Frisell blends in seamlessly, sliding between the other instruments and adding his own unique voice to the music; his guitar serves as the counterpoint to Potter's lead lines. It is hard to believe that although drummer Nate Smith has played with Potter for many years, this is the first time he has worked with Frisell, they are intuitively locked in as if they had been playing together for years. Bassist Burniss Travis brings a loose, funky "groove" to the proceedings, providing a fluid anchor alongside Smith to form a formidable rhythm section. Potter's playing throughout is profound; he is not just playing; he is issuing a warning that the same discontent that fueled the fire that led to Brown's failed raid to free the enslaved people at Harper's Ferry is still smoldering beneath the surface of society today. On "Osawatomie Brown," the addition of Sara Caswell on violin, Rane Moore on clarinet and Zekkereya El-magharbel on trombone transforms the band from a traditional jazz quartet into something much more strongly suited to the historical weight of the song, adding a sense of tension to the music, almost as if they were a Greek chorus, answering Potter's playing, commenting on it. They bring a mournful, melancholic sound to the song, haunting and passing judgment on the unfolding events of the unsuccessful raid, as Brown now must face the consequences of leading the failed rebellion. Brown's final words before his execution serve as a grim warning that is as true today as it was then. "I, John Brown, am now quite certain that the crimes of this guilty land will never be purged away but with blood." In fact, Potter's suite does not so much as play out as a tribute to Brown, but serves as a haunting reminder that these ghosts are still very alive and relevant today. Potter's weary tone throughout the album points to his disbelief that 167 years after Brown's failed raid on Harpers Ferry, we are still caught up in an endless cycle of conflict, doomed to repeat the failures of the past until we rectify the present. Alive With Ghosts Today is not an easy listen, not because it is not a good album; in fact, it is a triumph of artistic vision, but because it demands the listener to do more than "listen." It is a thought-provoking statement from one of the great artists of today, passing judgment on society through the lens of examining the past and demanding that we act to finally put those ghosts to rest so that we can positively impact the society of both today and tomorrow.
items._cn_summary: 克里斯·波特与比尔·弗里塞尔、奈特·史密斯等音乐家合作的爵士套曲，以1859年约翰·布朗袭击哈普斯渡口的历史事件为核心概念，将爵士四重奏与民间音乐及室内乐元素融合，引入小提琴、单簧管和长号拓展乐队编制与历史叙事重量。音乐风格跨越学院派爵士、即兴演奏与民谣融合领域，弗里塞尔的吉他与波特的中音萨克斯形成对位张力。整体呈现出概念驱动的严肃爵士美学，强调历史反思与社会批判的叙事深度，而非纯粹的形式实验。Edition Records为英国独立厂牌，作品定位介于传统后波普爵士与跨界融合之间，偏向具有思想厚度的音乐表达。

items.body: Feebles, Fables and Ferns captures a rare duo session between guitarist Mick Goodrick and pianist Fred Hersch. Recorded in August 1988 at Hersch's studio in New York, the album provides an intimate display of the superbly matched improvisational skills of two musicians in full flight. During his career, Goodrick perfected the art of avoiding the spotlight, even when collaborating with artists such as John Surman, Charlie Haden and Gary Burton. He was not prolific as a composer or recording artist, preferring to work behind the scenes, often in educational roles. Yet his innovative approach to improvisation proved influential, with many prominent musicians, among them Julian Lage and Pat Metheny, acknowledging his impact. For over three decades, Hersch's work as a pianist, composer and collaborator has resulted in over 60 albums, either as a leader or co-leader, along with multiple Grammy nominations and a host of awards. He is internationally recognized as one of jazz's most distinctive voices. The album opens with the title track. This was composed by Goodrick and was originally recorded on his debut album In Passing (ECM, 1979). The guitar opens the track, Hersch joins, and soon the instruments are intertwined, spinning and folding solo lines around, each leaving spaces for the other to explore as they move through an array of moods. Hersch's composition "Heartsong" is the central track. The piece has previously been featured in trio format on his 1990 album Heartsongs (Sunnyside) and on his 2001 solo album Songs Without Words (Nonesuch Records). In the duo's hands, the piece becomes a harmonic delight, the instruments exchanging the melody to captivating effect. The whole album is an exercise in listening and responding. This reaches its height on the spontaneous improvisations of "Five Excursions." As Hersch notes, "The highlight to me is just the level of ensemble playing. There was a lot of profound listening going on between the both of us." Alongside the originals are four covers. "Falling Grace" and "Amazing" are both Steve Swallow compositions, with the latter leading in with Goodrick's "Away 10." Its beautiful unfolding melody and improvised passages form another highlight. Johnny Green and Edward Heyman's "Out Of Nowhere" sees melodic fragments eventually merge and Goodrick's solo shimmers through Mal Waldron's "Soul Eyes." These two musicians are so well matched that they conjure something close to magic in this intimate studio session. They interweave their lines, expanding and contracting to build delicate miniatures, tender melodic exchanges and romantic drifts. But there is energy here too, making this pure musical communication of the highest order.
items._cn_summary: 这张1988年录制的专辑呈现了吉他手Mick Goodrick与钢琴家Fred Hersch的爵士二重奏对话，属于较为传统的原声爵士即兴范畴。整张专辑以原声吉他和钢琴为核心，强调两人之间的倾听与呼应，通过旋律片段的交换、线条的交织来构建细腻的迷你音画。曲目包含原创作品与Steve Swallow、Mal Waldron等作曲家的翻唱，风格偏向内省与抒情，带有后波普的优雅气质。即兴成分贯穿全片，但整体手法偏向保守与精致，未涉及先锋爵士的自由解构或电子声响的实验处理。录音在小型工作室完成，氛围亲密。对偏爱学院派即兴与自由爵士的听众而言，其中蕴含的深度互动与现场即兴逻辑具有参考价值，但缺乏突破性的声音探索或跨类型融合。

items.body:
Crackshot rap x club hybridiser Andrea Corradi splices dozens female spitters and mutant beats on ‘Outtakes’, the 2nd of his tapes for Reel Torque - Big RIYL DJ Screw, Rabit, Bobby Beethoven, Croww, Clams Casino, Hud Mo, Shadetek...

After his first volume sold out in a minute, Italian sound artist Andrea Corradi returns with a heat-seeking follow-up, shelling a 90 minute carousel of exclusive edits on tape, replete with a bonus 31 digital components for the DJs on an included download. It’s a rowdy cut ’n splice ram-raid that imagines; what would X rapper sound like on Y beat? The abundant results explore myriad permutations of this rudely unbalanced equation, from aggro jit paired with double speed fire, to Cerwin Vega-testing subs squashed with bitchiest bars, and genuine WTF‽ juxtapositions that go incredibly hard. 

The title ‘Outtakes’ knowingly undersells the prime material inside, which hits wider and just as rude as the ‘Ichinoya’ motherload which reached Mary Anne Hobbs’ BBC Radio 6 show and rinsed The White Hotel earlier this year. All the material lives up to expectations, firing from-the-hip mercurial fusions of underground, female rappers with leading-edge club ructions, with particular focus on mapping mutual, metric sweetspots between tunes that were never supposed to go together, but clearly work a treat. 

It’s effectively one of the canniest exercises in locating the mythical “3rd track” that we’ve heard in a hot minute, nailing the transitory pleasure of on-the-fly blends with a game sense of daring and rude empathy that rewards many happy returns in its spectrum of surprises - especially if you’ve had a keen ear on these pages over the years.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以拼贴和混剪为核心的实验电子说唱合辑，由意大利声音艺术家Andrea Corradi在独立厂牌Reel Torque下发行。作品将大量地下女性说唱艺人的人声与变异的俱乐部节拍进行随机拼接，制造出风格跨度极大的听觉碰撞。整体手法偏向DJ Screw、Rabit、Shadetek一脉的实验俱乐部美学，强调即兴式的配对逻辑与节奏上的不协调张力。编辑思路清晰，大量素材被重新组织成具有内在逻辑的混音单元，对俱乐部音乐解构与重组有较强的探索意识。但作品的说唱基底使其更贴近俱乐部/地下说唱场景，与纯粹的前卫实验、学院派即兴或当代古典语汇存在一定距离，更适合电子与IDM爱好者的口味。

items.body:
Forest Drive West speaks to a decade dominating UK floors, and beyond, with a 2nd album of squashed, locked-in D&B x beatdown permutations RIYL Logos, DB1, Carrier, Pessimist, DJs Plead & Python.

Swivelling right on the slow/fast sweetspot, Joe Baker’s cult solo project Forest Drive West deploys signature measures of metric ingenuity and ascetic soundscaping within a proper UK vein on ‘Mantis 1920’. The successor to his ‘Apparitions’ LP of 2018 for Livity Sound, eight tracks marks the distance travelled over the past decade with taut refinements of his interests in that space between D&B, techno, dubtech, all delivered with a disciplined relish for the sort of offbeat, aerodynamic rolige that’s been in constant R&D in the UK since the mid ‘90s.

 In FDW’s lab the sound’s bloodline is refreshed with twysts of prevailing dembow-dancehall patterns and subtle technical sorcery that make this batch his best yet, equally effective as DJ material and as an immersive album experience. Tilting in with echoes of Werkbund’s washed-out industrial atmospheres on ‘Latent’, the set firms up sharp slants on dembow style and pattern in the rugged tension of ‘Circuit’ that inform the rest of the set. He takes it to dankest Pessimist levels in the shark-eyed motion of ‘Bias’ and a standout ‘Uromastyx’, leading to worm-charming subbass tremors in the skeletal ‘Tensor’ and dread skulk to ‘Node’, whilst ‘Vector’ recalls Mike Parker’s recent switch to D&B hydrolicks, and ‘Plane’ tags in Berlin’s DB1 on a scuzzy halfstep hunch.
items._cn_summary: 这是英国地下电子音乐人Forest Drive West的第二张专辑，延续其对鼓打贝斯与电子舞曲之间灰色地带的探索。整张作品以节拍为核心，融合了Drum & Bass、Techno、Dubtech与Dembow/Dancehall节奏型，强调律动的变化与不规则性，而非传统舞曲的流畅感。声音设计偏向极简与工业质感，Werkband式的阴冷氛围、半拍碎步的幽暗低频、以及类似Pessimist的压迫感在多首曲目中交替出现。整体气质冷峻、克制、实验性强，适合在俱乐部深夜时段使用，也具备一定的沉浸式聆听价值。制作上展现了对节奏语言的深入理解，是一张在UK地下电子场景中具有代表性的作品。

items.body:
Much needed reissue of Stephen Hitchell’s sleepwalking dub house trips, faithfully remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion. FFO Maurizio, GAS, Shinichi Atobe.

Echospace’s Stephen Hitchell is in his element as Intrusion on two durational treks deep into the studio haze. Also found in much longer versions on original release, back in 2015, ‘A Gentle Embrace’ appears here thru13 min timeframes ideal for long blends in-the-mix, or more simply enjoyed on their own, floating and soporific terms.

The original puffs up a sublime architecture of diffused fumes and rolling, velvet-coated bass that yearns upward, outwards with a gorgeous sense of deferred gratification that he tempers to an even more light-headed feel in the B-side reduction, whisking the choral pads and chords to cirrus wisps and beatific harmony.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Echospace成员Stephen Hitchell以Intrusion名义发行的dub house作品，由Pole操刀重制。整体风格游走于dub techno与ambient的交界，以绵长的篇幅构建朦胧的声场层次：弥漫的烟雾质感、深沉的天鹅绒般低频缓缓推进，配合合唱式pad与和弦营造出漂浮、催眠式的听感。B面的缩减版更为轻盈剔透，将和声处理成高空卷云般的纤薄质感。重制版本将时长压缩至十三分钟左右，更适合DJ混音使用。这是一张典型的地下电子乐再版发行，面向小众氛围电子乐迷，与学院派爵士或世界音乐等用户偏好方向距离较远，但在ambient与experimental电子范畴内具有相当的品质与艺术定位。

items.body:
Enigmatic golden-era 4AD act Swallow reissue their first two albums from 1992 - Blow & Blowback - as an expanded double pack, 'Blown'.

"A chance for shoegaze fans to discover this forgotten gem from the 4AD catalogue, Blown is an essential but underrated body of work embracing the genre’s signature atmospheric layering of fuzzy guitar textures, accompanied by Louise Trehy’s beautiful and haunting vocals, creating hazy waves and swirls of luscious noise.

Swallow was formed by Louise Trehy and Mike Mason in London in the early 90’s, signed by Ivo Watts-Russell after receiving 4-song demo tape by post. Blow was originally released in July 1992, followed by Blowback in autumn of the same year featuring new mixes and overdubs and released as a limited CDEP that quickly fell out of print, known only to the most fervent 4AD fans. Swallow parted ways with 4AD shortly after the release of Blowback, but their brief period with the label has been outlived by this cornerstone dream-pop classic which has until now been obscured by the mists of time and memory.

With Blown, Swallow are reintroduced as an important force in the 4AD canon and the shoegaze genre, alongside their more well-known counterparts. The songs of Blown have been reconstructed from the original 24 track tape recordings and remixed. It has been freshly remastered by Anne Taegart at Dubplates and Mastering Berlin and lovingly presented in a brand-new package designed by longtime supporter Chris Bigg (v23) based on the original design by Vaughn Oliver.

Louise Trehy and Mike Mason met in early 90’s Camberwell, London. Both were deeply involved with the independent music scene of the time; Louise co-founded Setanta Records (home of The Divine Comedy, Edwyn Collins and Into Paradise with whom Mike would occasionally play), and Mike traversed between bike courier, video director, and lighting designer for Spacemen 3, Slowdive, Spiritualized, Curve and Chapterhouse. Prompted by Louise, they started writing songs together, drawing inspiration from a healthy mix of sources: CAN, noise, post-punk, and American forces of nature like Captain Beefheart and Butthole Surfers. Their first songs quickly surfaced and were recorded onto a Tascam 4-track portastudio. Louise posted the four-song demo to Ivo Watts-Russell who signed them to 4AD, sight unseen.

With the task of finishing their first record, the pair borrowed guitars from Tom Greenhalgh of the Mekons and they decamped to record at Edinburgh’s Palladium Studios and later, Blackwing in London. John Fryer was enlisted to produce (right off handling Nine Inch Nails’ 1989 record Pretty Hate Machine), utilizing Eventide Harmonizers (a Cocteau Twins staple) to provide the band’s lush, ethereal dazzle.

Blow would be released in July of 1992, and arrived in a sleeve designed by Vaughan Oliver (v23). Subsequently, they did a handful of support gigs with Bob Mould’s post-Hüsker Dü project Sugar and American shoegaze peers Medicine to promote the album across the UK. Contemporary reviews of Blow would unimaginatively make much of the 4AD and Cocteau’s connections. But with the music press’ attention later shifted to the Nirvana explosion of underground American bands, it was difficult for the album to get much attention.

Though, in the end, the band found the finished album different than they imagined it would sound. Feeling as though their initial ideas had been lost in the production, they petitioned Ivo to re-record parts of the album; he suggested they remix the tracks as they wished, instead. New mixes and overdubs resulted in dissonant and ambient versions closer to the band’s intentions, released as Blowback in the autumn of 1992. Sadly, expectations, hopes, and shifting priorities from both Ivo and the band led to Swallow’s departure from 4AD shortly after the release of Blowback.

Swallow pressed on and were invited to play a ten date UK tour with Mazzy Star. It was Mazzy Star who recommended Geoff Travis sign the band to his label Rough Trade in late 1993. Mike and Louise’s only release for the label was the 1994 Hush EP — recorded at home and more stripped back than the band’s previous releases, the release allowed the songs to stand ahead of their production for the first time. The full Hush session recordings would ultimately be released digitally in 2009."
items._cn_summary: Swallow是1990年代初签约4AD厂牌的英国二人组，此次以双碟形式再版其1992年的两张专辑《Blow》与《Blowback》。音乐风格以梦幻流行与自赏派为核心，融合噪音、后朋克元素，制作人John Fryer（曾操刀Nine Inch Nails首专）使用Eventide Harmonizer营造出层次丰富的朦胧音墙。女主唱Louise Trehy的声线空灵飘渺，与粗糙吉他质感形成对比。乐队受到Can、Captain Beefheart、Butthole Surfers等噪音与实验摇滚影响，4AD厂牌的标志性美学贯穿始终。整张作品是4AD黄金时代被忽视的佳作，对暗潮、后朋克、梦幻流行及实验声响爱好者具有参考价值。原文为再版发行介绍与历史回顾的混合文本，含有部分评论性质内容，但整体偏向推广性质，且文本在末尾被截断。

items.body:
One of dubstep’s greatest albums returns to roost on its maker’s label, some 17 years since it first dropped on Loefah’s Swamp81. Big one FFO Distance, Cyrus/Random Trio, Icicle, Raime.

To set the scene, by 2009 dubstep had arguably jumped the shark into its brostep phase, but a new influx of artists from more D&B and dub techno-related styles had begun to bring it back to fundamentals in studio science, rather than quick fix jump-up cartoonishness. After spending most of the prior decade dealing in seething neuro D&B defined by bleeding-edge sound design, Kryptic Minds’ ship-jump to the halfstep sound would bring the sound back to heel in pendulous dankness, and return it to ideals of slower D&B explored by the likes of El-B, Loefah, and Burial before them. 

KM have now largely shifted into offbeat techno mutations, with its Simon Shreeve credited as half of CUB with Karl O’Connor, and slower, atmospheric pressure as Mønic, but ‘One of Us’ remains their greatest offering to the dubstep phenomena, and one of its best in class. On a dozen taut variations within a theme, they pay keen attention to marble-sculpted subs, chiselled percussion and unyielding sci-fi atmosfear for the hardest-to-please steppas, holding to a proper thru-line of darkside pressure from front to back that certifies it as a classic in its field.
items._cn_summary: 这张2026年重制版专辑是英国制作人组合Kryptic Minds于2009年发行的dubstep代表作，堪称该类型最出色的专辑之一。他们将神经D&B的尖端声音设计技术融入halfstep节奏，以十二首紧密围绕同一主题的变奏展开，营造出大理石雕塑般的低频、冷峻的打击节奏和冷酷的科幻氛围。整张专辑从头至尾维持着深沉黑暗的压力线，被乐评视为dubstep现象中的经典之作。值得注意的是，Kryptic Minds成员后来分别转向offbeat techno和氛围音乐方向，这张作品可视为他们从俱乐部导向的电子乐通向更实验性声音设计领域的过渡桥梁，在dubstep与暗潮/暗氛围美学之间建立了紧密联系。

items.body:
Ukrainian lo-fi pop maker Regina Collage proves a natural selection to Jabu’s label with a dusty nugget backed by beautifully faithful rework from guest + A. Childs

In the glistening wake of Jabu’s jams with Teresa Winter, the Bristol staples host local transplant Regina Collage on her first solo turn, pairing purring vox and a percolating drum machine with perfect measures of guitar jangle, all smudged to hazed perfecction. The song is sure to snag fans of Teresa Winter’s wist as much as early Svitlana Nianio or Yana Pavlova, whilst the danker version from guest & Amos Childs lets it dance in its own echoic headspace with crafty, dematerialised dubbing inna classic Bristol style and fashion. 

A gem.
items._cn_summary: 乌克兰独立音乐人Regina Collage在Bristol厂牌Jabu旗下发行的单曲，定位为lo-fi pop。主打曲目以人声、鼓机与吉他质感为骨架，整体制作带有朦胧、涂抹式的低保真美学，靠近艺术流行与独立流行的交叉地带。评论将其与Teresa Winter及乌克兰前辈Svitlana Nianio、Yana Pavlova并列，暗示其延续了东欧地下流行的脉络。B面由guest与Amos Childs操刀的混音版本以Bristol式的dub手法重塑原作，加入回声空间与去物质化的处理，呈现一定的实验电子倾向。整体而言，这是一张兼具地区文化特色与轻度实验色彩的独立小厂牌作品，介于艺术流行与地下电子之间，但在声音设计的深度与冒险性上仍偏保守。

items.body:
On a rudely aerodynamic debut LP, Tectonic's franco-british hope flexes a signature balance of ruff & smooth, building on a solid reputation earned via 12”s with her label, Bait, plus Tempa and Darwin’s SPE:C

Dubstep is not necessarily an album genre: beyond scant examples from the likes of Burial, Shackleton, or 2562, 12”s and DJ sets serve the sound in best context. However, Beatrice M.’s grasp of subtle sensuality and propulsive traction patently ends itself well to the format on ’Sinking’, with nearly an hour of rolling, stepping and skanking permutations that deftly dance in the space between dubstep, proper, and its close-related cousins - UKG, broken beat, dub techno - with a finely measured proprioception of space, weight and pressure. 

Along with 2562’s recently dispensed ‘Lost Dubs 2006-09’, Beatrice M.’s album is arguably the best thing on Tectonic in recent memory, with a sound that revels in more ambiguous club suss. It’s the type of album primed for cans/buds as much as big cones, proving she’s equally adept at sublime tension, as in the languid ‘Ever’ and weightless love note ‘Dear Dubstep’, as propelling a dance in the Martyn-esque wriggler ‘Motion’, and offbeat hood of ‘Disco Corner’, and thru the 2562-like fluid hydrodynamics of ‘Juice,’ to the R&B-slicked ‘In Touch’, or broken beat friction of ‘Here.’
items._cn_summary: Beatrice M. 是一位法英双国籍电子音乐制作人，首张专辑《Sinking》由Tectonic厂牌发行。整张专辑时长近一小时，融合了dubstep、UKG、broken beat、dub techno及R&B等多种元素，体现出制作人在节奏编排与声音空间感方面的成熟掌控力。作品同时面向俱乐部舞池与耳机聆听两个场景，既有《Motion》《Disco Corner》这类律动驱动的舞曲，也有《Ever》《Dear Dubstep》这类氛围化、注重张力铺陈的曲目。评论将其与2562等实验性低音制作人并置，认为这是Tectonic近年来最为出色的长篇发行之一，展现出制作人在沉重低频与细腻感性之间游走的平衡能力。

items.body:
NDW stalwarts of Ata Tak & Pyrolator vintage reflect on Düsseldorf’s post-Kraut styles with a fine grasp of slippery chill-out sleaze and pungent downbeat waft.

 

"Marking its 25th anniversary, A Certain Frank's 'Nothing' stands as a quietly distinctive chapter in Düsseldorf’s post-Kraut electronic lineage – understated, atmospheric, and strikingly timeless. With this anniversary edition, Bureau B once again highlights a strand of German electronic music that exists between eras and categories. Carefully remastered and now pressed on vinyl for the first time, Nothing returns not as a relic, but as a work whose understated clarity continues to resonate – a testament to Bureau B’s ongoing dedication to preserving and recontextualising Germany’s experimental pop heritage."
items._cn_summary: A Certain Frank的《Nothing》是一张2025年发行的25周年纪念再版专辑，厂牌为德国独立电子厂牌Bureau B。音乐根植于杜塞尔多夫后Krautrock电子脉络，融合新德意志浪潮的冷峻气质与downbeat、chill-out的松弛氛围，呈现低调、氛围化的电子声响。再版经过重新母带处理并首次以黑胶形式发行，定位于实验电子与氛围音乐的交叉地带。整体风格内敛而具有时间感，承接德国电子音乐从Kraftwerk到当代地下场景的传统，但对前卫实验与即兴元素的探索较为有限，更偏向氛围电子与downbeat的审美范畴。

items.body:
Beautiful, mystic trodders by Lee “Scratch” Perry for Cedric Myton, Congo Ashanti & Watty Burnett’s harmonious reggae vocal trio The Congos, including the wee radge packet’s Black Ark mixes.

All deriving from sessions for The Congo’s legendary debut ‘Heart of The Congos’ (1977), as issued on Perry’s Black Ark Studio-related label, Black Art, ‘Ark Of The Covenant’ best portrays the producer’s genius for innovative vocal and instrumental production that captures his performers’ spirits like few others. 

The A-side is a slice of roots heaven, framing The Congos’ swaying, layered harmonies in heat-melted chords and swollen bass, sealed within the Black Ark’s soft wooden resonance, while the original 7” B-side ‘Noah Sugar Pan’ swipes the vox into ether, revealing Perry’s treacly bass underfoot and his lysergic guitar finesse under the hood. 

Perhaps the biggest attraction, however, is Lee Perry’s Original Black Ark Mix, utterly haunted with duppied vocal refractions and phantasmic details in the air that really tickle susceptible souls and soles of feet.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Congos与传奇制作人Lee "Scratch" Perry在Black Ark录音棚合作的作品，源自1977年经典首专的录音档案。音乐本质为牙买加根源雷鬼，以三重唱的和声为核心，辅以深沉的低音线和律动节奏。制作层面展现了Perry标志性的实验性手法，包括迷幻吉他纹理、人声回响折射、幻象般的空间细节处理，模糊了根源雷鬼与前卫声响探索的边界。Black Art厂牌保持独立地下属性。从用户口味来看，此作归属世界音乐范畴，其制作手法的实验性与前卫性也与用户偏好有一定交集，但整体仍植根于传统雷鬼框架，与电子、暗潮、当代古典等核心偏好领域距离较远。

items.body:
Tapes touches bass(bins) with OG patrons Jahtari on a bevy of digi-dancehall party starters.

Big fun, this one! Back in his dub lane after the fruity flex of ‘Funk Plates Vol. 1’ (2023) for Disrupt’s adorable label, Jackson Bailey aka Tapes taps right into the label’s dub and chip tune tastes with a mix of full fat originals and 8-bit versions bound to put a big daft grin on red-eyed mugs. 

Stepping up nimbly strongback with dancehall croaker ‘Photos of my Frog’, riddled with sampled snippets of said snaps, she appears to weave in waviest traces of South African bubblegum top lines in the gummier bubble of ‘Cleat Skank’, replete with a saturated, bit-crushed version on the skweee tip.

Dung below he toes a darker dancehall line laden with killer snares, Gregorian ribbet and mystic melodies in ‘Ramp Up’ and the irresistible UK steppers momentum of a ‘Back Cramp’ licked up with frothiest choral vamps, whistles, and amphibian motifs that come squashed like King Tubby fucking with the OG Prince of Persia OST.
items._cn_summary: Tapes 回归 Jahtari 厂牌，发布了一张融合数字dancehall、dub与8-bit芯片音乐概念的EP。作品在传统牙买加dancehall节奏基础上叠加bit-crushed音效与chiptune元素，部分曲目融入南非bubblegum旋律线，整体走向偏向派对化、轻快有趣而非深沉实验。King Tubby式dub处理与Prince of Persia游戏原声碎片的并置赋予作品一定的怀旧趣味和跨媒介拼贴感。跨类型融合（dancehall+chiptune+dub+南非流行）是其主要亮点，但作品整体情绪明亮、强调舞池功能性，与深度实验/前卫路线存在一定距离，更接近电子音乐与世界音乐交界处的趣味性小品。Jahtari作为专注digital dub的地下厂牌保证了发行的独立性与小众定位。

items.body: Neba Solo and Benego Diakité A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking Nonesuch Review by Mike Adcock Photo: Aboubacar Traoré A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakité The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakité is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakité, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Haïdara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Touré and Toumani Diabaté to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakité also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakité The opening track, “Djinê Mogo Tiki” begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakité introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. “Djinê Mogo Tiki” is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakité The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakité, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. “Yeredon Bali” begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakité's n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakité. They are referred to as the “Garden Demos” since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djinê Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking . Find the artist online.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由马里音乐家Neba Solo与Benego Diakité合作完成，核心乐器为巴拉风琴与恩戈尼，均为马里传统乐器。专辑以双CD形式发行，前半部分在2013年原始二重奏录音基础上，加入弦乐、键盘、吉他、打击乐及人声合奏进行重新编排，后半部分保留原始未修饰的录音。制作人Nick Gold曾促成Ali Farka Touré与Toumani Diabaté的经典合作。整体风格植根于曼丁哥音乐传统，演唱采用典型的呼应式结构，编曲在传统基底上进行了现代化的层次丰富处理，但实验性与先锋性较为有限。专辑由Nonesuch厂牌发行，该厂牌隶属华纳音乐集团。

items.body: Canzionerere Grecanico Salentino Il Mito Ponderosa Music Review by Chris Nickson How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that’s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It’s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now. The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they’ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They’ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his Taranta project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the “Taranta” track with him is included. In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history. Il Mito (The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There’s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here. The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS’s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on “Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.” Yet this isn’t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It’s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound. This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that’s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question: Where will all this be in another 50 years? Find the artists online.
items._cn_summary: 意大利南部萨伦托地区的皮兹卡传统音乐，由Canzionerere Grecanico Salentino乐团为庆祝成立50周年而作。音乐以手提琴、框鼓与人声为核心载体，在保留皮兹卡地域传统的同时引入合成器贝斯等少量电子声响元素，并由乐团两代人共同演绎，呈现出传承与革新的交织。专辑收录与钢琴家Ludovico Einaudi合作的塔兰泰拉曲目混音版，触及传统音乐与现代古典的跨界对话。整体定位为根植于南意大利希腊-萨伦托文化、面向世界音乐舞台的作品，节奏具有强烈的舞蹈驱动力，编曲在原真性与当代感之间寻求平衡，音响风格以原声为主、现代点缀为辅。

items.body: Teija Niku Tovi Artist release Review by Chris Nickson Tovi by Teija Niku It’s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she’s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That’s amply illustrated on her composition “Finsko Dajchovo,” inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or “Seitsemän,” taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. “Elokuu,” a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as “an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while”), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener “Ohto.” Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with “Poloneesi äidille,” a piece Niku composed for her mother’s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It’s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it’s not such a long gap before she’s back in the studio. Find the artist online. Further listening: Duo Ruut - Ilmateade Maria Moramarco, Fabio Mina, and Francesco Savoretti - Pietrafonie Jaune Toujours - Vertigo
items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku的第四张专辑《Tovi》，将北欧民谣与巴尔干音乐传统进行跨地域融合。专辑以芬兰民间旋律为基础，融入保加利亚民间舞曲节奏与马其顿情歌元素，在polska舞曲与巴尔干节奏之间形成对比。手风琴作为核心乐器贯穿始终，展现出清晰的旋律感和忧郁与明亮交替的情绪变化。终曲《Poloneesi äidille》是献给已故母亲的挽歌，演唱部分真挚动人。整体定位属于传统框架内的世界音乐融合，作曲精致且有个人情感深度，但在声响探索和实验性方面较为保守，更偏重民谣传统的自然延伸而非突破性创造。

items.body: Emi Makabe Echo Sunnyside Review by John Alan Urquhart Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gonçalves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell’s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, “Birthday Song” comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, “I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.” The record closes with “Overture,” anchored by Gonçalves’ dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe’s Japanese exhortation, “Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.” Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father’s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. “Snow” begins with Makabe’s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while “Text” swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe’s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe “Morisan” hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music
items._cn_summary: Emi Makabe是出生于日本、活跃于纽约的爵士歌手与器乐演奏者。《Echo》是她在独立爵士厂牌Sunnyside Records发行的第二张专辑，以父亲去世为情感主题，融合日本传统音乐与现代爵士。专辑使用三味线、横笛、日语演唱等传统元素，搭配钢琴、低音提琴、鼓等爵士编制，并邀请Bill Frisell、Jason Moran、Meshell Ndegeocello等客座乐手参与。音乐风格横跨日本传统民谣与bebop爵士，旋律抒情且具怀旧气质，强调文化传承与代际连接。整体属于世界音乐与爵士的跨界融合，制作精良但偏向抒情传统路线，缺乏显著的实验性或前卫声响探索。

items.body: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — The War of the Worlds: ULLAdubULLA ? The Remix Album is a strange but fascinating offshoot of Jeff Wayne's bombastic sci-fi epic.This remix project takes the theatrical prog-rock of the original War of the Worlds and drags it firmly onto the late-90s-00s dancefloor. Prog trance indeed with lashings of house, and techno-adjacent versions, often stripping away the narrative drama in favour of rhythm and atmosphere. But is it welcome? Admittedly I miss the original powerhouse versions, who wouldn't? So the result is uneven though never boring. Some tracks hit surprisingly hard?especially the more propulsive remixes of "The Eve of the War" and "Forever Autumn," which reimagine the original themes as club-ready melancholic anthems. But it all feels like novelty experiments and keys face it without the narrative voice they lose the tension and storytelling that made the original so distinctive and brilliant.What makes ULLAdubULLA interesting is its sheer audacity as it treats a grand, orchestral concept album as raw material for electronic reinterpretation. Definitely not essential listening in the Jeff Wayne catalogue, but it can be treated as a curious time capsule of when prog, gaming culture, and club remix culture briefly collided
