items.body: Eastside Festival will return to Karlsbad in Halle/Saale on 3 and 4 July 2026. Presented by Pluswelt Promotion, the Pop and Wave open air event brings together synthpop, EBM, dark wave, electro and alternative electronic music in a lakeside setting. Now entering its fourth edition, Eastside Festival has grown from a pandemic-era idea into an established meeting point for the electronic and wave-oriented scene. The festival takes place at Karlsbad Halle, located by the Angersdorfer Teiche, with camping options, a beach setting and a summer atmosphere closer to a scene gathering than to a standard large-scale commercial festival. Nitzer Ebb, Devision Redux and Black Nail Cabaret on Friday Nitzer Ebb (Photo by Karo Kratochwil) Friday’s programme connects several generations of electronic underground music. British EBM pioneers Nitzer Ebb remain one of the defining names of body music, known for their stripped-down force, commanding vocals and percussive physicality. Their appearance gives the first Eastside Festival day a clear historical anchor. Another major point of interest is Devision Redux, the new electronic format around Steffen Keth and Daniel Myer. The project reworks material from the De/Vision catalogue into a club-oriented language, giving familiar songs a leaner, more contemporary and more physical shape. Black Nail Cabaret bring their elegant, dark electronic pop to the line-up. The Hungarian duo have built a distinctive identity around sharp synth work, controlled sensuality and a sense of theatrical restraint. Canadian duo Traitrs add a colder post-punk and darkwave presence, with a sound shaped by guitars, tension and emotional urgency. Black Nail cabaret (Photo by Karo Kratochwil) In Strict Confidence appear with an electro set, linking the Eastside Festival to the long-running German dark electronic tradition. Future Lied To Us bring polished synthpop with a melodic, emotionally direct approach, while Spanish act Huir open the day with a newer voice from the electronic underground. The evening continues after the concerts with a DJ set by Richard Silverthorn of Mesh in a separate area. Covenant, Solitary Experiments and Bigod 20 on Saturday Covenant (Photo by Karo Kratochwil) Saturday expands the spectrum from synthpop and dark electronic music to EBM history and club culture. Covenant remain one of the most important Swedish electronic acts, combining philosophical lyrics, elegant synth architecture and a strong live presence. Their place in the programme gives the second day a major synthpop focus. Solitary Experiments bring a different kind of emotional force: melodic, powerful, direct and deeply connected to the German futurepop and electro scene. Bigod 20 provide the midnight special, adding a classic EBM and electronic heritage element to the festival’s second night. Priest contribute a darker, more stylised synth-based sound, while UK act Auger bring a more alternative, song-oriented edge to the programme. Beborn Beton add sophisticated German electronic pop with a long history in the synth scene, while Swiss act Blackbook represent a newer generation of sleek, melodic synthpop. M/A/T open the second day with harder electronic energy, and Lennart Salomon performs a special lakeside acoustic set, creating a quieter contrast before the programme returns to full electronic intensity. The night continues with a DJ set by Talla 2XLC and an after-show party in a separate area. A lakeside festival for the pop, wave and EBM audience The full 2026 line-up includes Nitzer Ebb, Covenant, Devision Redux, Bigod 20, Solitary Experiments, In Strict Confidence, Priest, Traitrs, Auger, Black Nail Cabaret, Lennart Salomon, Beborn Beton, Blackbook, Future Lied To Us, Huir and M/A/T. Christian Schottstädt of Forced To Mode will host the festival as moderator. The location gives Eastside Festival its particular identity. Karlsbad offers an open air setting by the lake, with a sandy beach, camping possibilities and a relaxed summer atmosphere. For an audience often associated with clubs, dark venues and late-night dancefloors, this combination of electronic music and open air surroundings gives the festival a distinct rhythm. Eastside Festival 2026 does not present itself as a purely nostalgic event. The programme places established names next to newer and mid-generation acts, connecting different branches of the electronic underground: EBM history, synthpop melancholy, contemporary darkwave, alternative pop structures and club-oriented electronics. Tickets are available through the official Eastside Festival website, Pluswelt Promotion ticketing and Eventim. items.body: UK dark alternative artist j:dead released the single “Keep Walking” on June 5, 2026, via Infacted Recordings. The track is the seventh single in a year-long monthly release series and is available to stream and download. “Keep Walking” continues a release campaign that j:dead launched in December 2025. Side-Line reported on the start of the run when the project launched the year-long single series with ‘Pressure’ in December 2025, and again in January 2026 when j:dead announced ‘Who Knows’ as the third single in the series. In March 2026, j:dead premiered the ‘Feeling Alone’ video on Side-Line one day ahead of its release. These are the 2026 singles released so far: “Disgusting,” “Who Knows,” “Feeling Alone,” “Silence Calls,” “Over The Years” and “Keep Walking,” following “Pressure” in December 2025. “Keep Walking” was inspired by the act of literally walking through trauma. It was written, performed and recorded by j:dead (Jay Taylor). Guitars were played by Hilger Tintel. The track was produced by Motel-Music and mastered by Studio-600. About j:dead j:dead is the project of UK artist Jay Taylor. He produces a mix of industrial, gothic, electronic and modern-metal. The project started with the single “Haunt” (2019), followed by “Feeding On Me” (2020) and the album “A Complicated Genocide” (2021). Subsequent releases include the singles “Tearing Me Apart” (with Teknovore) and “I’ll Wait” (both 2021); “DAS OM3N” (a cover), the EP “Vision Of Time,” and the single “Hold Tight” (all 2022); and the collaborations “High Time (Chinese Takeaway)” with FabrikC and “Thrive” with Nature Of Wires (both 2022). Side-Line covered the EP “Vision Of Time” on its 2022 release via Infacted Recordings. In 2023 j:dead issued “Surrendering,” a cover of “You Spin Me Round (Like a Record)” with Menschdefekt, the single “Harbour,” and the EP “ROOTS,” followed by “What We’ll Be” (2024) and “Pressure” (2025). The latter opened a year-long campaign of monthly singles continued in 2026 by “Disgusting,” “Who Knows,” “Feeling Alone,” “Silence Calls” and “Over The Years.” “Keep Walking,” released on June 5, 2026, is the seventh single in that series.
items._cn_summary: j:dead是英国暗潮/工业电子艺人Jay Taylor的个人项目，融合工业、哥特、电子与现代金属元素，走的是典型的暗潮工业路线。其新作"Keep Walking"延续了自2025年12月开启的每月单曲发行计划，是该系列的第七首单曲。灵感来源于穿越创伤的实际行走体验，制作团队包括吉他手Hilger Tintel、制作人Motel-Music及母带处理Studio-600，发行厂牌为德国独立暗潮厂牌Infacted Recordings。整体风格属于暗潮工业领域的常规制作，虽与用户口味方向吻合，但在声音设计或创作手法上未展现明显的实验性突破，且本文为新闻通稿性质，缺乏实质性的音乐评论内容。

items.body: Electronic musician Rodrigo Passannanti released “Timeless Conceptions” on June 5, 2026 through Cyclical Dreams. Musicaly the nine-track album offers Berlin School and space-synth material. It is available as a digital release and on CD. “Timeless Conceptions” runs to nine tracks: “Mineral Silence,” “Never Was,” “Time Watches Itself,” “Raccoglimi (feat Claudia Placanica),” “Voidstar,” “Dustborn,” “Magic Flight (ZX4827),” “Residual Existence,” and “Lucid Call.” The album was composed, produced and mastered by Rodrigo Passannanti in London, United Kingdom. Vocals on “Raccoglimi” are by Claudia Placanica (Costume) of Italy, and “Residual Existence” uses vocal samples credited to Audioslave. The label describes the record as a sequence of “long, evolving sequences, widescreen ambient chords, and rich analog textures,” with the artist working under his own name rather than his harsher Hypercube alias. “Timeless Conceptions” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp as well. A CD edition is available through Kunaki. Timeless Conceptions [CYD 0159] by Rodrigo Passannanti About Rodrigo Passannanti Rodrigo Passannanti is an electronic music producer who has been active since the early 1990s, working across a range of styles under several aliases. He has collaborated with producers including Andy Hughes (The Orb), Michael Allen (Wolfgang Press, 4AD) and Håkan Lidbo. Alongside composing music for short films and video games, he records experimental material under the name Hypercube. He is based in London, United Kingdom, and releases through the Cyclical Dreams label, whose catalogue spans vintage and contemporary ambient synth. “Timeless Conceptions”, issued June 5, 2026, is presented as a return to a classic Berlin School and space-synth approach under his own name.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑定位为柏林学派与太空合成器风格的电子作品，包含九首曲目，涵盖长篇渐变序列、宽幅环境和弦与丰富的模拟音色质感。制作人Rodrigo Passannanti自九十年代起活跃于电子音乐领域，曾与The Orb成员Andy Hughes及4AD旗下音乐人合作，并以更具工业色彩的Hypercube别名进行更激进的实验创作。此次回归本名发行，呈现的是较为经典的柏林学派太空电子路线。专辑中一首曲目邀请意大利歌手Claudia Placanica献声，另一首使用了Audioslave的人声采样，增添了一定的人声层次。整体风格偏向传统电子子类型内部的探索，与前沿实验电子及IDM方向存在一定距离。

items.body: Poeme Electronique is a British band formed in 1980, featuring the quartet Dave Hewson, Sharon Abbott, Julie Ruler, and Les Hewson. “The Echoes Fade” was originally released as a single. In 2009, a self-titled album was released, featuring many other songs from the early years. Now, many years later, comes this reissue with exactly the same number of tracks. The 16 tracks take us back in time, and in that sense, Poeme Electronique sounds truly magical: synth music from a bygone era. This is pure Electro-Wave with indescribable space-like sounds, but also Psychedelic elements. The main course remains Electro-Wave, supported by slow yet danceable rhythms and female vocals. The music is not an ode to the 80s, but simply the 80s itself, with very recognizable sounds and effects. This is vintage Electro, featuring some strong tracks as well. However, I find the eight tracks on the second vinyl somewhat weaker, sometimes even a bit bland, as if the inspiration had run out. “The Echoes Fade” seems to me primarily an album for insiders and collectors of the golden age of 80s electro. (Rating:7). Listen to “She’s An Image”: https://davehewson.bandcamp.com/track/shes-an-image
items._cn_summary: Poeme Electronique是1980年成立的英国四人乐队，《The Echoes Fade》为其早期单曲及作品的再版合集。整体风格为纯正的八十年代Electro-Wave合成器音乐，辅以迷幻元素，节奏缓慢而适于舞蹈，女声主唱贯穿始终。声响设计具有强烈的时代辨识度，模拟合成器音色与空间感音效营造出复古氛围。专辑前半部分收录了若干颇具力度的作品，但后半部分被评论者认为略显平淡，创作灵感有所衰退。该专辑主要面向八十年代电子黄金时代的资深乐迷与收藏者，独立厂牌Anna Logue Records发行。作为复古合成器合辑，其在电子与暗潮边缘地带具有一定吸引力，但在实验性、创新性与跨领域融合方面较为有限，整体定位偏怀旧与类型化。

items.body:
London’s soul positive festival-turned-family, GALA hail a decade of community action with 15 cuts spanning Charlie Dark’s spoken word to Marcellus Pittman’s choice deep house, soca-techno from Amaliah, and Yu Su’s dreamy garage-house glyder...

"Ten Years of GALA is both an archive and a horizon: a reflection on where GALA has come from, and a signal of what lies ahead. Founded in 2016 as a one-day gathering in South London, GALA has grown into a global point of reference for dancers, artists and collectives drawn together by a shared commitment to independence, collaboration and underground music culture. Rather than charting success through scale alone, the festival has consistently prioritised integrity, community and musical curiosity – values that underpin this release.

Spanning fifteen tracks, Ten Years of GALA unfolds as a considered journey. It opens with an intimate spoken contribution from Charlie Dark, grounding the compilation firmly in GALA’s home of Peckham before gradually expanding outward into fuller, club-focused terrain. From there, the record moves between moods and tempos, tracing a path from reflective moments into the physical language of the dancefloor.

The compilation brings together longtime friends of the festival alongside newer voices drawn into its orbit in recent years. Each artist contributes a distinct perspective, but collectively the tracks form a coherent portrait – not of a single sound, but of a shared ethos shaped over ten years of gatherings, collaborations and days spent dancing together.

Rather than a retrospective in the conventional sense, Ten Years of GALA functions as a living document. It captures fragments of past editions, scenes and relationships, while remaining firmly oriented toward the future. These are not museum pieces, but records designed to be played, shared and folded back into the spaces from which they came. Together, the compilation holds a piece of GALA’s first decade – not as a closed chapter, but as a foundation for what comes next."
items._cn_summary: 《Ten Years of GALA》是伦敦地下音乐节GALA成立十周年的纪念合辑，收录十五首作品，横跨口语诗、深邃浩室、soca-techno与梦幻车库浩室等风格。合辑以Peckham为起点，呈现派对场景的演变脉络，强调社群文化与地下舞曲传统的延续。参与艺人包括资深电子音乐人Marcellus Pittman、Yu Su等，作品以俱乐部语境为核心，融合了soca等加勒比节奏元素与电子节拍，在世界音乐与电子舞曲之间形成一定跨界。但整体仍偏向舞曲与俱乐部文化范畴，在声音实验、即兴或前卫方向上的探索有限，与实验电子、IDM、环境音乐、前卫爵士等深度实验路线的距离较远。

items.body: Review by Alana — It seems only appropriate that I should put forth my own review of this album, after having witnessed its creation from a thought into a record.I will not pretend to understand the musicality in any technical way. I am a simple punter in that regard. This level of mastery is a lifetime of heartache channeled into something far more beautiful than I would have ever imagined would be born from pain.Preconceived ideas can be harmful in that way I suppose. I always thought sadness begets sad songs and pain drives an angry soundtrack but this album moves me through my own emotions in a way I didn't expect at all.It begins in a place of scarcity and uncertainty that feels really familiar to me. The first track 'Always' is such a catchy one, though it manages to dip into instrumental sections the radio would hesitate to touch, before dancing back to a chorus you can sing along to, and I do.It's upbeat and memorable, and leads well into the second track, 'Sexy Ceiling Magic'.This one starts with a few seconds of silence before bursting into a funky groove that makes me want to dance. The vocals from Benny Grant are phenomenal, especially when you realise he's playing that virtuosic guitar at the same time. My favourite line is "I can't feel my feet. They're running, right?"I feel that in my soul. That numbness that freezes you and you just hope you are in motion nonetheless. Surreal.The song sounds funky, and though I can't pull it apart technically, I can tell there is some magic going on that's tricking my ear into hearing simplicity over complex composition.'Stone Cold Turkey' comes in hard, right when you're ready for it. The guitar virtuosity shines right away and you're thinking "here we go". The vocals are powerful and yet effortlessly move with a dynamic range that's impressive and emotionally gripping. I remember hearing this song instrumentally at first and wondering how one would even sing over it with the depth of the musicality, but there it is.It's my second favourite track on the album after 'Sexy Ceiling Magic', mainly because I just love singing those title lyrics over and over through the absolute jam of an ending.Mike Mangini knocked this one out of the park, I say that like he didn't do that on all the tracks he worked on but this one, I thought this one really sounded like he's having so much fun! I love his charisma shining through, the personality he poured into it and how he manages to play so much without crowding the song at all. I have no idea how he does it, to me it sounds impossible for one man to play, and yet, I have no doubt as everyone I speak to about this record tells me Mike makes the impossible possible. I'll take their word for it, they're usually drummers who remember Mike for his incredible skill level.'I Am The Man' - there's a section at 3:25, I was told it's "polymeter" which meant absolutely nothing to me at the time and even though I've educated myself since, I still can't fully wrap my head around it when I hear it. The song has tricks beyond my comprehension which I love, it feels like magic to be thinking "how did they do that??"My favourite part of this has one to be the build up to the line "Under the sun, I am the one". I think this is the song Mike was comparing to a lava lamp and I get that. It's viscous and yet fluid.The next track, 'Sucker' is such a stark reminder of our humanity. "Scroll, scroll, scroll ? I'm just getting started, waging war with myself".Oh boy, what a mirror. An unflattering one at that, and yet there I am singing along again. What can I say? I am a sucker indeed.The closing track 'Head In The Clouds' is this hard hitting anthem you just want to belt out despite your uncanny ability to sound like a cat that's being thrown into a bath by an enthusiastic toddler.The chorus is one of those ones you just can't help it, you scream it out as loud as you can and it helps. You get out all your frustrations and you feel heard and seen and when the song ends, you feel better!Mike did this one in a single take, I remember Benny wanting no changes, zero, which almost NEVER happens.This album is phenomenal in my completely biased opinion. The guitar work is undeniably insane, the composition is fascinating and there's something for everyone in there whether you can fully appreciate the techniques deployed or you're like myself and just love how it makes you feel. Howie Weinberg amplified the Solfeggio frequencies 174Hz, 285Hz, 396Hz, 417Hz, 528Hz, 639Hz, 741Hz, 852Hz, 963Hz, and the Schumann Resonance frequency 7.83Hz during the mastering process. Personally I feel a real sense of resolution as the final drum hits roll out, maybe that's the frequencies, maybe that's the journey coming to an end. I know it's a cliche but this album really is a journey. It guides me through my own experiences and sends me out the other side a different person, a better person who has a firmer grip on what it is to exist comfortably in one's skin. There is a sense of acceptance as the final track closes, then you want to press play again and take it from the top.This is what SYNAESTHESIA is to me, and I would encourage anyone to sit down and listen to this album because it will change you and I truly mean that.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张归类为Eclectic Prog的前卫摇滚专辑，由SONIC MANTRA乐队创作，吉他手兼主唱Benny Grant与鼓手Mike Mangini（前Dream Theater成员）合作。乐评描述音乐融合了funky律动与复杂作曲技法，包含polymeter等前卫摇滚元素，吉他演奏极具技术性。专辑在funk律动与前卫复杂性之间取得平衡，旋律性强且具有器乐炫技段落。乐评人并非技术导向的听众，更注重情感共鸣的描述。从用户偏好来看，前卫摇滚这一标签与用户首要关注的前卫/实验音乐有交集，但专辑整体呈现更偏向技巧型prog fusion，而非真正的前卫实验、爵士即兴或电子声响探索，与用户偏好的核心方向存在一定距离。

items.body: Review by Wisdom Moon — Simon Phillips' 'Protocol' outings never disappoint. He always employs the cream of the crop virtuosos to flesh out his musical vision. This time round, he has:Ernest Tibbs / bassOtmaro Ruiz / piano, keyboardsAlex Sill / guitarPhillip Whack / alto saxophoneAlmost the same line up as Protocol 5, just with a different saxophonist. The album kicks off with 'Andromeda', full of brooding angular riffs, a powerful opener. 'Unstable Grounds' that follows is all funk and fusion, with Ernest Tibbs' slap bass setting the scene - such a grooving tune with delightful twists and turns and unpredictable drum patterns from Simon in the middle section. 'Intrepid Traveller' starts of with low piano bass, cross stick from Simon and muted clean chords from Alex. Phillips stretches out in a screeching solo over funky chord stabs provided by Otmaro, heading into the main memorable riff - and so it goes on.If you have enjoyed the previous incarnations of Protocol, then you are sure to enjoy this one too. It's fusion music at its finest
items._cn_summary: Simon Phillips的《Protocol 6》延续了其爵士融合系列的路线，乐队阵容几乎与前作相同，仅更换了萨克斯手。专辑以暗涌式的棱角分明riff开场，随后进入放克与融合律动的交织，低音 slap 与鼓组的不规则节奏变化成为亮点。钢琴与吉他的配合提供旋律与和声框架，萨克斯独奏在放克和弦推进中展开。整体定位为成熟的爵士融合作品，演奏水准扎实，编曲注重律动与即兴段落的交替。然而，评论中未提及任何突破性的实验元素或跨领域探索，乐手配置和制作思路与前作高度相似，对于追求前卫与实验声响的听众而言缺乏新鲜感。

items.body: Review by ProgfanJP — French multi-instrumentalist Tom Penaguin has made no secret of his deep admiration for the Canterbury rock scene that flourished in the 1960s and 70s, and his vintage jazz-rock sound, rooted directly in the tradition of Egg and National Health, has been making waves among Canterbury and progressive rock fans worldwide. Now his long-awaited follow-up, II, arrives in 2026.Like its predecessor, the album was built entirely as a one-man overdub recording, pieced together over roughly four months in his home studio with an enviable arsenal of vintage gear including a Fender Rhodes Mark II, Hohner Pianet C and Hammond L122. The result is the same composition-driven, carefully constructed jazz-rock that defined his debut, carrying forward both the sound and the spirit of the 70s Canterbury scene in full.The signatures are all there: the Dave Stewart-influenced organ and electric piano, the warm, full-bodied bass tone, and guitar playing with real confidence and conviction. The centrepiece of the album is "The Ornamental Hermit Suite", a four-part suite that stands comfortably alongside classic Canterbury recordings like "Mumps", showcasing a remarkable range of timbres and a level of harmonic sophistication that makes it essential listening on its own terms.A record built with genuine love for the music and the craft to back it up.
items._cn_summary: 法国音乐人Tom Penaguin的第二张专辑延续了七十年代坎特伯雷摇滚乐派的爵士摇滚传统，采用一人多轨叠加录音方式完成。制作中使用Fender Rhodes Mark II、Hohner Pianet C与Hammond L122等经典复古键盘设备，音色温暖饱满。作品受Egg、National Health以及Dave Stewart影响明显，管风琴与电钢琴交织出浓郁的怀旧氛围。核心曲目《The Ornamental Hermit Suite》为四乐章套曲，在和声复杂度和音色层次上展现了一定功力。整体而言，这是一张以传统为根基的复兴型坎特伯雷场景作品，技术扎实、编曲工整，但在创新性与实验性方面较为保守，更接近对经典风格的忠实复刻而非突破。

The core trio of Metheny with keyboardist Chris Fishman and drummer Joe Dyson anchors the record, joined by Darryl Johns on bass, Brandee Younger on harp, Luis Conte on percussion and others, for a set of 8 completely original compositions.Pat Metheny has always been one of those artists who never disappoints, and this record is no exception. There's a warmth and ease to the whole thing that makes it genuinely enjoyable from start to finish, the kind of album you put on and just let run.
items._cn_summary: Pat Metheny Side-Eye项目的第二张专辑，延续了邀约年轻乐手合作的模式。核心三重奏由Metheny、键盘手Chris Fishman和鼓手Joe Dyson组成，另有贝斯手Darryl Johns、竖琴演奏家Brandee Younger、打击乐手Luis Conte等客座乐手参与，共收录八首原创作品。整体风格定位为爵士摇滚与融合爵士，评论形容其氛围温暖流畅，从头至尾保持轻松愉悦的听感。竖琴等非常规乐器的加入为传统爵士融合增添了一些音色变化，但整体仍属主流爵士融合范畴，偏向可听性较强的器乐作品。

items.body: Away from the grand orchestral stages and the heavy resonance of the piano, Elena Stojceska and Romain Petiot find a fragile, breathtakingly intimate nocturnal world in their new album, “Pour que la nuit…” Artist: Duo Solipse (Elena Stojceska: flute / Romain Petiot: guitar) Album: Pour que la nuit… Label: Solipse Records Release Date: June 5, 2026 Recorded at: Studio 150, Amsterdam (Sessions: April 2024) Sometimes, an album is not just a collection of recorded pieces, but the physical translation of a long, shared human journey. For Elena Stojceska and Romain Petiot—the minds and hands behind Duo Solipse—their latest release, Pour que la nuit…, is exactly that: the beautiful, hard-earned fruit of a deep companionship with the music of Claude Debussy, shaped over years, changing seasons, and different places. To build an entire album around Debussy using only a flute and a guitar feels beautifully audacious—mostly because Debussy never actually wrote a single note for this combination. Yet, listening to these tracks, recorded in the warm, quiet atmosphere of Amsterdam’s Studio 150, it feels like this music was always meant to live here, stripped of its traditional grandeur and laid bare. A Study in Black, White, and Iridescent Color The spark for this whole project was lit back in 2017, when a close friend of the duo, Vincent Airault, suggested a wild idea: arranging Prélude à l’après-midi d’un Faune for just flute and guitar. Elena and Romain admit they were skeptical at first. How do you translate a massive, glittering orchestral masterpiece into the quiet dialogue of two intimate acoustic instruments? They solved it by embracing the restriction. They turned the Prélude into a “black and white” study. By peeling away the heavy symphonic layers, they exposed a raw, fragile, and deeply human core. Curiously, they placed this track at the very end of the album, turning it into a circular ending—a sudden burst of daylight that casts a retrospective warmth over the entire night you just walked through. If the Prélude is about stripping away color, their rendition of the Six épigraphes antiques (arranged by Romain himself from the four-hand piano original) does the exact opposite. Here, the duo takes the stark “black and white” of the piano and transforms it into something iridescent and shimmering. The breathy warmth of the flute and the tactile pluck of the guitar strings create a dream-like landscape inspired by ancient myths and distant, idealized worlds, blurring the lines between what is real and what is imagined. From Modern Anxiety to Oceanic Peace The night, however, isn’t always peaceful, and the album doesn’t shy away from its darker, heavier corners. It opens with Edison Denisov’s Sonata, which feels like entering a restless, midnight cityscape. Through a dialogue filled with avant-garde sound effects and quarter-tones, the music mimics the subtle, unpredictable sounds of a nocturnal wildlife taking over the dark. Meanwhile, the guitar plods along imperturbably—a striking, almost ironic echo of our modern world, completely oblivious to the secret life that unfolds after hours. The perfect antidote to this tension comes through the music of Tōru Takemitsu, a composer who truly inherited Debussy’s spiritual obsession with nature. His piece Toward the Sea (originally commissioned by Greenpeace and performed here on the alto flute) is a gorgeous, immersive experience. Takemitsu weaves notes into what he called “the sea of tonality”. The music becomes fluid, wide, and spacious; the flute feels like a solitary wind blowing across dark, deep waters, carrying a cinematic weight that hits you straight in the chest. Intimate Solitudes In the middle of this journey, the duo steps back to give each other room for two haunting solo confessions. Romain takes on Manuel de Falla’s Homenaje, a piece written as a funeral tribute to Debussy. His guitar carries a heavy, austere Spanish grief that builds tension before melting into a distant musical quote. In response, Elena delivers Tomislav Zografski’s Invention “Syrinx”, a solo flute monologue that stands as a contemporary, lonely echo bouncing through the dark. The Verdict Pour que la nuit… is a profoundly honest album. It takes immense courage to take historical, academic classical masterpieces and play them with this level of vulnerability and space. Under the artistic direction of Daniel Rowland and captured beautifully by sound engineer Joeri Saal, the recording feels incredibly close—you can hear the wood, the breath, the fingers sliding on strings, and the quiet spaces in between. For the modern classical and ambient community, this is a record to be cherished. It’s a bridge between old-world impressionism and modern, cinematic sound design. Turn off the lights, close your eyes, and let this circular night wash over you. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由长笛与吉他二重奏演绎，以德彪西作品的改编为核心，辅以苏联作曲家杰尼索夫的奏鸣曲，呈现出当代室内乐与少量现代主义语汇的交织。两位音乐家通过精简的编制剥离了原作的交响化外壳，暴露出更内在、更亲密的线条，同时保留了印象派特有的色彩感与呼吸感。杰尼索夫奏鸣曲部分引入了先锋音响技法和微分音元素，为整体偏古典的基调增添了一定的实验性张力。然而，从整体定位来看，专辑仍然根植于传统古典语汇，与纯粹的前卫实验、即兴爵士或电子声响领域距离较远。编配思路有一定新意，厂牌为独立小规模发行，演奏具有细腻的室内乐品质，但跨界融合的深度有限，更适合当代古典乐迷而非极端实验音乐爱好者。

items.body: A war of words, They want you on their side, It’s all for power, To conquer and divide. Promises have a strange power: they ask us to believe in something that has not happened yet, turning a word given in the present into a bridge toward the future. At their best, they hold up friendships, love affairs, movements, contracts, countries, and songs — invisible, but load-bearing. But somewhere along the way, the promise became another tool of persuasion, polished into a slogan, stamped onto a product, fed through a corporate choir, and sold back to us under fluorescent light. Now promises arrive dressed in branding, panic, and performance, offered by people who profit when everyone else starts doubting the ground beneath their feet. The word remains, but the weight has changed: what once carried trust now often carries leverage. That crisis of faith runs through “World of Promises,” the new single from Scottish synthwave and synthpop artist Michael Oakley. The track appears on his new album Prologue, out now via NewRetroWave, and finds Oakley turning the bright machinery of retro-futurist pop toward something darker: a world of overstimulation, public fracture, and language drained of meaning. Musically, “World of Promises” moves with a sleek, late-night pressure: a seductive bass synth, compressed dance-floor stomp, warping metallic accents, cinematic pads, and Oakley’s silk-smooth vocal delivery cutting through the dry ice. The reference points are there — Depeche Mode, Pet Shop Boys, New Order, The Midnight, FM-84 — but Oakley pushes the track into a glossier, more high-stakes register, where synthpop romance meets corporate dread and the dance floor starts to look like a control room. Lyrically, “World of Promises” takes aim at false hope, weaponized messaging, corporate agendas, and the way public life turns people into factions. Oakley frames the song as a question of trust: “Do our words still mean a thing?” From there, the track spirals through cracked social bonds, power games, and the sense that every statement arrives with a hidden hand behind it. The song’s title becomes less a phrase of optimism than a warning label for an age built on empty guarantees. The video turns that idea into a neon-noir surveillance thriller. It opens inside a red-lit club world of dark glasses, glowing tubes, shadowed faces, and bodies caught in the blur of VHS damage. Oakley appears amid the party’s controlled chaos, while a red-haired woman in patterned sunglasses watches from above, then from a bank of monitors, studying security footage as if she were tracking a target through a private system of power. From there, the clip cuts between bound figures, gloved hands, a blindfolded man wrapped in rope, a silver briefcase, and a gun and martini left under club lights. The imagery plays like a retro cyber-crime caper spliced into a nightclub fever dream: CCTV grids, scan-mode graphics, coded data, red rooms, blue corridors, and sudden flashes of violence held back by the video’s stylized restraint. Captions break the tension with “WHOA. HEY!”, “THAT’S HER!”, and “STOP!!!” as the video’s mystery red-haired femme fatale, brandishing the silver briefcase, gives two men the slip—giving the clip the feel of the Tech Noir scene in The Terminator, The Starck Club scene in Robocop, or a late-night broadcast from a cult film aired on Nightflight. By the final stretch, the video widens into a chase for the woman with the case, moving through backstage rooms, club corridors, a logo wall, and a burst of falling papers. When her pursuer tries to vaporize her, the blast rebounds, turning the weapon back on him and leaving smoke curling around his boots as she slips outside to a waiting car. There, the case is opened for a man whose interest only deepens the mystery — a sly nod to the glowing, unknowable MacGuffin at the center of Quentin Tarantino’s Pulp Fiction. It is sleek, theatrical, and slightly absurd in the best way: part espionage fantasy, part nightclub power struggle, part commentary on who gets watched, who gives the orders, and who walks away with the prize. Watch the video for “World of Promises” below: Michael Oakley is a Scottish synthwave producer, songwriter, and musician whose work draws from synthpop, new wave, and widescreen 1980s studio craft. Born in Glasgow, Oakley moved to Los Angeles in 2016 before settling in Canada in 2018. A self-taught musician, he first broke through with the California EP in 2017, followed by his debut full-length, Introspect, in 2019 and Odyssey in 2021. Across his catalog, Oakley has become a key figure in the modern synthwave world, balancing polished pop songwriting with the romantic voltage of vintage machines. His work has appeared in gaming projects including Wave Break: High Tides and Retro Drive, and he has also designed sound packs and synth patches for producers working in the same retro-electronic orbit. With Prologue, Oakley returns after nearly five years with a sharper, bigger, and more politically charged sound. “Imagine what Depeche Mode’s Violator album would have sounded like if it was produced by Trevor Horn.” Says Oakley, “Or if Peter Hook stumbled into Haddaway’s recording sessions. That’s Prologue.” Michael Oakley’s new album Prologue is out now. Available in red and blue editions across multiple formats, including vinyl, cassette, CD, and MiniDisc. Order the album here. items.body: Blone Noble Dominator Mystic Transfers We had very little idea what to expect when Blone Noble took the stage at Verboden Festival here in Vancouver last weekend, but were won over almost instantly by the Los Angeles art pop act’s combination of theatrical whimsy, and easy to groove to songs. Recent EP Dominator cinches the one-man show’s charms via a fairly omnivorous combination of electronic pop sounds and pure, undiluted personality. Opener “High Society” gets to the point quickly in both the original and Kontravoid remixes, layering samples, octave bass, and crooned vocals, along with a kitchen sink’s worth of vocal and guitar samples, house pianos and acid lines that are somehow corralled together into a funky whole. “Body Fascination” goes more minimal, with a simple combination of synths and drums, the song’s appeal coming from the vocal switch ups, half falsetto, half processed into weird mutant shapes. The title track is presented in both its normal version and a remix from “Tony Price” and differs considerably in each form; the former is a dance punky joint with a laidback vibe, Lou Reed by way of the discotheque, where the remix transforms the song into a hot slice of balaeric techno, all sunny vibes and drum machine shake. It’s a fun, mildly puzzling, but undeniably enjoyable suite of songs that captures Blone Noble’s charms ably. Dominator by Blone Noble Child Of Night Conspiracy Phage Tapes If you happened to have checked out Ohio duo Child Of Night’s 2021 debut The Walls At Dawn, a number of surprises await on new LP Conspiracy, none of which are unpleasant. One is the presence of a record this melodic on a label as traditionally harsh as Phage Tapes, but most important is a decided shift away from a holistic approach to moody darkwave and towards a classic, chilly vein of synthpop. The icy chirp of opener “Old Moons”‘ perky but minimal synth leads is backed by a restrained bed of supporting programming recalling either the halcyon days of Mute releases or millennial bedroom synthpop, take your pick. While one or two cuts on Child Of Night’s debut played about with these sounds, they’re the sustained focus of Conspiracy, with everything from “Complacent”‘s impatient angst to the pensive pulse of closer “The Very Last Time” holding just a patina of analog haze and echo across all their elements. There’s something of a paucity of fully-developed and memorable songs in and of themselves on the record, with individual grooves, moments, and licks standing out more than full tracks after a few listens, but the catchy vocal refrain on “It’s Cold In Here”, or the psychedelic synth squalls on “Controlled Burn” which bring The Glove to mind, all have a charm suited to Child Of Night’s new direction. Conspiracy by C.O.N. The post Observer: Blone Noble & Child Of Night appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 本篇乐评涵盖两张专辑。来自洛杉矶的Blone Noble在《Dominator》EP中呈现艺术流行风格，融合电子流行、浩室、迪斯科与舞曲朋克元素，声部层次丰富但未深入实验领域。俄亥俄组合Child Of Night的《Conspiracy》由Phage Tapes发行，从暗潮风格转向冷调合成器流行，参考Mute厂牌黄金时期与The Glove的声响特征，旋律可听性强但被乐评指出缺乏完整记忆点的曲作。整体而言，两张作品均带有暗潮与电子的底色，但更偏向旋律化的可听性方向，与深度实验/前卫路线有一定距离。

items.body:
Golden jubilee edition of a library music classic, flush with lavish, melodramatic string and key arrangements commanded by the legendary composer of the ‘Mah Nà Mah Nà’ tune, made famous by The Muppets and Benny Hill.

"Performed by a compact string ensemble and subtly augmented by piano, Hammond organ, Eminent organ, and Rhodes, the album unfolds through a series of classically-informed compositions where melody takes center stage. Each piece is concise, evocative, and purpose-built - reflecting the functional yet highly expressive nature of Italian library music at its peak.

Conceptually, the record is structured in two contrasting halves: the first side explores themes of optimism and resolution, while the second delves into darker, more introspective territories, mirroring the emotional duality suggested by its title (Tragedies and Hopes). Long overlooked outside specialist circles, Drammi e Speranze is here presented for the first time ever on vinyl reissue, newly remastered to highlight the depth and tonal richness of Umiliani’s arrangements. This release celebrates 100 years since the birth of Piero Umiliani, honoring the enduring legacy of a composer whose work continues to resonate across cinematic, library, and contemporary sample-driven music."
items._cn_summary: Piero Umiliani 经典意大利图书馆音乐的五十周年纪念再版，以弦乐合奏为核心，辅以钢琴、哈蒙德管风琴、Eminent 管风琴与 Rhodes 电钢琴，呈现出学院派古典作曲与爵士和声语汇的融合。专辑以标题"悲剧与希望"为概念分轴，上半段偏向明朗与信念主题，下半段则探索更暗沉、内省的情绪领域。作为功能性图书馆音乐巅峰时期的代表，其旋律主导、结构精炼的特质反映了该类型高度表达性的一面。该作对当代采样文化与电子音乐场景具有深远影响，是连接电影配乐、实验声响与现代制作美学的重要历史文本。

items.body:
Returning to Warp alongside Dean Blunt and Mobbs collaborator POiSON ANNA, Wu-Lu does his best Tricky impression on 'Bakerz Dozen', rapping listlessly over blown-out, rattly beats and low-slung riffs while ANNA brings the charisma.

The trip-hop that ends up being regurgitated most frequently is the polite, coffee-table gear, not the paranoid, druggy shit that gave the scene its name in the first place. But Wu-Lu knows the score by now; he's worked closely enough with the CURL crew and Touching Bass to have figured out what made that music so affecting. And 'Bakerz Dozen' is his most convincing set yet; on 'Silver Surfer', his rasping voice braids effortlessly with ANNA's adding much needed grunge to a simple drum machine beat and a worm-y, dissonant Moog bassline, while 'West Window' sounds like a real redux of the 'Maxinquaye' formula, with ANNA playing the Martina Topley-Bird roll and speak-singing, whispering or deadpanning over Wu-Lu's ominous synths.

Even the brief 'Cold Bricks (Wu Version)' helps set the scene, with its reverberating guitars and muffled duet. It's not all successful: 'Fade Thru' tries a little too hard to re-create Massive Attack's 'Unfinished Sympathy' and 'King Kong' sounds like a Prodigy b-side, but when they get the recipe right - like on 'All That I Needed' - it's magic.
items._cn_summary: 这是Wu-Lu与POiSON ANNA合作发行于Warp厂牌的trip-hop专辑，风格明显承袭Tricky与Massive Attack的九十年代英伦trip-hop传统。制作以失真鼓机节奏、混响吉他和低沉的Moog贝斯线为骨架，POiSON ANNA的说唱与人声演绎带有Martina Topley-Bird式的冷感气质，人声编织出迷幻而阴郁的氛围。暗色调合成器与粗粝质感使其在电子与暗潮领域有一定交集，但整体仍是在既有trip-hop框架内的演绎，原创性和实验性有限。部分曲目对经典配方有较为直接的参照，削弱了其独立突破的力度。

items.body:
Brassy, in-the-pocket, big band Afrobeat-jazz swag by 13-piece Hungarian ensemble, Hakumba.

“Written in a one week jam session retreat in the Hungarian countryside, and recorded at one of the highest peaks of Hungary after a year of global touring, The Garden becomes an amalgamation of the band's personal and artistic experiences. The material conveys a more jazzier approach, with complex harmonies, and an almost cinematic, dreamlike atmosphere, somewhat distancing from (but not completely forgetting) the previously emphasized, dance-oriented Afro- and Latino roots. Song for Ramon serves as the EP’s emotional climax inspired by the passing of a close friend and local underground chef pioneer.

Formed in 2019 in Budapest, Hakumba is a staple of the Hungarian festival circuit, with a growing international presence (SXSW London, SHIP, PIN Music Showcase). They’ve recently finished a tour in Australia this January.

The groove-driven ensemble blends afrobeat, jazz, and various strands of world music into a sound that is both rhythmically powerful and harmonically adventurous. With an eleven-piece lineup featuring an expansive horn section, multiple vocalists, percussion, and keys, the band moves effortlessly between dancefloor energy and more intricate, jazz-influenced musical ideas. Like the band’s previous album, the EP was again recorded, mixed, and mastered by András Weil, the producer behind The Qualitons, the only hungarian band ever performed Live at KEXP. This continuity preserves Hakumba’s recognizable sonic identity while giving space for new colors and more complex musical ideas to emerge.”
items._cn_summary: Hakumba 是一支来自匈牙利的13人大型乐团，专辑《The Garden》融合了非洲节奏、爵士和世界音乐元素。作品在匈牙利乡村的即兴创作中孕育，并录制于高山之上，呈现出电影感与梦幻氛围。编曲以铜管乐组为核心，结合人声、打击乐与键盘，节奏强劲且和声复杂，从舞曲能量延伸至更深层的爵士表达。其中《Song for Ramon》以情感高潮的形式致敬已故好友。该作在传统Afrobeat/Latino根基上融入了更自由的爵士语汇，展现了东欧音乐人对世界融合音乐的独特理解。整体定位介于舞曲型世界音乐与学院爵士之间，融合度较高但实验性有限。

items.body: Back after a four-year absence, Dublin's Gilla Band have lost none of their bite, packing two songs into 'Giraffe': one noisy, dubbed-out slow burner and a grotty, dance-punk coda. It's hard to believe it's been so long since 'Most Normal', easily 2022's best "rock" album. And the Irish four piece tease the next album with 'Giraffe', a suitably absurd whirl of frontman Dara Kiely's observations and consternations that the rest of the crew meet with oblique rhythms, distortions and scratchy noise. If they can maintain this energy for the whole record, it's gonna be special. more
items._cn_summary: 来自都柏林的四人乐队Gilla Band沉寂四年后回归，发布双曲作品《Giraffe》，延续其粗粝的后朋克与噪音摇滚路线。一首为低沉燃烧的dub-out慢板，另一首为肮脏的dance-punk尾曲。乐队以主唱Dara Kiely荒诞的观察与愤懑为核心，搭配oblique式节奏、扭曲失真与刮擦噪音，营造出密集且不安的声响质感。其前作《Most Normal》曾被认为是当年最佳摇滚专辑之一。该作品在后朋克框架内融入dub处理与噪音实验，介于工业噪音与后朋克之间，但整体仍以吉他摇滚为基底，在电子、爵士、前卫等维度上探索有限，对于偏好暗潮与后朋克的听众有一定吸引力，但跨界融合的深度与实验性较为克制。

items.body:
Echospace Detroit’s Stephen Hitchell is at his most romantic, club-friendly and elemental on these effortless dub house glyders, newly remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion

Originally issued on 12” in 2015 and hard-to-find ever since, ‘Lost Sequence’ is classic, archetypal Echospace tackle. The OG goes for 14 mins of strutting deep house groove swaddled in velvet-coated textures dubbed to the rafters and happy to hold its lane for the duration, adding extra layers of conga and crackling atmosphere as it proceeds. Hitchell’s Intrusion dub pitches the same elements in a spring weather system, drenching everything in fine mist of elemental FX and loosening the bass drum to a satisfyingly soggy slosh for 16 minutes of hypnotic bliss out.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自Echospace Detroit的Stephen Hitchell，是典型化的dub house作品，融合了深沉浩室节奏与dub回声处理技术。评论描述其质感丰富、音景沉浸，包含一首14分钟的原版深浩室groove和一首16分钟的Intrusion dub混音版本，后者在细密的元素音效雾气中展现催眠般的延展性。整体定位偏向俱乐部友好型电子音乐，声音设计注重纹理层次和氛围营造，经过Pole重新母带处理以提升沉浸感。风格上属于电子大类中的dub house分支，在用户关注的电子音乐范畴内，但更偏向舞曲场景而非IDM、ambient或glitch等更具实验性的方向，融合性有限，创新性以dub手法在浩室中的运用为主。

items.body: Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris café, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur. Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth. Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I’m guessing here), and musical saw. Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt) The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle, just to get the list started. Ukulele Lady (excerpt) The liner notes point out that “Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.” Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous “Ukulele Lady” from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie’s 1971 album Hobo’s Lullaby . The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler. N'oublie pas Gréco (excerpt) A more serious item is “N’oublie pas Gréco” (Don’t Forget Gréco”) is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gréco, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like “Fumée aux yeux” (“Smoke Gets in Your Eyes”), “Boude pas” (“Take Five”), and “Prive d’amour” (“As Time Goes By”). This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, “The young have fire, but we have light.” In its own little corner, Les Crimes du Musette shines bright. Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Carolina Chocolate Drops - Genuine Negro Jig (Review)

items.body: A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene’s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There’s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout. The opener, “Svennedal,” with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer’s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to “Nordgård,” the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus. Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional “Agnete Of Bjergmanden,” with Guldhammer’s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, “Ormsø,” mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental. Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning – what will GuldGanger do with an entire album? Find the artist online. Further reading and listening: Mats Edén - Tellef Kvifte - Knut Kvifte Nesheim - Króta (Review) Duo Ruut - Ilmateade (Review) Floating Sofa Quartet - Sofa Songs (Review)

items.body: A Common Ground Beneath Our Feet My Journey with the Silkroad Ensemble In His Own Words: Mauro Durante In 2026, I was invited to join the Silkroad Ensemble, the international collective directed by Rhiannon Giddens, as a musician (frame drums, violin, and voice) and contributor of new arrangements and compositions. Following an initial workshop and preview performance in New York in January 2026, the project will unfold through a North American tour in March 2026, featuring nine concerts alongside workshops and community outreach activities across the United States, as part of the new program Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual . The tour will continue later in the year with further residencies and performances in North America and Europe. There are musical projects that are built around a repertoire, others around a geography, and others still around a specific aesthetic vision. The Silkroad Ensemble belongs to a different category: it is a living organism built around an idea. A simple and radical idea at once—that music can be a real space of encounter between cultures, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a daily, concrete, lived practice. Founded in 1998 by Yo-Yo Ma, Silkroad has never been an ensemble in the traditional sense. There is no fixed lineup, no stable repertoire. Instead, it is a community of musicians from different traditions, chosen not only for their technical excellence, but for their ability to inhabit a threshold—the space between rootedness and transformation. Each musician brings with them a language, a sound, a memory. What matters most is the willingness to place that language in dialogue with others, without hierarchy. In recent years, the project has been guided by Rhiannon Giddens, one of the most powerful and deeply insightful voices in contemporary music. Her presence gives the work a clear direction: the goal is not to create an artificial synthesis of traditions, but to create the conditions for each tradition to speak fully, and to transform through encounter. Rhiannon possesses a rare kind of leadership—one that never imposes itself, but quietly shapes the space, both musically and humanly. Entering this context means immediately finding yourself in a space where musical identity is not something to defend, but something to offer. The pizzica, the frame drums, the violin I carry with me are no longer only instruments of a local tradition, but elements in a broader conversation, where every sound is heard both for what it is and for what it might become. It is within this space that my participation in Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual began to take shape. Even before the music itself, what stands out is the quality of listening. A real, deep listening, in which every musical gesture is at once personal and collective. This, perhaps, is the true nature of Silkroad: not simply an ensemble, but a place. A circle. A space where music returns to what it has always been—a form of relationship. Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual Music as Refuge and Resistance The word sanctuary can be understood in many ways: refuge, protected space, a place where it is still possible to pause, to listen, to rebuild a sense of community. Working on this project in the United States today carries a particular weight. This is a country marked by deep and increasingly visible tensions, where public discourse is often shaped by fear, by closure, by the idea that identity is something to be defended against someone else. The same tendency can be seen elsewhere—in Italy, across Europe, and in many parts of the world. The rise of nationalism, ongoing wars, and increasingly restrictive migration policies contribute to a climate in which separation begins to feel like the natural order of things. Within this context, finding yourself in a room each day with musicians from Morocco, India, Japan, Armenia, Scotland, Congo, Italy, and the United States becomes something very real. Each person brings their own history, their own sound, their own way of inhabiting music. What emerges is not a fusion of identities, but their coexistence. The taranta, Gnawa music, Indian classical tradition, American folk music—these practices were never conceived merely as forms of entertainment. They were born as tools to accompany moments of transformation, to help individuals and communities move through crisis, grief, healing, and renewal. Sanctuary begins with this understanding. With the idea that music can still be a space where encounter is possible without the need to simplify or protect oneself. A space where listening becomes an act of trust. Something simple and real happens: people from different parts of the world breathe together, listen together, and build something that did not exist before. In a time that often pushes toward division, this act acquires a different weight. It becomes, in its own quiet way, a form of resistance. Entering the Circle The first rehearsals are always a delicate moment. I took part in an initial workshop in Ireland last December, with a smaller group—Rhiannon, Mazz, Francesco, Niwel, and myself—and then a second workshop with the full ensemble in January, followed by a beautiful preview performance in New York on January 10, 2026, as part of the Winter Jazz Fest. At that stage, there is no shared language yet. You observe each other, you play, you try things, you listen. What strikes you immediately is the extraordinary musical and human level of the people involved. They are incredible. Not only great instrumentalists, but musicians who have developed a deep relationship with their own musical traditions, and who have learned to question them, to keep them flexible and alive. The Hawaiian bassist Shawn Conley, for example, moves effortlessly between bow and pizzicato, shifting from a lyrical, singing tone to remarkable rhythmic agility, using the instrument with a freedom that easily recalls the expressive range of a cello. Beside him, Scottish harpist Maeve Gilchrist brings a presence that is both refined and fearless. Beyond a complete mastery of everything one might expect from the harp—the luminous, almost celestial sound—she possesses an extraordinary rhythmic and harmonic awareness, and a musical curiosity that allows her to make bold, unexpected choices without hesitation. Armenian cellist Karen Ouzounian represents the very highest level of classical tradition, but with something more: a strong personal voice, a deep compositional sensibility, and a lyrical approach to improvisation that makes every gesture feel necessary. With Francesco Turrisi, who like me comes from Italy, we already share a longer history. Yet I remain constantly struck by his ability to move between radically different instruments—accordion, piano, frame drums, string instruments—with complete naturalness. His immense musicality is not tied to any single instrument, but to a broader understanding of sound, form, and structure. Congolese guitarist Niwel Tsumbu is simply one of the finest guitarists I have ever encountered. His relationship with the guitar transcends the instrument itself. He brings together a deep knowledge of African musical traditions, an innate rhythmic sensibility, refined harmonic awareness, and an extraordinary improvisational freedom. Kaoru Watanabe embodies, in a profound way, the idea that tradition is also a choice. Japanese and American, he moves fluidly between cultural languages with a rare balance of respect, discipline, and expressive freedom. His playing is never a reproduction of the past, but its living continuation. With Mehdi Nassouli, on guembri and voice, I feel a particular closeness. Like me with pizzica, he belongs deeply to a specific musical world—in his case, the Gnawa tradition of Morocco. Yet his experience has given him an equally deep ability to engage in dialogue with other musical languages, without ever losing the center of his own sound. Sandeep Das’s presence on tabla is a constant point of reference. He is, quite literally, a guru of Indian music, and yet his authority never creates distance. On the contrary, he makes every interaction feel natural, effortless, both musically and humanly. Japanese percussionist Haruka Fujii brings an extraordinary level of precision and listening. Her virtuosity is never displayed for its own sake, but always placed in service of the music, strengthening the cohesion of the ensemble. American violinist and vocalist Mazz Swift embodies a rare combination of strength and openness. Their voice and violin move fluidly across genres and traditions, grounded yet constantly searching, expanding the expressive space of the group. And then there is Rhiannon. It is difficult to find a single word that captures her presence. She is a complete musician—singer, instrumentalist, composer, dancer, and leader—but above all, she possesses a clarity of vision that holds everything together and inspires everyone around her. Her leadership does not operate through control, but through listening. She creates a space in which each musician can fully express themselves, while contributing to something larger than any individual voice. Common Ground "Common Ground" is the pizzica I wrote for the Silkroad Ensemble. I use the word “wrote” with caution, because the piece truly exists only through the creative contribution of each musician involved. I laid the foundations: the rhythm, the groove, the structure, the overall architecture, and the fixed melodic and harmonic elements. But what makes it alive is the way each musician inhabits it. The idea first emerged during the workshop in Ireland. At that stage, we were still searching for common ground, a way of being together musically without renouncing our individual identities. It felt natural for me to bring the rhythm of pizzica—my familiar and chosen refuge, my Sanctuary. Back home, I began to develop that intuition, shaping a structure that preserved the physical and rhythmic core of the tradition, while remaining open enough to allow each musician to find their own place within it. We worked on the piece during the workshop in the United States, and performed it live for the first time in New York, just days later, at the Winter Jazz Fest. It was extraordinary to witness how naturally each musician entered that rhythm without hesitation. No one was trying to imitate something that did not belong to them. Instead, each voice emerged clearly, freely coexisting alongside the others. In that moment, I understood that the piece had found its true meaning. It was no longer simply the pizzica I had written, but a shared space. A Common Ground laid beneath our feet. Experiences like this change you in subtle but lasting ways. The energy they transmit, the enthusiasm, the renewed sense of trust in the future—all of it remains. A few years ago, I was in Adelaide to perform at WOMAD with Justin Adams, and the night before our concert I had the chance to attend a performance by Billy Bragg. At one point, he said something that has stayed with me ever since: “Music does not have the power to change the world. But it can make you believe that the world can be changed.” Further information about the Silk Road project This article was originally published in Italian in Blogfoolk
items._cn_summary: 本文为意大利手鼓与提琴演奏家毛罗·杜兰特加入丝绸之路乐团的个人随笔，介绍了该乐团由大提琴家马友友创立、现由格莱美得主丽安农·吉登斯执掌的跨文化音乐理念。乐团无固定编制与曲目，强调不同传统之间的平等对话，新项目《庇护所：共鸣与仪式的力量》以北美及欧洲巡演为核心。文中提及意大利南部萨伦托地区的皮齐卡舞曲与手鼓传统在跨文化语境中的转化，呈现世界融合的音乐方向。文章本质为艺术家自述而非乐评，缺乏对具体声响、编曲或演奏技法的深入分析，信息密度有限。整体定位偏世界音乐与跨文化融合，与当代实验或前卫方向距离较远。

items.body: WÖR x Kongero Songbooks Live Review by Chris Nickson WÖR, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group Wör, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here’s a spoiler: it turns out they’re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with “Var Är Du?”, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). WÖR, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it’s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled “Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,” where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful “Klosterjungfrun.” The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It’s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. WÖR, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There’s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that’s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they’ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. Kongero WÖR More music: Kongero - Live In Longueiul WÖR - Back to the 1780s
items._cn_summary: 这张《Songbooks Live》是比利时五件乐器组合WÖR与瑞典女性无伴奏民歌四重唱Kongero的跨文化合作现场专辑。WÖR擅长演绎早期音乐，Kongero则以瑞典民歌阿卡贝拉闻名。专辑将两者的传统曲目及一首原创作品融合，以复杂的编曲和精致的和声编排呈现。音乐风格定位为欧洲早期音乐与北欧民歌的跨界对话，演唱与器乐交织，氛围优雅而沉稳。从风格来看，该作品更偏向传统民谣与早期音乐的交汇，而非带有实验性或前卫色彩的世界融合，在声音设计和即兴拓展上较为保守。整体制作精良，演奏精准，但创新维度和声音实验性有限，适合对欧洲传统民谣及早期音乐跨界合作感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — Mirror to the Sky is a late-career prog rock statement from Yes that leans heavily into atmosphere, texture, and long-form composition rather than hooks or radio-friendly structure.The album feels lush, spacious, and often meditative. Steve Howe's guitar is still the spine of the record, weaving melodic lines that drift between gentle acoustic passages and more expansive, symphonic builds. I always love hearing him launch into lead guitar passages that drift into the stratosphere. When the band locks into a groove or gradually escalates a theme, you get that classic prog reward which is slow-burning immersion. Mirror to the Sky is a solid entry in the Yes catalogue, very reflective and easy on the ears. You can't mistake that distinctive Yes sound and admittedly I was drawn in by the art on the cover again. I don't think its a masterpiece by any means but it's a journey into modern prog rather than high-impact drama.
items._cn_summary: Mirror to the Sky 是 Yes 乐队2023年发行的交响前卫摇滚专辑。作品延续乐队标志性的长篇作曲手法，以氛围、质感和空间感为核心，融合轻柔原声段落与宏大交响化构建。Steve Howe 的吉他穿插于沉思的民谣片段与宽广器乐展开之间。整体偏向冥想性与沉浸式聆听，强调缓慢情绪铺陈而非戏剧性冲突。作为资深主流前卫乐队的成熟期作品，编曲工整扎实，但未展现明显实验性突破或跨类型融合意图，在前卫摇滚谱系中属于较为传统成熟的路线表达。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — In a recent MRR newsletter Nick Katona highlighted this album, originally released in 2010, and given I had previously reviewed their 2017 release, 'Chaptersend', I thought I would give it a try. Although their debut had been released just the previous year, there had been a line-up change in the departure of guitarist Stefano Lago, but the remaining members just shared the duties between them and carried on as a trio. Richard George Allen (drums, assorted percussion, vocals), Luca Briccola (guitars, keyboards, flute, orchestration, backing vocals) and Paolo Pigni (bass, acoustic guitars, vocals) here deliver a concept album inspired by a true story suggested by Richard. It follows a businessman trapped in a New York lift over a weekend and takes us through multiple emotions, from claustrophobic panic to the exhilaration of a new beginning.Mogador are a band who I feel never truly gained the recognition they deserved, possibly because they are an Italian progressive band who followed much more of a crossover style than the somewhat heavier and more robust RPI, and they certainly have a good home in MRR in that their music is heavily influenced by the lighter and more American influences with AOR melding with pop melodies and classic progressive layering and styles. This is an album which certainly benefits from repeated listenings as the more it is played the more one hears, from tubular bells and underlying acoustic guitars to complex bass runs and classic keyboard sounds as they cross genres making music which is both immediate and enjoyable, complex yet somehow simplistic and easy to understand at the same time. Sadly, the highly influential Pigni left after this album, turning instead to his solo project Sarastro Blake who released their solo album in 2013, and there have been just two more Mogador releases since then, although the band do appear to have been gigging until a few years ago. That is a real shame as this is a thoroughly enjoyable album which anyone who likes crossover prog should definitely seek out.
items._cn_summary: 意大利乐队Mogador于2010年发行的跨界前卫摇滚专辑，以真实故事为概念蓝本，讲述一位商人在纽约电梯中困度周末的多重情绪变化。音乐风格定位为跨界前卫摇滚，融合AOR成人抒情摇滚、流行旋律与经典前卫摇滚的层次编排，呈现出轻盈的美式影响。评论者指出该专辑在反复聆听后展现出管钟琴、原声吉他、复杂贝斯线条与经典键盘音色的丰富层次，兼具即时可听性与复杂编曲。乐评人认为乐队未获得应有的关注，但作品质量扎实。整体属于偏向主流可听性的前卫摇滚，与实验性、极端前卫路线相距较远。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — I was scrolling though my FB feed recently (it is an awful habit, I know) and came across a band saying they had just been given access to the promo of their new album, and would anyone be interested in reviewing it? As far as I was aware, I knew nothing about them so said I would go for it and was soon listening to a real throwback in time, something which reminded me just why I keeping doing this writing lark after so many years. It came as quite a shock to realise I had actually reviewed these guys previously, when I said nice things about their 2019 release 'Nattfolien', but having heard this one I am now determined to keep more on track with what they are doing as this is nothing short of incredible.The line-up is still H�kon Oftung (vocals, guitars, keyboards, flute) and Kristian Fr�land (drums) plus some guests in the form of Jon Henriksen from Black Magic, Kristian Valbo from Obliteration/Aura Noir, and Andreas Prestmo and Lars Fredrik Fr�islie from Wobbler, and although their ninth album is just 36 minutes long it feels much bigger than that. This is an album out of time, something which belongs in a time 50 years ago when I was a teenager reading Tolkein and listening to the wide breadth of progressive rock. This is classic progressive rock as a genre as opposed to a direction, bringing in elements of Gentle Giant (in particular), Deep Purple, Atomic Rooster, Rush, Genesis, Camel and more. It has a warm analogue feeling as opposed to digital, and the world disappears when listening to this as they move between acoustic and heavy, with influences from Steve Howe and Yes never too far away. As I said before, one could easily imagine this album is all about Oftung given he provides everything apart from drums, but it is Fr�land who keeps it all together, turning the drums very much into an instrument in their own right, being very reminiscent of the likes of Bruford and Peart. This does not feel like an album from 2026 but instead is a lost masterpiece from 50 years ago. I am glad it is not too long as this keeps it short and sweet, just like the albums were back then, when they happily sat on one side of a TDK D90. This is classic symphonic progressive rock with elements of hard rock and folk, all brought into a 1970's pot and stirred with love. It is the type of album which makes the listener fall in love with the genre all over again.
items._cn_summary: JORDSJØ的《Pestkrønikene》是一部向1970年代交响前卫摇滚致敬的回溯之作，融合了硬摇滚、民谣元素，风格上接近Gentle Giant、Genesis、Yes等乐队的经典语汇。整张专辑以温暖的模拟音色为基调，键盘、吉他、长笛与人声交织，鼓手表现出色，整体呈现出浓厚的复古氛围。虽然具备前卫摇滚的编制与结构意识，但本质上属于传统类型作品，缺乏实验性与创新性，也不涉及电子、爵士、即兴或暗潮等元素。与用户偏好的实验/先锋/爵士/电子路线距离较远，作为扎实的复古交响前卫摇滚有一定价值，但在其口味框架下匹配度有限。

items.body: Australian industrial-punk project Schkeuditzer Kreuz has released the single “Keep Dancing” on June 5, 2026. The Schkeuditzer Kreuz “Keep Dancing” single pairs the “Fresh Graves Mix” of the track, taken from the 2025 album “Swan Grinder”, with the B-side “Poor Impulse Control (Three Days Deep)”. The single is issued as a 7-inch vinyl release with a digital edition. The artwork is by Rufus Dayglo, and the audio was mastered by Martin Bowes of Attrition, who also mastered the parent album “Swan Grinder”. “Keep Dancing” originally appeared on that record; the “Fresh Graves Mix” reworks the track for this release. Keep Dancing by Schkeuditzer Kreuz Kieren Hills says: “Keep Dancing is a song of rebellion. It is a song about standing up for what you think is right. And it is a song of standing up for those who can’t stand up for themselves. It is about sticking together and sticking around to make our voice heard in a time where we feel under constant attack. The world feels pretty bad right now, but the song is about not switching off even when that feels like the only option.” Kieren continues: “I have always wanted to have a go at putting guitar with one of my songs and this seemed like the perfect one to do. So I rerecorded it with guitars as well as redoing the drums and synths to make it sound more urgent and more, well, danceable.” About the B-side “Three Days Deep” he says: “I took the original song and sped it up to 240bpm, distorted the fuck out of everything and well, we all know what Three Days Deep refers to…” Meanwhile, Schkeuditzer Kreuz is also using the “Keep Dancing” release to make an early announcement of an own 19-date tour of Japan, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia in October this year. Schkeuditzer Kreuz – Japan & Southeast Asia Tour 2026 02 Oct ’26, Fri – Japan / Tokyo – Earthdom 03 Oct ’26, Sat – Japan / Tokyo – Ochiai 04 Oct ’26, Sun – Japan / city TBC – venue TBC 06 Oct ’26, Tue – Japan / Shizuoka – Sou-gen 07 Oct ’26, Wed – Japan / Osaka – Hokage 08 Oct ’26, Thu – Cambodia / Siem Reap – Atlantis Metal Bar 09 Oct ’26, Fri – Cambodia / Phnom Penh – Distortion 10 Oct ’26, Sat – Thailand / Chiang Mai – Yoda Gallery 13 Oct ’26, Tue – Thailand / Bangkok – venue TBC 16 Oct ’26, Fri – Malaysia / Kuala Lumpur – Moutou 17 Oct ’26, Sat – Philippines / Bacolod City – Visayas Hardcore Punk Fest 18 Oct ’26, Sun – Philippines / General Santos City – venue TBC 19 Oct ’26, Mon – Philippines / Davao City – venue TBC 20 Oct ’26, Tue – Philippines / Cebu City – venue TBC 21 Oct ’26, Wed – Philippines / Quezon City – venue TBC 22 Oct ’26, Thu – Philippines / Dasmariñas Cavite – venue TBC 23 Oct ’26, Fri – Indonesia / Bali – Gimme Shelter 24 Oct ’26, Sat – Indonesia / Jogjakarta – venue TBC 25 Oct ’26, Sun – Indonesia / Purworejo – venue TBC About Schkeuditzer Kreuz Schkeuditzer Kreuz is the solo project of Kieren Hills, who was born in New Zealand and is based in Lawson, in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia. The project combines electronic body music and industrial with crust and d-beat punk, a sound Hills has described with terms such as “industrial synth crust” and “d-beat raw synth punk”. The discography includes “Isolated and Alone” (2021) and “No Life Left” (2023), the latter repressed on Bad Habit Records. In November 2024 the project shared a split 7-inch with Decide Today, which Side-Line reported at the time. The third album “Swan Grinder“, mastered by Martin Bowes, was released on August 30, 2025, and was supported by a European tour across September and October 2025. The “Keep Dancing” single is released on June 5, 2026.

items.body: French covers project Nouvelle Vague has announced a 13-date UK tour, “A Date With Depeche Mode,” running across March 2027 to mark a new album of the same name. Nouvelle Vague was founded in 2003 by Marc Collin and Olivier Libaux, who reworked post-punk and new-wave songs in a bossa nova style. Libaux died in 2021 but the project continues to tour. Tour dates for Nouvelle Vague All confirmed dates take place in the United Kingdom in March 2027. Tickets went on sale on 5 June 2026. 4 March 2027 — Stratford-upon-Avon, Rother Street Arts House, United Kingdom 5 March 2027 — London, KOKO (Camden), United Kingdom 6 March 2027 — Manchester, Band on the Wall, United Kingdom 7 March 2027 — Norwich, The Waterfront, United Kingdom 10 March 2027 — Hove, The Old Market, United Kingdom 11 March 2027 — Cambridge, The Cambridge Junction, United Kingdom 12 March 2027 — Canterbury, Gulbenkian Theatre, United Kingdom 13 March 2027 — Liverpool, Hangar 34, United Kingdom 14 March 2027 — Bristol, The Trinity Centre, United Kingdom 17 March 2027 — Nottingham, Metronome, United Kingdom 18 March 2027 — Leeds, Howard Assembly Room, United Kingdom 19 March 2027 — Glasgow, Saint Luke’s, United Kingdom 20 March 2027 — Edinburgh, The Queen’s Hall, United Kingdom ‘A Date With Depeche Mode’ album The tour celebrates the launch of Nouvelle Vague’s new album “A Date With Depeche Mode.” The set focuses on Depeche Mode material reworked in the band’s bossa nova and lounge idiom. Depeche Mode and Nouvelle Vague have crossed paths before. The band’s third album, “3” (2009), included a version of “Master and Servant” sung by Depeche Mode’s Martin Gore with Nouvelle Vague vocalist Mélanie Pain. That album also featured Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen, Terry Hall of The Specials, and Barry Adamson. For this new album the band reworked thirteen iconic Depeche Mode songs. The whole was recorded in Rio with Brazilian musicians. The first single from “A Date with Depeche Mode” is a duet of “Enjoy the Silence” performed by Skye Edwards (Morcheeba) and Larry Love (Alabama 3) alongside Nouvelle Vague. About Nouvelle Vague Nouvelle Vague is a French covers project formed in Paris in 2003 by producers Marc Collin and Olivier Libaux. The name plays on three references at once: the French New Wave cinema of the 1960s, the new-wave music the band covers, and bossa nova. Collin’s idea was to record Joy Division’s “Love Will Tear Us Apart” in a bossa nova arrangement; the duo then recorded versions of Depeche Mode’s “Just Can’t Get Enough” and The Clash’s “The Guns of Brixton” and assembled a debut over roughly eight months. The self-titled debut album “Nouvelle Vague” was released in 2004 on Peacefrog and reworked songs by acts including XTC, Modern English, Killing Joke, The Clash, Joy Division, Tuxedomoon, The Cure and The Undertones. The second album, “Bande à Part”, followed in 2006 and included versions of Buzzcocks’ “Ever Fallen in Love”, New Order’s “Blue Monday”, Echo & the Bunnymen’s “The Killing Moon” and Blondie’s “Heart of Glass.” The band’s third album, “3” (2009), brought in guest vocalists linked with the original songs, including Martin Gore, Ian McCulloch, Terry Hall and Barry Adamson. “Couleurs sur Paris” (2010) collected French-language remakes with guests such as Vanessa Paradis and Cœur de pirate. The project is known for a rotating cast of mostly female vocalists, several of whom went on to solo careers, including Camille, Phoebe Killdeer, Mélanie Pain, Nadéah Miranda and Élodie Frégé. Marc Collin also released “Hollywood, mon amour” (2008), applying the same method to 1980s film-soundtrack songs. After “3” and “Couleurs sur Paris,” the band reduced its activity before returning with the EP “Athol Brose” and the album “I Could Be Happy” in 2016. Olivier Libaux died in 2021, and Collin has continued to lead the project live. The 2027 UK tour, “A Date With Depeche Mode,” ties the band’s covers approach to a new album built around Depeche Mode’s catalogue.
items._cn_summary: 法国翻唱项目Nouvelle Vague宣布2027年3月英国巡演，配套发行新专辑《A Date With Depeche Mode》，将Depeche Mode的十三首作品以bossa nova与lounge风格重新编排。项目由Marc Collin与已故的Olivier Libaux于2003年创立，理念是将后朋克与新浪潮歌曲以bossa nova方式重塑，并在巴西里约与当地音乐人合作录制。风格上涉及世界音乐元素与后朋克/暗潮素材的跨界融合，翻唱对象包括Depeche Mode、Joy Division、The Clash等。但整体定位偏向轻量化的lounge/翻唱路线，缺乏深度实验性，原创性有限。

items.body:
Low-key cult Japanese house entity Shin Watanabe trades in pure, redlit deep house sleaze on a substantial debut payload for L.I.E.S.

‘Red Zone-Ethos Mama Trax’ arrives in the wake of Watanabe’s introductory ‘Album 1986’ (Hot Street Records, 2025) with a sureshot affirmation of his greazy steez up-to-the-hilt on 13 ‘floor-ready jams. The spectres of earliest Chi and NYC house are summoned with strong attention to the sound’s subtle variegation and fine grasp of its raw but classy hallmarks, or more simply what makes it endure in the dance floor’s collective imagination.

Tune to tune he pinpoints the sound coming into its own from a blend of prevailing disco, industrial, soul and synth-pop touchstones, and with particular emphasis on its sinuous, psychosexual thirst/thrust. Shake  stick and you’ll hit an ace anywhere across the set, from the haughty stride and belting vox of pt. VI thru the sexy Lynchian chords of pt. III, to DJ Pierre-esque percolations in pt. I, a Burrell Brothers-like pt. II, the body-floatigb warehouse sassy of pt. VII, and Virgo Fpur styles on pt. X.
items._cn_summary: 日本制作人Shin Watanabe在地下厂牌L.I.E.S.发行的首张全长专辑，定位于芝加哥与纽约早期deep house的回溯与延伸。十三首俱乐部导向的作品融合了disco、industrial、soul与synth-pop等元素，强调律动感与暗色调氛围。评论提及DJ Pierre的酸屋律动、Virgo Four的经典风格以及Burrell Brothers式的质感，表明其美学取向偏向对经典house传统的致敬与再现，而非前沿实验。L.I.E.S.作为独立地下厂牌保证了发行的非商业定位，但整体风格仍属于传统deep house范畴，在创新性与跨类型融合方面有限，与实验电子、IDM、暗潮等前卫取向距离较远。日本地区出品的属性为其带来一定的文化独特性加分。

items.body:
True skool Chicago house don Mark Grusane packs inch-tight jakbeat budge and hypnotic depth on a definitive 6-track statement for his label, Disctechno and FFO Traxx, Adonis, Jamal Moss

A Windy City staple who has been DJing since the early ‘90s, and producing for over 20 years, Grusane’s experienced touch is tangible on all six tracky jams of ‘A House of My Own’. It’s a low-key masterclass in finding variation within a style, working the ruddiest bass and reedy synths to the bone on the title tune, and going tripper with it on ‘Essence of Life (Afterhours Mix)’, with over-the-shoulder vocals that are removed on its brighter ‘Daytime Mix’, and replaced with weird chirrups. He brings the acid to a gnarly simmer on the cold beat track ‘Knock Knock, Who’s There’, and taps a classic vein of Chi darkroom smut in the NSFW ace ‘Love and Lust (Explicit Lyrics)’, beside the filthy buck of ‘Jack Your Ass’.
items._cn_summary: Mark Grusane是芝加哥地下House领域的资深制作人，此专辑收录六首曲目，以紧凑的Jakbeat节拍和催眠式纵深感为基调。音乐风格扎根于芝加哥House传统，融合酸涩的Acid 303元素、暗室氛围以及挑逗性人声采样，部分曲目在日间与深夜混音版本之间探索情绪对比。制作扎实，体现了作者二十余年的舞曲经验，但在声音设计层面偏重类型内的常规演绎，未见显著的实验性突破或跨领域融合。作为独立厂牌Disctechno发行的地下电子舞曲，其气质偏向俱乐部舞池实用主义，与用户偏好的实验性电子、IDM、Ambient、Glitch等方向有一定距离，但同属电子大类。

items.body:
After curating beloved annual edits comps for years, Latane Hughes and Billy Scher are now making their own music with the help of producer Miles Felix.

"Look, there are a lot of DJ duos in Brooklyn. Most of them are fine. Fundido are the kind who’ve been doing the good work for 10 years. What started as euphoric, after-band free-for-alls in the front room at Baby’s All Right now takes place in increasingly bigger rooms, further afield, regulars and new faces side by side. It’s a music lover’s paradise and a responsible adult’s worst nightmare.

“Get A Grip” felt almost purpose-built for DFA: four-on-the-floor drums, a synth that maws away your inhibitions, a vocal from Emma Dufaux that closes the deal. It’s really good.

The 12” gives you four ways to hear it: the Original Mix, a Bliss Mix (less maw), and remixes from rising stars Make A Dance and Asa Tate. These guys spent a decade learning what makes people lose themselves and keep coming back. Now they’re making the tracks to match."
items._cn_summary: Fundido 是一支来自布鲁克林的 DJ 组合，拥有十年俱乐部经验。《Get A Grip》是一首四拍底的舞曲电子作品，合成器音色突出，搭配 Emma Dufaux 的人声，整体偏向俱乐部舞曲风格。12寸黑胶包含原版、Bliss Mix 以及 Make A Dance 和 Asa Tate 的混音版本。该作品风格偏向主流舞曲领域，旋律感和律动感突出，但缺乏实验性声响设计、IDM式的解构或暗潮/工业的侵略性元素。虽然具备电子音乐属性，但更接近商业化俱乐部舞曲而非用户偏好的实验/前卫/IDM方向。来自布鲁克林独立场景为其增添一定地下色彩，但音乐本身的可听性与商业亲和力较强，创新性有限。
