items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Being the same quartet that would later make two masterpieces of 70s European fusion, and now with the presence of Jukka Tolonen, Tombstone Valentine, their second album surprises as a misstep, a transitional album let's say, in which there are nevertheless interesting discoveries, such as the homonymous theme, which with the accordion of Kalevi Nyqvist and the organ achieved a certain dreamlike atmosphere that they would later enhance.In Gratitude! is a blues song still influenced by Steve Wingwood. Frederick & Bill is good in a loose, psychedelic style, with Pekka Pohjola demonstrating his skill on bass and violin... but still without that Finnish recipe, since the lack of focus and a common thread is what makes this second album fall apart. Wishful Thinker and Autograph share a country style almost reminiscent of Bob Dylan.1936 Lost in the Snow is an instrumental jazz ballad with a certain mysterious air that saves it...because then Let the World Ramble On returns to pop.As on the previous album, they felt most comfortable and sounded best in jazz, before discovering the alchemy present on later albums. For America is pure jazz with Jukka Tolonen on guitar, Jukka Gustavson on piano, Pekka Pohjola on bass, and of course Ronnie �sterberg on drums.Captain Supernatural, like End, already contains at times that atonal keyboard that goes beyond the margin, that deep sung note...that shadow that clouds the sun like an eclipse and that would bring the fairies.
items._cn_summary: WIGWAM乐队1970年发行的第二张专辑《Tombstone Valentine》定位为爵士摇滚融合。乐评将其描述为乐队在创作巅峰之前的过渡性作品，称其存在缺乏焦点与主线的问题。专辑风格呈现多样性：同名曲中手风琴与管风琴营造出梦幻氛围，For America展现纯正爵士底蕴，Captain Supernatural已显露无调性键盘的实验萌芽。然而整体上融合了民谣、布鲁斯、乡村甚至流行元素，距离真正的前卫实验尚有距离。作为芬兰乐队的早期作品，虽有北欧爵士摇滚的特质，但尚未形成成熟的个人风格，对追求学院派爵士、自由即兴或前卫实验的听众而言，实验性和深度均有不足。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Three astute reasons why the Prog Rogue has committed to this artist's music to sit among his favourites, a freedom of choice that music can surely always provide. Firstly, Geoff is an accomplished musician, mastering a massive library of sounds on his electronic gear, including many organic instruments as well and composing flawlessly intricate specimens of medieval-tinged music. Secondly, he is evidently an avid historian as well, another personal liberty that one can learn from the past in order to better understand the future. His stunning previous opus, the magnificent "K of A" (Katherine of Aragon) was dutifully reviewed and honored with the entire starry spectrum at my disposal. Last but not least , I have been an openly critical of the relative disuse of an instrument that , in my humblest of opinions deserves a much better fate, not just in progressive rock but in all forms of music in general. I have named The Harpsichord. This masterful opus has plenty enough to satiate my very dry wishing well, and, just for that alone , I am ecstatic. The twenty-three tracks presented here feel like pages from a long-lost notebook, perhaps even recently discovered in some secret library , comments from the hand of the hapless Anne Boleyn, she of Rick Wakeman fame and Henry VII shame. Reading like a diary of her ordeal, personal moments of her trials and tribulations, her innermost thoughts on her own failings as well as the conspiratorial nature of the Tudor court, all translated into instrumental music of the very highest order. As such, an in-depth track-by-track descriptive would be a completely foolhardy exercise in tedious complication, as this kind of work requires the classic concentrated effort of sitting comfortably with headphones on, reading the copious notes as if a history book and letting go of the outside world entirely. From the onset of the exquisite opener "From Blickling to Hever" and arriving 42 minutes later to the fateful "I am Come Hither to Die", the listener is duty-bound to let the mind wander through the various scenes, most of them well within the 1-2 minutes in length, literally expressing my favourite definition of prog "Music for the imaginary movie in your own mind". The imagination of the artist begets the thoughts of the individual audience member. Is there any finer form of relationship ?That glorious crispness offered by the baroque harpsichord resonates on a multitude of attractive and densely melodic oddments ("We Three Boleyn, la Petite Boulain, My Lord Percy, An Injured Heart, Masque Dance, Patience Will Be My Song, A New Order, and Still I Will Prevail) , each gem played with passion, flair and heartfelt commitment. Organ and synthesized flute also appear regularly, so as to keep the flow of inspiration in a state of palpitating reverence, often embedded with orchestration. The ornate piano does take the spotlight on delicate pieces like "Learning Grounds", "The Lady Anne (Henry's Obsession)" and "Elizabeth" (many seem to forget that Elizabeth I was surely one the of the greatest monarchs in history and the daughter of Anne Boleyn), both melodies crushingly haunting as well as utterly memorable. Yet, the piano on the two final pieces , the achingly harrowing "All This for Such a Little Neck " and the previously mentioned finale verges on genius and easily on par with the golden caped Yes legend. There are also intense moments of emotion , such as on the glittering melancholia of "We Shall Have Sons" where Proudley gets to express his arrangement savvy on orchestrating grandiose effects. The galloping horses' effect on "Riding Out to Hever" has all the instincts of a fox on the run (Anne being the poor animal) with harrowing choir work to add some ominous doom to the chase. "Procession" feels like a scene from "Robin Hood", pageantry on full sonic display, church organ blaring. On "Traitor's Gate", the orchestral foundation skillfully demonstrates the ordeal of travelling to her fate, the tragic and deadly barge navigation to the Tower where Anne Boleyn will ultimately lose her head. The crow has the last word. Needless to say, fans of exquisite music need to search this one out, though all there of Geoff's albums are required ownership and eternal enjoyment. Coming in a masterful 52-page book , this is not just your usual modern stream download but an outright collector's item, whether historian or prog fan (I am lucky to be both) where either can find equal amounts of divinely inspired pleasure. Very proud of you, Geoff, your music really touches my soul ! Music like this only comes around a few times in life, it needs to be enjoyed while you can. 5 twists of fate
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Geoff Proudley的跨界前卫摇滚作品，以英国都铎王朝安妮·博林的历史故事为概念框架。音乐以中世纪与巴洛克风格为基调，大量使用羽管键琴、管风琴、合成长笛及管弦乐配器，融合电子设备与原声乐器，呈现二十三段短小的音画篇章。整体定位偏向历史叙事型概念专辑，强调旋律性与氛围营造，在器乐编排上注重巴洛克音色的精致表达。虽然有电子与原声乐器的融合尝试，但整体仍属保守的历史复兴风格，实验性、前卫性元素有限，与当代实验音乐、学院爵士、电子实验、暗潮等方向距离较远，适合偏好传统前卫摇滚与古典复兴的听众。

items.body:
After the cataclysm of their Om debut, Al Cisneros & Chris Hakius come right down with its hypnotic follow-up, now returned to circulation on its 20th anniversary FFO Sleep, Earth, Popol Vuh.

‘Conference of the Birds’ (2006) had big boots to fill after Om’s immense 2005 debut ‘Variations on a Theme’, so they effectively slipped into a pair of sandals instead, feeling the sand between their toes on a pair of more desert oriented jams. Still squinting at durational horizons, they take all the time needed - up to and over 15 mins per side - to concentrate on more brooding strains of modal, psych-inflected stoner rock that works it magic more subtly. 

The hairy nads-out appeal of their previous side, and the grungier tone of their earlier, cult work as Sleep is swapped out for mantric, pentatonic riffs and sway that channel the blues via Ethiopian music, kosmiche and hard rock in ‘At Giza’, placing Cisneros’ monotonic vox higher in the mix over shimmering backdrop of hazed hi-hats and uncurling bassline yoked with a tongue-tip tension.

But fret not heavy riff fiends, for that all comes with ‘Flight of the Eagle’, which effectively picks up where ‘Variation…’ left off, locking hard into a mantric cycle where Hakius’ damn slow but tight offbeat shuffles and the feedback worship riffs hold an intensity that breaks upward half way and soars in tumbling gyres to the end.
items._cn_summary: OM由Al Cisneros与Chris Hakius组成，二人此前是传奇doom金属乐队Sleep的成员。这张2006年发行的专辑是他们的第二张全长作品，以冥想式的滞重摇滚为基调，融合了埃塞俄比亚调式音乐、宇宙摇滚与硬摇滚元素。专辑仅收录两首曲目，每首时长超过十五分钟，以五声音阶重复乐句和极缓节奏构建出催眠般的声音景观。贝斯线条与人声在混音中占据主导，鼓点以松散的切分支撑整体律动。整体风格介于迷幻摇滚与东方冥想音乐之间，强调极简重复与氛围营造，弱化了传统stoner rock的粗粝感。该作由独立厂牌Drag City发行，在doom/stoner范畴内具有鲜明的跨文化融合实验色彩。

items.body: Review by andrea — Corporesano took form in Brescia in 2015 and soon started composing original music inspired by seventies prog. In 2019 they released an interesting eponymous debut album on the Mellow Records label with a line up featuring Lorenzo Ussoli (keyboards, backing vocals), Francesco Marchina Ares (lead and backing vocals), Simone Sandrini (guitars), Giordano Porta (bass) and Marco Dolfini (drums, percussion, backing vocals). Their music is dreamy, soft and pleasant though not particularly challenging. The art work by Giordano Porta, inspired by the fantastic landscapes by Roger Dean, tries to describe the musical and lyrical content...The opener "Alle porte di Zion" (At the gates of Zion) is a slow, reflective piece that evokes the end of a man's earthly journey at the gates of Zion and his liberation from pain, which leads to a state of infinite peace. It's an ideal place, where you can listen to music while sitting on green meadows and get lost in a deep sense of well-being surrounded by a flow of transforming souls..."Labirinti retorici" (Rhetorical labyrinths) is an introspective and dreamy piece where music and lyrics evoke the figure of a man in search of inspiration, lost chasing his fantasies through the alleys of an ancient city or in splendid gardens (the lyrics refer to the Boboli Gardens in Florence, a large park originally designed as the garden of the Medici family's Pitti Palace in the mid-16th century that houses statues of various styles and periods, large fountains, and artificial grottoes). Then, the protagonist finds himself composing melodies on the beach in Rimini, applauded only by dolphins. Useless thoughts are dispersed by a wind that carries with it the voices of insensitive sirens..."Nel bozzolo" (In the cocoon) tells the story of a man who can't find his place in a shattered, hopeless world and withdraws into himself. He seeks protection in a cocoon where he can sleep and dream. Upon awakening, however, a metamorphosis occurs: the cocoon opens, and the protagonist soars like a butterfly, reflecting on his past and trying to savour the nectar of life, leaving behind the shards of his shell..."Statim vivus fierem" (I would immediately become alive) is an introspective piece, titled in Latin, that speaks of the need for reconciliation between humanity and nature. Under a starry sky in the Taiga, the protagonist experiences visions that blur with reality. In that place, he feels part of an ancestral history and in balance with the universe..."Sulle rive del fiume Giordano" (On the banks of the Jordan river) describes a traveller sitting in silence on the banks of the Jordan river, a river that flows through the tormented lands of the Middle East and ends into the Dead Sea. The protagonist dives into its waters, and when he resurfaces, time and space lose all meaning for him. He experiences an angelic peace and is overcome by celestial visions..."Lupo solitario" (Lone wolf) describes a man with a rebellious spirit who reflects on his past and his mistakes. Now he realises that he must move forward with humility and courage, without heeding siren songs that might divert his path. For him it's time to start over and make sense of his new role as a father, with transparency and honesty...In "Onda inarrestabile" (Unstoppable wave) the music and lyrics evoke a powerful wave, capable of tuning cells, causing chaos, and instilling vibrations, vertigo and happiness. The lyrics were partially inspired by "The Sirius Mystery", a book by Robert K. G. Temple supporting the pseudoscientific ancient astronauts hypothesis that intelligent extra-terrestrial beings visited the Earth and made contact with humans in antiquity and prehistoric times..."La zavorra inutile" (The useless ballast) evokes the image of a man crushed by an unbearable weight. What weighs him down is anxiety about the future and regrets about a past that can never return. To move forward, he clings to the habits, judgments, and clich�s that give him security. When a memory of childhood games timidly surfaces, however, the protagonist senses that within him there is still a great life force and an ocean of energy. He regains his balance and forgets the fears of the future and the regrets of the past to live in the flow of the present, the only true aspect of reality..."Lo spirito della montagna" (The spirit of the mountain) describes the strength and beauty of nature by identifying with the benign spirit of a mountain that teaches us to honour life. The spirt bestows peace, silence, and serenity upon those who appreciate it and its magical songs resonate throughout the valley, bringing joy to those who listen...The closing track, "I venti dell'inverno" (The winds of Winter), is a piece suspended between nostalgia and hope for the future. The protagonist turns his thoughts to a past love, hoping that the sweet moments they shared will return. He feels almost swallowed up in a dark vortex where icy winds blow. Then, he becomes aware of the need to overcome the past and look to the future with confidence. New encounters and new ideas can still shape a new path in his life...On the whole, a really good work that deserves listening to. Unfortunately the band split up soon after the album was released, but you never know. In Italian prog reunions can always happen.
items._cn_summary: Corporesano是2015年成立于意大利布雷西亚的摇滚乐团，2019年由独立厂牌Mellow Records发行首张同名专辑。音乐风格为传统意大利前卫摇滚，灵感来源于七十年代prog传统。整体气质梦幻、柔和、悦目，乐评人明确指出'并不特别具有挑战性'。专辑曲目以叙事性概念为主，歌词涉及梦境、自然、灵魂救赎等意象，配器包含键盘、电吉他、贝斯和鼓的经典编制。专辑封面由贝斯手Giordano Porta操刀，模仿Roger Dean的奇幻风景风格。音乐上属于温暖抒情的传统前卫路线，缺乏实验声响设计、电子元素、即兴段落或跨界融合，与用户偏好的实验前卫、学术爵士、电子、世界音乐及暗潮方向距离较远，属于主流前卫摇滚范畴内的舒适型作品。

items.body: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — I reviewed the DVD of this so heres the audio review. Right off the bat I can say that you are genuinely missing out if you have not seen the visual display on offer here, its mind blowing when the light show takes off especially the dazzling light displays on Run like Hell with a pyrotechnic ending that literally explodes the Pompeii collisseum. On Comfortably Numb we are treated to an eyeball searing laser show that is a feast for the eyes. One of These Days is incredible, with psychedelic strobe lights and Gilmour makes that slide guitar scream and howl, as good as the Pink Floyd days. High Hopes is beautifully performed with a clanging bell and soaring lead solo. There's great sax on Money also, a powerful performance. Gilmours voice is wonderful and he is joined by a brilliant band. The three singers take over on Great Gig in the Sky which is a different variation on Clare Torry. Its also great to hear Gilmours songs as I am not so familiar with these. I particularly like On an Island. The sound quality is excellent but again I rather watch this with the visuals as juxtaposed together its an enthralling experience. Overall this is a great concert worth devouring on DVD and has some fascinating special features.

items.body: Norwegian jazz pianist and composer Kjetil Andre Mulelid was born on February 4th 1991, in Hurdal, Norway. In 2014, he completed his studies at the Jazz program at Norwegian University of Science and Technology in Trondheim. Thereafter, he has been active with such bands as Kjemile, Wako and others, as well as his own work with Kjetil Mulelid Trio and his duo with Siril Malmedal Hauge. Hauge, a Norwegian jazz singer, was born on November 28th 1992. She was also educated on the jazz program at University of Science and Technology in Trondheim. In addition to heading projects such as Fieldfare and Wild Things Run Fast, she has collaberated with other bands and musicians. In 2010, she received the Norwegian Cultural Educational Council (dream scholarship). In recent years, Hauge and Mulelid have established themselves as prominent voices in the Norwegian music scene, with extensive touring, Spellmann nominations, and critically acclaimed releases, which have gained international attention. Hauge and Mulelid have made themselves known in the Norwegian music scene in recent years. With active touring, a Norwegian grammy award nomination, and several album releases praised by the worldwide press, they have distinguished themselves as a bold voice representing the Norwegian music in the 21st century. Since their studies in Trondheim, they have worked regularly together. Both together and individually, Hauge and Mulelid have become important artists of their generation. The two musicians have collaborated in various constellations since 2013, performing at festivals and venues across Norway, including through Siril's solo project. On March 17th, 2023, their debut duo album Blues and Bells (Grappa) was released. In autumn 2022, Hauge and Mulelid formally established their duo and since then they have developed their distinctive interplay and musical language through concerts in countries such as Japan, China, South Korea, Portugal, France, Romania and Norway. As the recording of Mulelid and Haugh below illustrates, they are perfectly suited for one another.

items.body:
Wiki returns with 'Right Away', a cloud rap/drill hybrid that's backed with the beatless slow-burner 'Park'.

It's hard to believe that it's been three years since we last heard from Wiki. He dropped '14K Figaro', going head-to-head with MIKE-collaborator Tony Seltzer and then went dark. Sure, he might have been spotted in 'Marty Supreme', but that hardly counts, does it? Well, 'Right Away' was worth the wait; production-wise it's a curiosity, rhythmically indebted to drill but lightened by Silky Johnson-style smeared samples. And Wiki's in his zone, twisting his tongue around the snaps like he's got a foot between Kodak Black and A$AP Rocky.

items.body:
Ditching the free jazz, at least for a spell, sax prodigy Zoh Amba follows their blistering deployments for Smalltown and Tzadik and collaborations with Wobbly, Chris Corsano and Bill Orcutt with an album of fragile indie Americana. Unexpected, for sure, but welcome - RIYL 'Eureka'-mode Jim O'Rourke, early Joanna Newsom, Bonnie 'Prince' Billy or Bill Callahan.

Still in their mid-20s, Amba has already lived a lifetime on the US improv scene, releasing so many records in the space of the last half-decade that it's easy to understand why they needed some downtime. The story goes that they were back in their hometown of Kingsport, Tennessee - the birthplace of horror legend Nick Castle, who played Michael Myers in the first 'Halloween' - when they were inspired to drop their horn and tinker with their old acoustic guitar, the first instrument they learned to play, way back when. The instrument itself isn't really the most unexpected thing about 'Eyes Full', though, most surprising is the way Amba approaches it. Although they're a seasoned free improv fixture, there's none of the expected aesthetics on show here; quite the opposite, in fact, the album sounds as if it's barely aware that Albert Ayler existed, instead spying classic Appalachian folk, Nashville alt-country and headsy indie-rock for its creative Cliff's Notes. 

Listen in carefully though and you'll be able to identify the same eccentric energy that coursed through last year's excellent 'Sun'. Amba's voice is immediately a draw, molded into a drawl of elongated vowels and half-tuned syllables that sounds as if it's locked into a lineage that you can easily trace back to Alan Lomax's American folk field recordings. And their performance on the guitar seems to work to accent that distinct phrasing, indebted to John Fahey and his acolytes in a way, but also purposefully rough around the edges, punk-y, even. There's something about the way Amba is able to stab at the strings and turn the guitar into a percussive instrument for a second before lurching it back to melody that betrays their background. And their choice of collaborators is also key: they're backed up on 'Eyes Full' by drummer Jim White and their bestie Kevin Hyland on electric guitar, and the songs evolved through session after session of rehearsals. 

So there's a tightness here that's somehow shaped into pop that's ragged enough to feel fresh, vital and different. Lead single 'Another Time' will help you understand what planet they're on, with Amba's tactile strums and throaty intimacies wrapped casually around their collaborators' chic scaffolding. "In another lifetime, I take you to the sea," they half-screech. "I show you honey, how sweet that soul's meant to be." And on 'Southern Soil', they reflect on the history of small town, working class folk music in America, taking the lead with an acrobatic vocal performance that sounds as if it belongs in church. Even if you're missing the old Amba, there's a glimmer of improv running through 'Child You'll See' just for the heads, when their jangling guitar is swallowed by filthy reverb trails and supplanted by drones and pained sax wails. Very nice.
items._cn_summary: Zoh Amba是活跃于自由即兴领域的萨克斯演奏者，曾在Tzadik、Smalltown等厂牌发行作品，并与Bill Orcutt、Chris Corsano等合作。《Eyes Full》标志着其从自由爵士转向独立美式民谣，以原声吉他为核心，融入阿巴拉契亚民谣、纳什维尔另类乡村及独立摇滚元素。人声风格粗粝而具教堂感，吉他演奏受John Fahey影响但带有刻意粗粝的朋克色彩。乐手阵容包括鼓手Jim White和吉他手Kevin Hyland。整体虽保留了部分即兴乐手的独特律动和非常规感，但本质上是一张美式民谣/另类乡村作品，与实验、自由爵士、电子等核心审美方向距离较远。

items.body:
YOUTH return with a second dose of inexorable House pressure from Paul Bennett aka Duster Valentine, primed for DJs and dancers and a sureshot tip FFO Michael J. Blood, Todd Terry, Ron Trent, Anthony “Shake” Shakir, DJ Sprinkles…

Aye it’s another haul of hard hitting gems pressed to vinyl for the first time, a love note to formative years in the ‘80s and early ‘90s, off his chops at The Haçienda and other legendary Manchester spots. It’s a masterclass in demonstrating the flavours-within-a-theme that emerged from the Chi, 313, and NYC during that pivotal era, and which would eventually light the touch paper of a UK club revolution. 

In Duster Valentine’s hands, the sound is presented stripped to salient fundamentals, before it went commercial, ranging from sampler-knuckling garage-house stabbers thru haughty canter and plushest, pendulous grooves. He homes in hard on the exact point when hip hop and electro gave way to house in the Todd Terry-via-Pal Joey style jam ‘Getting’ Dub’, and gives a big salute to Chez N Trent’s rugged, chord-riding haughtiness via Levon Vincent in ‘Hit Me From Behind’.

‘Strobelight Honnies’ leans into the sound’s deepest ends with a perfectly weighted bassline, cold drums and sublime string tension dubbed with hypnotic elegance, where ‘The KatG Chord’ follows with shimmers of Anthony Shakir via Michael J Blood. Suffice it to say they’re all essential and bang on the dollar if you know what’s good.

100% perlers!
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国制作人Duster Valentine（Paul Bennett）发行的怀旧向浩室舞曲，根植于1980年代末至1990年代初芝加哥、底特律与纽约的经典浩室传统，风格涵盖车库浩室、深层浩室与俱乐部舞曲。评论将其与Todd Terry、Ron Trent、Anthony Shakir、DJ Sprinkles等老派制作人并列，强调对黄金时代俱乐部声响的忠实复刻。制作手法偏向精简纯粹，注重律动与贝斯线的分量感，整体定位明确指向DJ与舞池场景。该专辑在电子音乐大类下，但属于传统俱乐部浩室范畴，与实验电子、前卫即兴、IDM、氛围等方向有较大距离，缺乏明显的实验性或跨类型融合元素。

items.body:
Someone had to do it: Ennio Morricone and co.’s creepy OST for Pier Paolo Pasolini’s scandalous ’75 film rendition of the notorious novel ‘120 Days of Sodom’, by Marquis De Sade, lands on arch industrialist label, Cold Spring. Mangia!

Next in the label’s line of cult scores, after ‘Decoder’ and Psychic TV’s ‘A Prayer for Derek Jarman’, comes this deeply uneasy score to Pasolini’s infamous enactment of De Sade’s pornographic dystopia-come-study of male power dynamics. Whether you’ve seen it or not, the book and film’s reputation precedes them as both a piece of pure, unadulterated filth, or handy encyclopaedia of depravity, depending on one’s take. Each to their own, as one might say, but fuck me: without going into snuff or dark web realms, the imagery is about as mad as it gets. Which all makes the soundtrack of breezy to discordant chamber classical (Bach, Chopin, Orff, Puccini, and Graziosi) and parlour jazz arrangements register even harder in the memory, especially when paired with its scenes representing everything from coprophilia to bestiality, incest, and worse.
items._cn_summary: 该专辑是埃尼奥·莫里科内为帕索里尼争议性电影《萨罗》所创作的配乐，由英国独立厂牌Cold Spring发行。音乐内容以巴赫、肖邦、奥尔夫、普契尼及格拉齐奥西的室内古典作品与沙龙爵士改编为主，属于传统古典与轻量级爵士范畴，并非当代古典或实验作曲。评论着重描述了轻快音乐与极端影像之间的反差所产生的记忆冲击，这一策展视角本身具有一定的艺术张力，但音乐本体并不具备实验性、噪音性或暗潮工业属性。整体而言，这张原声带与实验、前卫、暗潮、学院爵士等核心偏好之间存在较大距离，其艺术价值更多体现在语境与反差层面。

items.body: Angelique Kidjo – Hope!! (Parlophone/Warner Music, 2026) Angélique Kidjo’s Hope!! , her joyful 16-track Afropop set spiced with neosoul, Afrobeats and other popular music influences features a wide range of collaborators, including Pharrell Williams, Quavo, Ayra Starr, Davido, Nile Rodgers, Charlie Wilson, IZA, and PJ Morton. Pharrell produced three songs. Their collaboration began after Pharrell invited Kidjo to perform at his Grace For The World concert in St. Peter’s Square in Vatican City in September 2025. That meeting led to three original songs written and produced in Pharrell’s Paris studio with Kidjo’s voice and style in mind. Among them, “For Me” features Charlie Wilson and focuses on self-celebration in the face of adversity. “No Stopping Us” grew out of a conversation between Kidjo and Pharrell about social change. Meanwhile, “Bando,” which also features Quavo and vocals from Pharrell, draws on the slang term for an abandoned house and points to the street origins of popular trends. Elsewhere, the album is dedicated to Kidjo’s late mother, Yvonne. According to Kidjo, her mother’s favorite song was the moving “Malaika,” which closes the album in an orchestral version arranged by Derrick Hodge and featuring French singer Florent Pagny. Recorded in Paris and Los Angeles over the past three years, Hope!! also includes contributions from The Cavemen on “I’m On Fire,” Fally Ipupa on “Nadi Balance,” Sheila Maurice-Grey of Kokoroko, Dadju on “Superwoman,” and Diamond Platnumz on “Kakua.” In addition, Brazilian artist IZA appears on the “Oyaya.” The album also features “Sunlight To My Soul,” written by Diane Warren, as well as performances by the Soweto Gospel Choir, who previously worked with Kidjo at a 2003 Nelson Mandela benefit concert. Kidjo said the project reflects a message of hope and human connection at a time of growing division. In that spirit, the album continues a career that has paired music with activism, including her work through the Batonga Foundation and as a UNICEF goodwill ambassador. Kidjo’s previous album was her 2021 Grammy-winning album Mother Nature . Buy Hope!!
items._cn_summary: 安琪莉克·琪蒂欧（Angelique Kidjo）来自贝宁的第十六张专辑《Hope!!》是一部16首作品的Afropop集合，融合neosoul、Afrobeats及多种流行音乐元素。专辑由华纳音乐旗下Parlophone发行，邀请了Pharrell Williams、Quavo、Davido、IZA等多位主流艺人参与，Pharrell在巴黎工作室制作了三首原创歌曲。专辑向已故母亲致敬，延续了琪蒂欧将音乐与社会行动主义结合的路线，包括巴东加基金会及联合国儿童基金会亲善大使工作。整体制作偏商业化主流定位，跨文化协作丰富但缺乏深层实验性或前卫元素，与实验/学院派爵士/电子等深度聆听路线距离较远。

items._cn_summary: Pink Floyd 1973年发行的概念专辑《The Dark Side of the Moon》，属于迷幻与太空摇滚领域，融合前卫摇滚、电子音效、环境音景及管弦乐元素，以连续不间断的曲目编排探讨时间、死亡、疯狂与金钱等主题。制作中运用早期合成器、音效循环与多轨录音技术，包含被认为是首批电子循环音乐的片段之一，在声音设计与电子元素引入摇滚框架方面具有历史性开创意义。然而该专辑是商业史上最畅销的唱片之一，由主流厂牌发行，定位偏向大众经典而非小众实验前沿。相较于当代实验音乐、前卫爵士和电子音乐的前沿探索，其手法在整体编曲与结构上仍属传统，实验性更多局限在摇滚范畴内。乐评文本以哲学反思和自我提问为主，偏向个人化聆听引导而非专业音乐分析，且末尾内容存在截断。

items.body:
With third album If This Is It, DJ Seinfeld (Armand Jakobsson) refines his emotional, club-leaning sound across nostalgic house, UKG, and 2000s-tinged trance.

"The 12-track LP - featuring SG Lewis, Confidence Man, TS Graye, Dan Whitlam, ARY, “Norwegian pop witch” Moyka, and Barry Can’t Swim affiliate just lil - explores letting go in a world that can often feel overwhelming.

“A million ideas turned into a few, a few turned into no ideas at all, and no ideas eventually turned into one” says Jakobsson of the album, which he began the week his acclaimed 2021 record Mirrors was released. “Through writing it, I’ve tried to turn long-held anxieties into acceptance, and I hope listeners can take their own meaning from it”."

items.body:
Wino finally drop the long-teased label debut of Dublin pal Officer John, operating with a sort of dusted trip hop energy that starts off full of baggy swagger and gets more blissed as we go, finishing off with a remix from long serving label captain Morgan Buckley. 

Wino cap off an imperial 2025 with a 6 track peach from Niall Rogers aka Officer John, opening with sleeper hit ‘Stay’ that comes like The Beta Band riffing on MBV’s ‘soon’, before ‘Pass’ takes us to a more downbeat landscape just north of A.S.O., while ‘Handle’ feels like a late summer afternoon soundtracked by some Escho ace. To end, Morgan Buckley ups the funky drummer and stutters the vox for a classic slice of 90’s balearic-pop.

It’s all so naggingly ear-wormy and achingly familiar that it already feels like a classic. Sleep and, um, weep?!
items._cn_summary: 这张六曲EP由都柏林音乐人Officer John（Niall Rogers）在独立小厂牌Wino发行，整体定位于trip hop与balearic-pop的交汇地带。作品以dusty质感的电子声响为基底，融合了90年代brit-pop的松弛律动与Balearic流行的余韵，参考了The Beta Band的随性气质和MBV式的情绪化音墙。Morgan Buckley的混音版收尾加入了funky drummer的碎拍节奏与人声切碎处理。整张专辑呈现出舒适怀旧的听感，旋律易记但缺乏实验性突破，声音美学偏向于对经典的致敬与复刻，与前卫电子、即兴爵士或暗潮实验等领域的距离较为明显。

items.body: Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm “Mac” Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms. Taped at the height of Dr. John’s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close. A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac’s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions. Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic “Iko, Iko,” a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast “Qualified,” wherein the singer warns, “I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.” Any Dr. John fan will recognize “I Walk on Guilded Splinters,” a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper’s immersion in “funknology” (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: “Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.” Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own “Sweet Home New Orleans” and “Goin’ Back to New Orleans,” and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington’s “I'm Gonna Go Fishin’.” Among other gems are Mac’s Top–10 hit “Right Place, Wrong Time,” and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King’s “Big Chief,” another Mardi Gras burner. Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, “I always play a little bit of everything. I think that’s what music’s about: a little bit of somethin’ old, somethin’ in the middle, somethin’ new, and somethin’ as yet uncreated.” Dr John's’s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of At the Rockpalast is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, “If you’re gonna get off on somethin’ you don’t need to know nothin’ about it. Music is a universal language.” Dr. John (Mac Rebennack) - Things Happen That Way (Review) Lakou Mizik - HaitiNola (Review)

items.body: A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared, seemingly from nowhere. From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music opened a window on something so many didn’t even know existed to show that country music had never been a white preserve. That album was a few years before the Carolina Chocolate Drops burst on the scene, reclaiming the Black heritage in country and string band music, plus a great deal more. Genuine Negro Jig , their third release, saw them move up to the prestigious Nonesuch label, a powerful artistic imprimatur, winning them a Grammy for an album very far removed from the mainstream. Genuine Negro Jig (15th Anniversary Edition) by Carolina Chocolate Drops This expanded 15th anniversary edition marks a good time to look back at the band’s mix of Piedmont string band and traditional music, nestling beside early 20th century blues, and a few original and modern pieces in the mix (like the Tom Waits-penned “Trampled Rose”). The trio roared into the music, playing it with fire and unalloyed joy – yet also with plenty of subtlety; list to “Snowden’s Jig (Genuine Negro Jig)” for a taste of how the members worked together. For many, this would have been the first opportunity to hear Rhiannon Giddens – quite a big global star these days – and Don Flemons, as well as Sule Greg Wilson, standard bears for an idea whose time had come. This is an album very much worth of this deluxe reissue treatment, a real landmark, not simply for the career of the Carolina Chocolate Drops, but for roots music in general. And people responded – hence that Grammy. Genuine Negro Jig (15th Anniversary Edition) by Carolina Chocolate Drops There are plenty of bonus tracks here, all worth hearing, but the real meat is on the original release. There’s the delicious, sultry blues of “Why Don’t You Do Right?”, the wild string band abandon of “Cindy Gal,” Giddens’s unaccompanied voice on “Reynardine,” and the full-tilt race through “Sandy Boys.” It’s exhilarating, but so much more. There’s deep thought given to the arrangements and the interplay between instruments and voices. Genuine Negro Jig (15th Anniversary Edition) by Carolina Chocolate Drops The band aren’t purists. They don’t need to be. Whatever the sources for the material, they transform it and turn it into something that speaks with their voice. Released a decade after From Where I Stand , Genuine Negro Jig was a bold manifesto that still speaks loudly today. It is an album very much worth of this deluxe reissue, waiting for a new audience to discover. Find the artists online.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Carolina Chocolate Drops演绎，融合了皮埃蒙特弦乐传统、早期二十世纪布鲁斯以及部分原创和现代作品，其中包括Tom Waits创作的"Trampled Rose"。乐队由Rhiannon Giddens、Dom Flemons和Sule Greg Wilson组成，致力于重新发掘黑人在乡村音乐和弦乐传统中的历史遗产。乐评指出乐队演奏充满活力，编曲层次丰富，但并非纯粹的复古复刻，而是以当代视角转化传统素材。专辑获格莱美奖，由知名独立厂牌Nonesuch发行。整体而言，这是一张扎根于美国南方民谣与弦乐传统的作品，在传统与现代之间寻找平衡，但在风格上与实验、前卫、爵士、电子等方向相距较远，更偏向美国本土根源音乐范畴。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Chasing the Hydra" is the fifth full-length studio album by US, Florida based heavy/power metal actCrimson Glory. The album was released through BraveWords Records in April 2026. It's the successorto "Astronomica" from September 1999, so it's no less than 27 years down the line from the lastalbum release. Although Crimson Glory released a few singles in the early 2010s and played somesporadic shows (in the years 2005-2013) it wasn't until 2023 that they reunited for real and broughtin the two missing pieces for their lineup in guitarist Mark Borgmeyer and lead vocalist TravisWills (original singer Midnight died in 2009). Ideas for new material also began to appear andfinally after 27 years "Chasing the Hydra" is here.Not surprisingly Crimson Glory have returned to the US power/heavy metal music style of their1986-1988 heyday and the albums "Crimson Glory" (1986) and "Transcendence" (1988) and they don'tonce find inspiration in their next two albums "Strange And Beautiful" (1991) and "Astronomica"(1999), both of which are usually not lauded by their fan base. Just as the case was on the mid- tolate-1980s releases there is a slight progressive metal touch to the proceedings, but it's not adominant trait and Crimson Glory are generally a more straight forward US power/heavy metal act,although in the more sophisticated end of the scale. Wills is a skilled vocalist who can sing bothmid-range rough vocals and higher pitched screaming vocals. It was always going to be an impossibletask to replace Midnight because of his unique voice and piercing helium screams, and Willsthankfully don't try to replicate the past but instead brings his own vocal style and voice to thetable and they work perfectly with the instrumental part of "Chasing the Hydra"."Chasing the Hydra" features a powerful, clear, and detailed sound production and it's a sound whichis perfect for the material. Although Crimson Glory was overall never the most unique sounding bandon the US power/heavy metal scene, and especially Queensr'che always sounded like a big inspiration,Crimson Glory's long recording hiatus has meant that they have had the option to choose to playexactly the type of music that they felt like, and therefore "Chasing the Hydra" is also a lot moreheavy and aggressive than for example the last many Queensr'che releases, which have otherwise seenthat band return to a more heavy metal oriented sound. "Chasing the Hydra" is just much lesspolished, epic, and powerful and it's therefore closer to the US power/heavy metal of contemporaryreleases by Metal Church, Vicious Rumors, and Helstar (sans the thrash metal elements of those threeartists) than they are to Queensr'che.Listening to "Chasing the Hydra" it's obvious that the world missed Crimson Glory and that theircomeback is a welcome one. Band's playing this style of music with this much skill, experience, andconviction are hard to come by today, and it's great to know that someone is still holding the flagup high for the US power/heavy metal genre. A 3.5 star (70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._cn_summary: Crimson Glory 来自美国佛罗里达，是一支老牌力量/重金属乐队。这张2026年发行的第五张录音室专辑是他们时隔27年后的回归之作，风格上回归了乐队1986至1988年鼎盛时期的美式力量/重金属路线，带有轻微的前卫金属色彩但并非主导特征。乐队在Queenrÿche等乐派影响下发展出更为粗粝有力的声音，编曲清晰有力，制作精良。新任主唱Travis Wills继承了已故主唱Midnight的衣钵，但并未刻意模仿，而是带来了属于自己的中高音域嗓音。整体而言，这是一张扎实但传统的力量金属作品，在创新性、跨类型融合以及实验性方面均无突出表现，与实验、前卫、爵士、电子、世界音乐等前卫听感取向相距甚远。

items.body: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — One of the greatest concerts of David Gilmour with an enthralling set list to please Pink Floyd fans. There are some incredible lead breaks here and dazzling light displays especially on Run like Hell with a pyrotechnic ending that literally explodes the Pompeii collisseum. On Comfortably Numb we are treated to an eyeball searing laser show that is a feast for the eyes. One of These Days is incredible, with psychedelic strobe lights and Gilmour makes that slide guitar scream and howl, as good as the Pink Floyd days. High Hopes is beautifully performed with a clanging bell and soaring lead solo. There's great sax on Money also, a powerful performance. Gilmours voice is wonderful and he is joined by a brilliant band. The three singers take over on Great Gig in the Sky which is a different variation on Clare Torry. Its also great to hear Gilmours songs as I am not so familiar with these. I particularly like On an Island. Overall this is a great concert worth devouring on DVD and has some fascinating special features.
items._cn_summary: 这是Pink Floyd吉他手David Gilmour 2017年庞贝古剧场演唱会现场专辑，收录了多首Pink Floyd经典曲目如《Comfortably Numb》《Money》《High Hopes》《One of These Days》以及个人作品《On an Island》。整体风格为主流摇滚/前卫摇滚相关的现场演出，吉他演奏是其核心，辅以萨克斯和伴唱。演出以激光、烟火、灯光秀等视觉元素为重要卖点。从音乐本质上来看，这是经典摇滚曲目的标准现场演绎，虽带有前卫摇滚的血统，但并非实验性或创新性作品。与实验/前卫、爵士、电子、世界音乐、暗潮等偏好的距离较大，属于主流商业摇滚范畴。

items.album: DAVID GILMOUR Luck and Strange (Prog Related, 2024)
items.excerpt: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — The peaceful atmospheric music of David Gilmour is mesmerising on his final solo album. He is 80 now so we may suspect there is nothing more to come and this is a fine farewell to his brilliant career. His powerhouse lead guitar work is here along with shimmering keyboards and reflective lyrics. He is joined by Romany sounding angelic on vocals, and Gabrielle who plays a haunting harp on the album. items.body: Review by AtomicCrimsonRush — The peaceful atmospheric music of David Gilmour is mesmerising on his final solo album. He is 80 now so we may suspect there is nothing more to come and this is a fine farewell to his brilliant career. His powerhouse lead guitar work is here along with shimmering keyboards and reflective lyrics. He is joined by Romany sounding angelic on vocals, and Gabrielle who plays a haunting harp on the album. Highlights on this are Luck and Strange, Between two points, Dark and velvet nights and Scattered that are as good as Gilmour can offer. Overall its an album to relax to and put on headphones and just lose yourself in the ambience and beauty of the poetic symphonic waves. It is certainly one of Gilmours best though his prog days have faded as echoes of the past.

items.excerpt: Bluegrass singer-songwriter Aidan Muse has released “Progress,” a new original song inspired by concerns over deforestation and the loss of farmland in his home state
items.body: Bluegrass singer-songwriter Aidan Muse has released “ Progress ,” a new original song inspired by concerns over deforestation and the loss of farmland in his home state of Wisconsin. According to Muse, the track emerged after he witnessed forests cleared and land transferred away from local farmers at what he described as an alarming pace. The song examines the tension between economic development and environmental preservation, with lyrics that challenge the idea of progress when it comes at the expense of natural landscapes and agricultural communities. Throughout the song, Muse questions the long-term impact of large-scale development projects, arguing that promises of future growth often overlook present-day environmental consequences. “Progress” was entirely written, composed, arranged, and produced by Muse. Dave Dalton handled engineering, mixing, and mastering duties. The recording features contributions from Jon Muse on bass, Paul Breitenbach on guitar, Ernest Brusubardis IV on fiddle, Caleb Peters on mandolin, and Aidan Muse on lead vocals and banjo. Buy Progress .
items._cn_summary: Aidan Muse 是一位来自威斯康星州的蓝草音乐创作人，单曲《Progress》以该州森林砍伐与农田流失为创作背景，探讨经济发展与环境保护之间的张力。作品采用传统蓝草编制，班卓琴、小提琴、曼陀林、原声吉他与贝斯构成标准的美式根音音乐框架。Aidan Muse 独立完成词曲、编曲与制作，Dave Dalton 负责录音与混音。整体而言，这是一首以社会议题为导向的民谣作品，音乐风格根植于美国传统蓝草传统，在声响设计与类型融合方面缺乏实验性与跨界尝试，且发布内容以新闻通稿形式呈现，缺乏深度乐评视角。

items.body: A trumpet player who sings or a singer who plays trumpet? Christine Fawson puts those questions to the test (again) on It Could Happen to You, the fifth recording under her leadership, playing trumpet and singing on every one of the album's 11 carefully-mined selections from the Great American Songbook. The obvious answer is that Fawson is both a trumpet player who sings and a singer who plays trumpet, which would be beside the point if she did not do both so marvelously well. Many another instrumentalist has decided to widen his or her repertoire by adding a voice to the mix, more often than not with less than salutary results. The same cannot be said of Fawson, who is so impressive in either guise that she could make a decent living as a singer (which she has) or trumpet player (ditto). And should she ever need a backup plan, she is also an educator who taught for 14 years at the Berklee College of Music. Most of the tunes on It Could Happen to You are well known, as are their authors, who include Cole Porter, Hoagy Carmichael, Irving Berlin, Rodgers, Hart, and the Gershwin brothers. Fawson sings them basically as written, using rhythmic changes and occasional scatting (as well as the trumpet, often muted) for variety. She is aided and abetted by a blue-chip rhythm section: pianist Tim Ray, bassist Dave Zinno and drummer Casey Scheuerell, each of whom is pivotal to the album's overall temper and ambience. Fawson sings the way she plays trumpet: bright as sunlight, always squarely on-key, with an abundance of warmth and personality. Those indispensable traits hold her in good stead throughout, starting with the album's alluring title song, written by Johnny Burke and Jimmy Van Heusen and introduced by Dorothy Lamour in the 1944 film, And the Angels Sing. Fawson gives Porter's "It's All Right with Me" a merry ride, using the proper blend of discretion and come-hither charm, before tackling what may seem an odd choice, Carmichael and Johnny Mercer's easygoing "Lazybones," which works surprisingly well, thanks in part to superb counterpoint by Ray, who then sits in as Fawson's lone accompanist on Berlin's plaintive "What'll I Do." Fawson comes out scatting on Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart's "My Heart Stood Still," then uses the muted trumpet to announce another Burke and Van Heusen classic, "Like Someone in Love," which was introduced by Dinah Shore in 1944 and popularized a year later by Bing Crosby. She sings the seldom-heard verse on Don Raye and Gene DePaul's "You Don't Know What Love Is" before cruising through Ray's surprisingly upbeat arrangement, and wrings the last ounce of earnestness from Carl Fischer and Bill Carey's "You've Changed." A pair of songs by the Gershwin brothers follow, the first a curiously undervalued treasure, "I Was Doing All Right," from the 1938 film The Goldwyn Follies (superb bass solo by Zinno), the second the far better-known "Oh, Lady Be Good" (wherein Fawson, Ray and Scheurell deliver awesome solos). Fawson neatly wraps the package with another of Porter's many masterworks, "Every Time We Say Goodbye." When it comes to singing, playing trumpet, connecting with her teammates and simply having a wonderful time doing all of the above, Fawson is a tough act to follow, and It Could Happen to You is a clear-cut winner from start to finish.

items.body: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina’s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice. The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette. Kerosene Madrigal The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, “Kerosene Madrigal,” is a sort of miner’s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of “Imagined Love” reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy “Don’t Fault the Stars for Falling” could have been a Dolly Parton tune. A Grand Expanse “A Grand Expanse” has a more ambitious arrangement. It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun. The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it. Berceuse Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto’s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026. Where do you find the recordings? Find the artists Martina Sorbara (Dragonette) Don Rooke Jonathan Goldsmith Further reading The Henrys - Shrug (Review) Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review)

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter’s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages – and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: “Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.” Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It’s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he’s selected some great talent to help – guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like “Sam Bamford” and “Mary Fildes,” while the three short pieces that comprise “The Monkey Rides The Mare” capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It’s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets
items._cn_summary: 《Peter's Field》是Sean Cooney以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢大屠杀为背景创作的概念民谣专辑。音乐风格扎根于英格兰传统民谣与兰开夏工业民谣传统，以叙事性歌曲为主轴，邀请Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等民谣音乐人参与，以三重唱和小型器乐编制呈现。专辑以书籍形式发行，辅以历史信件、政治漫画与插图，构成结合历史文献与音乐的多媒体项目。作品聚焦英国工人阶级历史事件，强调歌词的纪实性与人文关怀，旋律以传统民谣为基础，注重情感表达与叙事张力。整体定位为英式历史题材的当代传统民谣创作，以音乐重现社会历史记忆。

items.body: Hollywood Vampires will return to the UK and Europe in 2026, bringing Alice Cooper, Johnny Depp, Joe Perry and Tommy Henriksen back to the stage for a new run of shows. The tour marks the band’s return to European audiences after almost three years away and includes dates in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, Croatia, Austria, Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland. The Polish stop – and also the last stop – will take place at Atlas Arena in Łódź on 10 September 2026. It will be the band’s only concert in Poland on this tour. Hollywood Vampires take their name from the legendary 1970s musicians’ club founded by Alice Cooper, whose circle was connected with the rock’n’roll mythology of the Sunset Strip. The current band transforms that legacy into a live project built around classic rock, theatrical stage presence, guitar-driven energy and tributes to rock history. Their concerts combine original Hollywood Vampires material with interpretations of rock classics. Rather than functioning as a static nostalgia project, the band bring together several layers of rock culture: Cooper’s shock rock theatricality, Perry’s Aerosmith guitar lineage, Depp’s rock sensibility and Henriksen’s experience as a powerful live musician and Cooper collaborator. The UK dates will feature special guests The Jesus And Mary Chain and The Damned on selected shows, while further guests for the European dates are to be announced. Hollywood Vampires UK + Europe Tour 2026 dates: 12 August 2026 – London, UK – The O2 14 August 2026 – Cardiff, UK – Cardiff Castle 15 August 2026 – Scarborough, UK – Scarborough Open Air Theatre 17 August 2026 – Glasgow, UK – OVO Hydro 18 August 2026 – Manchester, UK – AO Arena 19 August 2026 – Birmingham, UK – Utilita Arena Birmingham 21 August 2026 – Colchester, UK – Castle Park 22 August 2026 – Halifax, UK – The Piece Hall 25 August 2026 – Nuremberg, Germany – PSD Bank Nürnberg Arena 26 August 2026 – Paris, France – Adidas Arena 28 August 2026 – Cologne, Germany – Lanxess Arena 30 August 2026 – Hamburg, Germany – Barclays Arena 1 September 2026 – Novegro-Tregarezzo, Italy – Parco della Musica di Milano 2 September 2026 – Este, Italy – Castello Carrarese 3 September 2026 – Pula, Croatia 5 September 2026 – St. Pölten, Austria 6 September 2026 – Prague, Czech Republic 8 September 2026 – Budapest, Hungary 10 September 2026 – Łódź, Poland – Atlas Arena Tickets and VIP packages are available through the official Hollywood Vampires website and authorised ticketing platforms. items.body: When it comes to ragtime jazz, pianist, historian, author, and cultural preservationist Terry Waldo literally wrote the book. Said book is This Is Ragtime (Jazz at Lincoln Center, Inc., 1976), widely regarded as the most thorough and authoritative guide to one of modern jazz's early precursors. Treasury, Volume 3 is the last in a trilogy of recordings by Waldo's Gotham City Band devoted to the best of traditional ragtime music. This is exuberant toe-tapping jazz, radiating happiness and high spirits in every measure, from the impish opening number, "Minnie the Mermaid," to the final measures of Jelly Roll Morton's enticing "Black Bottom Stomp." Even the normally staid "Alice Blue Gown" is gussied up in a radiant new outfit that allows her to sashay rather than stroll. Waldo arranged every number, five of which encompass vocals by Waldo, trombonist Jim Fryer, trumpeter Mike Davis, drummer Jay Lepley, or banjo player Jerron Paxton. The band itself is an octet on five tracks, a septet on the other half-dozen. Besides piano, trombone and rhythm, it includes one (and sometimes two) trumpets—which are actually cornets—as well as clarinet and banjo. Whatever its makeup, the band works extremely well as a unit, and soloists needn't be concerned about any lag in their support. And yes, the various members of the band do improvise, and acquit themselves quite well, keeping in mind that their ad-libs are entrenched in the sort of "Dixieland" parlance that predated bop and even the Swing Era. Morton is represented again by "Kansas City Stomp" and "Frog-i-More Rag"; King Oliver by "Canal Street Blues" and "Mabel's Dream"; and W.C. Handy by "Memphis Blues." Blind Lemon Jefferson's "Take Me Back," Haven Gillespie's "Louisiana Fairy Tale" and Arnett Nelson's "Buddy's Habits" round out the charming program. Waldo's eloquent piano is a constant, as are Fryer's trombone, Brian Nalepka 's steady bass and Lepley's assertive drums. Mike Davis and Colin Hancock share trumpet (cornet) duties, Ricky Alexander and Evan Arntzen are the clarinetists. Paxton (who doubles as vocalist on "Take Me Back"), Nick Russo and Arnt Arntzen the banjoists. Fryer sings on "Minnie the Mermaid" and "Memphis Blues," trumpeter Davis on "Alice Blue Gown," Lepley on "Louisiana Fairy Tale," and each one is a stride or two above the norm. "Tradition is the framework that upholds this wonderful music," Hancock writes in the album's liner notes. "Terry Waldo embodies that tradition, and his music brings it to life." Waldo's Treasury, Volume 3 is a splendid storehouse of music that should never be disparaged or forgotten, and a fun-filled tribute the talented musicians who brought it to life while paving the way for more up-to-date and forward-leaning music yet to come.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张传统拉格泰姆爵士与迪克西兰风格的专辑，由钢琴家Terry Waldo与Gotham City乐队演奏。专辑收录了Jelly Roll Morton、King Oliver、W.C. Handy等早期爵士作曲家经典作品的重新编曲版本，包括《Memphis Blues》《Canal Street Blues》《Black Bottom Stomp》等。乐队编制为铜管、簧乐器、班卓与节奏组的传统爵士八重奏或七重奏，即兴演奏严格遵循迪克西兰语汇，不涉及bop之后的爵士语汇。项目定位明确为传统音乐的文化保存与致敬，不含任何实验性、跨界融合或现代爵士元素。制作精良但风格纯粹古典化。

items.excerpt: Armenian creative hub hosq will host the second edition of Notations this summer, bringing together 65 artists, musicians, performers, media makers, and researchers for a
items.body: Armenian creative hub hosq will host the second edition of Notations this summer, bringing together 65 artists, musicians, performers, media makers, and researchers for a 12-day interdisciplinary laboratory followed by a public festival in Yerevan. Notations Lab 2026 will take place from July 20–31 under the theme “Rituals.” The program will explore ritual as a framework for artistic experimentation, collective engagement, and the development of new creative practices. Participants from a range of disciplines will collaborate through workshops, lectures, performances, and research-based activities. The laboratory will conclude with the Notations Festival , scheduled for August 1–2. The festival will present newly developed works through concerts, installations, performances, and interdisciplinary projects at the Armenian State Philharmonia and the National Gallery of Armenia. Created and curated by hosq, an international cultural platform based in Armenia, Notations aims to strengthen connections between local, regional, and international practitioners while supporting new forms of artistic collaboration. Notations Lab The 2026 curatorial team includes Arman Peshtmaljyan, whose work with the Armenian Navy Band received the BBC Radio 3 Award for World Music 2006; Ben Wheeler, co-founder of the Mountains of Tongues label; producer and multi-instrumentalist Hayk Karoyi; and performance artist Venera Kazarova. According to the 2024 State of Armenia’s Cultural and Creative Ecosystem report by the Armenian General Benevolent Union, Armenia’s creative industries account for 4.4% of national GDP, with the sector nearly doubling in value since 2014. Organizers view Yerevan’s expanding cultural landscape as a key factor behind the project’s international appeal. Applications for Notations Lab 2026 remain open through June 1. Artists and researchers with at least five years of professional experience in music, sound, visual arts, performance, movement, media, somatic practices, or related fields are eligible to apply. No institutional affiliation is required. Hosq will cover participation costs, accommodation, and meals for selected participants. Of the 65 participants, approximately 70% will come from Armenia and neighboring countries, including Georgia, while 30% of places will be reserved for international applicants. The laboratory program will feature collaborative sessions, artist talks, workshops, a field trip, and the return of its daily collective rave, a feature introduced during the inaugural edition in 2025. Last year’s Notations brought together 60 artists and 22 curators from nine countries. Inspired by Avet Terterian’s Symphony No. 3 , the project generated 37 new artistic works, along with a documentary film, a vinyl release, and six digital releases. More than 1,000 visitors attended the concluding festival at the Armenian State Philharmonia. Key Dates Notations Lab 2026: July 20–31, 2026 Notations Festival: August 1–2, 2026 Location: Yerevan, Armenia Applications: Open through June 1, 2026 Information and Applications: hosq Notations Open Call Website: hosq

items.body:
Lebanese vocalist Sandy Chamoun's second solo album is inspired by Sardinian polyphonic folk music the Arab ecstatic forms, modernized by synths from her SANAM and Ghadr collaborator Anthony Sayhoun and percussion from Ali Hout.

If you caught either of those heavy SANAM albums - but especially 2023's 'Aykathani Malakon' - then you'll already be familiar with Chamoun's voice, that carries the Beirut-baed band's hallucinogenic blend of folk, free jazz and acid rock. On her own, however, Chamoun gives her voice even more room to breathe, following loose historical threads to re-interpret concepts that surge through her music. The album's title means "the sound of tears" and it directly addresses the war and genocide in the Levant; Chamoun looks to tarab, an intensely emotional song form that was the first performance style she learned, to guide her through the darkness. And the influence of cantu a tenòre, a four voice polyphonic folk style that's sung in rounds, emerges on the edges. Chamoun had initially planned to journey through Lebanon writing cantu a tenòre-influenced songs that celebrated humanity's victory over nature, but as the situation deepened, the material evolved.

The two forms collide in surprising ways, though. On opening track 'Khafiy خفي', Chamoun's voice is sculpted by AutoTune and placed into an ecstatic clearing, accompanied only by slow-motion drums and scraping resonances. But on the brilliant 'Shahed شاهد', her tarab folk song dissolves mid-way through into the ether, the syncopated percussion turning into 4/4 claps and a circle of voices emerging, met eventually by Sayhoun's microtonally-tuned modular bleeps. It's music that can't help but affect the body entirely: just listen to the lulling 'Ward W Shok ورد و شوك' or the operatic extended outro 'Ataba عتابا' that runs into a moving half-sung voice note.
